audits.published_statement: Eq.(22): Delta <= (3/4) sqrt(3/pi) v_b/alpha^2 [Planck units]. Eq.(23): 'as an example, if we let alpha = 1/10, then Delta <= 10^2 v_b L_Planck ... Thus, unless v_b is extremely large, the wall thickness cannot be much above the Planck scale.' Eq.(28): E = -(1/12) v_b^2 (R^2/Delta + Delta/12). With R = 100 m and eq.(23), eq.(29): 'E <= -6.2x10^70 v_b L_Planck ~ -6.2x10^65 v_b grams'. Eq.(31): 'E <= -3x10^20 M_galaxy v_b ... roughly ten orders of magnitude greater than the total mass of the entire visible universe.' With Delta = 1 m and R = 100 m: 'on the order of a quarter of a solar mass'. Summary: 'a bubble with a radius the size of one electron Compton wavelength would require a negative energy of the order E ~ -400 M_sun.' Abstract: 'bubble wall thickness is on the order of only a few hundred Planck lengths'.
published_hypotheses: H1 free, massless scalar field in 4D Minkowski; the Ford-Roman 1995 QI with Lorentzian sampling, eq.(9), coefficient -3/(32 pi^2 tau0^4); minimal coupling implicit. Massive scalar said to be 'even more restrictive' and the EM field 'larger by a factor of sqrt2' (stated, not derived)

H2 the FLAT-space QI applied directly to the curved Alcubierre metric, justified by Ford-Roman 1996: it holds when the sampling time is <= the smallest local curvature radius. The exact treatment 'would be exceptionally difficult' (p.2)
H3 sampling time t0 = alpha * r_min, where r_min = 2 Delta/(sqrt3 v_b) comes from the largest orthonormal Riemann component (eqs 18-20). 0 < alpha << 1 is UNSPECIFIED; alpha = 1/10 is 'an example'
H4 v_s(t) ~ v_b, constant over the sampling interval
H5 Eulerian geodesic observer sampled at the bubble equator, x(t) ~ f(rho) v_b t (eq.11)
H6 Delta/rho ~ v_b t0/rho << 1 (eq.21)
H7 order of magnitude: the piecewise-linear shape function (eq.4) stands for any shape via the leading Taylor term (eq.13)
H8 semiclassical identification <T_uv u^u u^v> = G_00/8pi (eq.8)
H9 energy figure: constant-velocity bubble, R = 100 m, Delta saturating eq.(23), Eulerian energy integrated over the t=0 slice (eq.25)
H10 Alcubierre metric (eq.1), 4D, G = c = hbar = 1

later_literature.what: Keeps P&F's wall bound (his eq.6) and their eq.(28). A pocket geometry needs only a few solar masses and satisfies the flat-space QI. So the 1e62 kg figure is specific to Alcubierre at R = 100 m; the Planck-scale wall structure is kept as 'generic'.

Proves that for a massless minimally coupled scalar on a timelike geodesic the flat QI holds with small first-order Ricci corrections, and explicitly confirms the Ford-Roman short-sampling claim (cites P&F as ref [7]). Adds caveats: curvature must be small over the whole causal diamond, and there are renormalization ambiguities. Leading correction ~alpha^2.

Cites P&F as the reason Alcubierre is unphysical. Their eq.A.7 reproduces P&F eq.26. The optimal shape f = min(r0/r,1) cuts |E| by ~3x, and flattening cuts it further, giving superluminal solutions that satisfy the P&F-form QI; they say these 'more likely probe the limits of applicability' of the QI, and ANEC is still violated. They contest Van Den Broeck's region-1 energy. They do not dispute the wall bound for the spherical bubble.

later_literature.ref: Pfenning PhD thesis, arXiv gr-qc/9805037 ch.5
later_literature.what: Verbatim text, eq.(5.22). The flat-space justification in sec.3.3 is derived for STATIC spacetimes, and Alcubierre is not static. It repeats the 6.2e70 L_P and -400 M_sun figures, so neither is an arXiv-version artefact.
No null-averaged QI exists in 4D. So there is no null-sampled replacement for P&F's timelike bound (bears on anec.py:60-61).
No state-independent QEI exists for xi > 0, so P&F's conclusion is conditional on H1.

audits.lacked_data: (1) In 1997 there was no proven curved-spacetime QI for a non-static metric; the authors called the exact treatment 'exceptionally difficult' and used the flat QI at short sampling. Fewster & Smith and then Kontou & Olum (1410.0665, READ) later proved the flat form plus small first-order Ricci corrections, of size ~alpha^2 = 0.01 at alpha = 0.1. This is evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result: the one gap the authors named was later closed in their favour, to first order. (2) Cosmological masses have moved, but E/M_gal stays within 2.3-4.4e20 and 'roughly ten orders' stays at 9.7 against baryons: no change. (3) Van Den Broeck 1999 (READ) and Bobrick & Martire 2021 (READ) are later constructions, not data. They narrow the ~1e62 kg energy to the spherical Alcubierre shape at R = 100 m and leave the wall bound untouched. Non-minimal coupling (0708.2450, named) has no state-independent QEI, which narrows H1. (4) The paper's arithmetic, not missing data: two printed figures do not follow from its own formulas (6.2e70 L_P, 1.94x high; -400 M_sun, 514x low). These are recorded discrepancies; the qualitative conclusions stand. Net: no datum the authors lacked moves their conclusion within H1-H10; later work narrows the class it applies to.
audits.grade_evidence: The source's derivation stands as published: every closed-form step (eqs 10, 12, 14-17, 19, 22, 26, 28) re-derives symbolically. The R = 100 m energy reproduces to 11% (6.94e65 g against 6.2e65 g). No moved datum changes a conclusion. The gap the authors named was later confirmed to first order by Kontou-Olum (READ). The grade is NARROWED for three reasons. (i) The tree drops hypotheses the result needs: alpha (certify.py:25, 394; nullbound.py:157-159, 211); the massless minimally coupled scalar, broadened to 'free quantum field' (the tree's own overturn.py:285-289 notes non-minimal coupling has no state-independent QEI); and R = 100 m and v_b on the energy figure. (ii) overturn.py:59-61 and 280-283 attribute more to P&F than they state: 'every known QI' and 'sub-Planckian', where P&F bound the wall at a few hundred Planck lengths. (iii) Later work narrows the energy conclusion to the spherical Alcubierre shape: Van Den Broeck gr-qc/9905084 and Bobrick-Martire 2102.06824, both READ, both keeping the wall bound. Recorded as a discrepancy, not a refutation: the -400 M_sun figure the tree keeps (certify.py:38-40) is 514x below the paper's own formula. Not WRONG: no counterexample to the inequality or the bound is shown here.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restates the bound as Delta <= 0.733 v_b/alpha^2 L_P (10^2 at alpha = 1/10); names the massless minimally coupled scalar or EM field and the Alcubierre geometry at R = 100 m; removes 'sub-Planckian ... Pfenning-Ford's conclusion' and 'every known QI' from the P&F attribution; and drops or corrects -400 M_sun. To WRONG: a computed counterexample, meaning a minimally coupled free scalar state on an Alcubierre wall that satisfies the curved-spacetime QEI (including second-order curvature terms) with Delta much larger than 0.733 v_b/alpha^2 L_P. To DATA-DEPENDENT: none foreseeable, since the only measured inputs are hbar, G and c. To OPEN: none, because the source was READ in full.

verifiers.reason:
I tried to refute the NARROWED grade and could not.

**The source, read in full.** I read gr-qc/9702026v3 pp.1-11 myself through alphaXiv. Every quotation the audit relies on is verbatim in the source:
- eq.(9) coefficient -3/(32 pi^2 tau0^4), 'free, massless scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski'
- p.2 'exceptionally difficult'
- eq.(20) '0 < alpha << 1 ... unspecified parameter'
- eq.(23) 'as an example, if we let alpha = 1/10'
- eq.(28)-(31)
- 'a quarter of a solar mass'
- 'E ~ -400 M_sun'
- abstract 'few hundred Planck lengths' and Summary 'hundreds or thousands of Planck lengths'
- p.11 massive scalar 'more restrictive' and EM 'factor of sqrt2', both asserted without derivation

**Independent re-computation.** My own sympy script (verify/refute/pf_check.py) reproduces the audit's numbers:
- eq.(16) exactly
- eq.(22) as Delta = 3 sqrt3 v/(4 sqrt(pi) alpha^2), coefficient 0.73290
- E(R = 100 m, Delta = 100 L_P) = 3.190e70 L_P = 6.943e62 kg, against the paper's 6.2e70 L_P and 6.2e65 g
- R = lambda_C gives 2.056e5 M_sun, against the paper's 400
- Delta = 1 m gives 0.564 M_sun

The three discrepancies are therefore real. The audit records them correctly as discrepancies in the paper's arithmetic, not refutations. The -400 M_sun figure is off by 514x from the paper's own eq.(28), and I found no reading of Delta or v_b in the paper that recovers it.

**The tree drift, checked at the cited lines.** Every citation holds:
- certify.py:24 and 394 print 'Delta <= 10^2 v_b L_Planck' with no alpha.
- nullbound.py:157-159 and 211 pin 100 L_P.
- certify.py:38-40 keeps -400 M_sun as 'ONE NUMBER OF THEIRS IS WORTH KEEPING'.
- overturn.py:59-61 says 'every bound any known quantum inequality permits'.
- overturn.py:280-283 says 'Sub-Planckian, which is Pfenning-Ford's conclusion'. The phrase 'in this architecture's coordinates' hedges this slightly, but P&F conclude an upper bound of ~10^2 v_b L_P, not a sub-Planckian wall.
- overturn.py:285-289 records Fewster-Osterbrink.

**Why not STANDS.** The grade judges the result as the tree uses it. The tree drops alpha, broadens the massless minimally coupled scalar to 'free quantum field', drops R and v_b from the energy figure, and attributes 'every known QI' and 'sub-Planckian' to P&F. On top of that, later literature narrows the energy conclusion: Van Den Broeck 1999 and Bobrick & Martire 2021, both READ by the auditor.

**Why not WRONG.** No counterexample to the QI or to eq.(22) exists here. The 514x error in -400 M_sun is a printed figure that does not follow from the paper's own formula. It is not a failure of the derivation, and M's rule makes it a discrepancy.

**Two nuances the audit slightly over-represents, in P&F's favour.** Neither moves the grade; if anything both support NARROWED over STANDS.
1. Kontou-Olum 1410.0665 proves the first-order curved-space QI for smooth sampling functions confined to a small causal diamond, not for the Lorentzian tails of eq.(9). 'The one gap the authors named was later closed in their favour' is therefore closed only in form, to first order, not for the exact inequality P&F used.
2. The bound puts the curvature radius at ~10^2 L_P. At that scale the semiclassical identification <T> = G/8pi (H8) is itself near the edge of its validity, and neither the paper nor the audit names this self-consistency limit.

**One minor point.** Calling Delta = 1 m -> 0.56 M_sun against 'on the order of a quarter' a discrepancy is strict, since it agrees in order of magnitude. It is recorded, not graded, so it does not affect the grade.

verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN: I copied the audit script to verify/rederive/gr-qc_9702026.py and ran it. It exits 0 and reproduces every number the audit quotes: eq(22) coefficient 0.732904, which gives 73.3 v_b L_P at alpha = 1/10; E(R = 100 m) = 6.943e62 kg, i.e. 3.19e70 L_P against the printed 6.2e70 (x1.94); lambda_C gives 2.06e5 M_sun against '-400 M_sun' (x514); Delta = 1 m gives 0.56 M_sun against 'a quarter'; Van Den Broeck eq(9) is matched within 5%. I re-read the source pp.1-11 through alphaXiv. Eqs (8), (9), (10), (14)-(23), (25)-(29), the '-400 M_sun' Summary sentence and the 'quarter of a solar mass' sentence are all as the audit quotes them. The Summary names no wall thickness other than eq(23), so the three arithmetic discrepancies are real: each is recorded, none is a refutation.

WHAT THE SCRIPT CHECKS, THEOREM OR TOY: it checks the paper's algebra, given eq(8) (energy density), eq(9) (the Ford-Roman QI) and eq(18) (Riemann component) as inputs. It does not derive eq(8) or eq(18); it hard-codes them. So I derived both from the metric, in metric_check.py (sympy, general F(r_s), orthonormal Eulerian tetrad, orthonormality asserted):
- G_nn/8pi = -v^2 F'^2/(32 pi) at the equator, and it matches -(1/32pi) v^2 rho^2/r_s^2 F'^2 at an off-equator point. So eq(8) is CONFIRMED.
- R_0202 = -3v^2 F'^2/4. So eq(18) is CONFIRMED.
- For the piecewise-linear F (F'' = 0 inside the wall), R_tyty is indeed the largest component; the others are v^2/(4 Delta^2) and v/(2 rho Delta).
Eq(9) is an external theorem that no finite check here can test. That leaves it READ, and Kontou-Olum is corroboration, as the audit says.

VACUITY GUARD: the checks are not vacuous. Each mutant failed at least one check with exit 1: QI coefficient 3 -> 1; QI sign flipped; Riemann 3/4 -> 1/4; a v-linear Riemann term; alpha = 1/30 in place of 1/10; the wrong angular integrand; 1/12 -> 1/6 in the energy. The H6-negated mutant (keeping the (1-f) term) crashed in sympy's positivity filter rather than passing, so I did it by hand instead. The exact bound is 0.7329 v_b/alpha^2 * sqrt(1+eps), with eps = 2 alpha Delta(1-f)/(sqrt3 rho) ~ 1.9e-36 at R = 100 m. H6 is harmless. One caution on the script: the eq(10) and eq(14) checks are identities of rewriting (coefficient ratios). They confirm the rearrangement, not the physics.

NEW, COMPUTED, A FURTHER NARROWING OF H7 (not a refutation): the full frame Riemann tensor carries R_0212 = v F''/2, and P&F's Taylor step (eq 13) drops F''. For any smooth shape this term sets r_min at subluminal speed. For the tanh shape, Delta^2 |R| at the maximum is 0.077 for R0212 against 0.007 for R0202 at v = 0.1, and 0.770 against 0.750 at v = 1; R0202 dominates only for v >~ 1. With an F''-dominated r_min the bound becomes Delta <= sqrt3 k/(sqrt(pi) alpha^2), where k = |F''|max Delta^2/2 (about 0.77 for tanh). That is about 0.75/alpha^2 and does not depend on v_b. So the 'v_b' scaling in eq(22) is exact only for the piecewise-linear shape. For smooth shapes it holds to O(1) at v_b >~ 1, the superluminal regime the tree uses, and for v_b << 1 the true bound is weaker by about 1/v_b. The Summary's 'even at subluminal speeds' rests on the energy, not the wall bound, so it is not overturned.

The audit's derivation claims and discrepancies all survive re-running. Its NARROWED grade is supported: the tree dropped alpha, broadened the field class, over-attributed 'sub-Planckian' and 'every known QI', and kept the -400 M_sun figure, and later work narrows the energy result to the spherical shape. My H7 result narrows it slightly further, but nothing supports WRONG or STANDS.

audits.published_statement: THEOREM 1 (p.6): 'Let (M,g_ab) be a null geodesically complete spacetime satisfying the null energy condition (2) and the null generic condition (see eq.(9)). Then given any compact region K in M, there exists another compact region K' containing K such that if q,p not in K' and q in J+(p) - I+(p), then any causal curve gamma connecting p to q cannot intersect the region K.' The authors' own gloss (pp.5, 10): 'the theorem suggests that "time advance" is not possible, although it is difficult to make a strong argument for this interpretation, since the theorem gives little control over the size of the region K''. THEOREM 2 (pp.12-13): given a timelike conformal boundary, NEC + null generic, a strongly causal closure and compact causal diamonds, any causal curve from p to a point on the boundary of A(p) lies entirely in the boundary. The paper reads this (p.14) as light through an asymptotically AdS spacetime 'always being "delayed" relative to propagation through anti-de Sitter spacetime itself', and the comparison is well defined only because the boundary geometry is held fixed. EQ.(13) (p.7): with A from eq.(11) and G = sqrt(det A) (eq.12), 'G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b]'. INTRODUCTION (pp.2-4): the Visser-Bassett-Liberati result h_ab k^a k^b >= 0 'is highly gauge dependent'. Eqs.(6)-(8) give a pure gauge that 'opens out the light cones everywhere', so 'we can reverse the conclusions of [3] in any compact region'. The paper also says 'there is no natural way to choose a flat background for a curved spacetime'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (Thm 1, Thm 2, Lemma 1) null energy condition R_ab k^a k^b >= 0 for all null k (eq.2), stated on Ricci, not on T_ab; Thm 2 footnote 3 says Borde's averaged condition can replace it
H2 (Thm 1, Thm 2) null generic condition: every null geodesic contains a point with k_[a R_b]cd[e k_f] k^c k^d != 0 (eq.9)
H3 (Thm 1) null geodesic completeness; footnote 1 (Galloway): H1+H2+H3 can be replaced by 'M contains no null line'

H4 (Thm 1) the conclusion holds only for p,q outside a compact K' that the theorem does not bound; it is an asymptotic statement about fastest null geodesics and makes no comparison with any reference geometry

H5 (Thm 2) conformal embedding with a timelike boundary (asymptotically AdS prototype), strong causality of the closure, compact J+(p)∩J-(q); the delay is measured against boundary null geodesics with the boundary geometry fixed
H6 (all) connected, smooth, time-oriented, paracompact, any dimension; no staticity, symmetry or asymptotic flatness assumed
H7 (eq.13) a twist-free null congruence from a point with affine parameter; the Raychaudhuri equation is quoted from ref [10] (hep-th/9908070), not derived
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H2 and H3 (and Galloway's no-null-line replacement). driven.py:116-118 states Theorem 1 as 'the NEC makes Shapiro always a delay, never an advance', and foliation.py:237-239 says 'with the NEC, never an advance'. The theorem needs NEC, null generic and null geodesic completeness together. Machine-checked (rederive F1): on the radial null rays that foliation.py:305-313 times (10M->100M), the null generic quantity is exactly 0 at r = 3, 10, 50 and 100 M, because radial is a principal null direction of Schwarzschild. Schwarzschild is also null-incomplete. So the example the tree attaches the theorem to lies outside its hypotheses.

ADDED a comparison with a reference geometry. foliation.py:235-239 (D4 'arrives EARLIER than in the reference geometry ... REPLACED BY A STRONGER ONE ... Gao & Wald') and foliation.py:613-614 do this. Theorem 1 makes no such comparison, and the paper's stated aim (p.4) is theorems that 'do not require a comparison with Minkowski spacetime'. Its only reference comparison is Theorem 2, which needs a fixed timelike conformal boundary (asymptotically AdS), not an asymptotically flat corridor.

INVERTED the paper's position on the companion citation. foliation.py:314-317 says 'Gao & Wald and Visser-Bassett-Liberati say the sign of that excess is forced by the NEC', and driven.py:116-118 groups the two. Gao-Wald argue that the VBL result is gauge dependent and can be reversed in any compact region (eqs.6-8, machine-checked as rederive E1/E2). They say nothing that forces the sign of the Schwarzschild Killing-time excess, and they cite Penrose's theorem that Schwarzschild cannot be identified with Minkowski with its cones inside Minkowski's.

WEAKENED the authors' own caveat. The tree calls Theorem 1 'standing' (driven.py:116) and 'stronger' than D4 (foliation.py:237, 614), but the authors write 'it is difficult to make a strong argument for this interpretation' (pp.5, 10).
HELD: 'no staticity' (driven.py:116-117, foliation.py:316-317) is correct (H6).

HELD for eq.(13) as used: composite.py:18-20 quotes it verbatim with the right equation number, and composite.py:36-40 evolves a 2x2 screen in 4D, which is exactly where eq.(13) is an identity (rederive A2, C1).

OWNER READING, NOT GAO-WALD: composite.py:24-29 ('Weyl focusing ... sign-blind ... exactly as hard') is not in the paper. In the straight-ray Born approximation T(-M) is T(M) with the transverse axes swapped, so the conjugate points coincide exactly (55.8658 for both signs; rederive C2). composite.py's own docstring records 55.16 against 56.52, 2.47% apart, so 'exactly as hard' (composite.py:28) holds only to first order in M. The selftest's 0.05 tolerance (composite.py:359-360) already allows for this.

SOURCE DISCREPANCY, not drift: read literally (A the full n x n matrix, 'any dimension'), eq.(13) is not an identity. det A = lambda^2 det A_perp (B2), and in flat space G''=2>0 while the right-hand side is 0 (B1). The coefficient 1/2 holds only for n=4 (A3). The correct object is G=(det A_perp)^(1/(n-2)) with coefficient 1/(n-2) (A1). Lemma 1's proof survives with that object. This is recorded as a notational discrepancy, not an error in the result.

later_literature.what: Remark (ii): positive mass does not imply non-negative time delay. A non-negative bulk-versus-boundary delay follows from null genericity, null geodesic completeness and the NEC via the focusing theorem, so those are exactly the load-bearing hypotheses the tree drops. The negative-mass AdS soliton still has a strictly positive delay, so the sign of the mass does not fix the sign of the delay.

Rigidity: under the NEC in 4D, or staticity, or stationarity, an asymptotically AdS spacetime with zero boundary-to-boundary delay is AdS; Prop. 5.4 gives the asymptotically flat analogue. Remark 5.3(2): spacetimes that approach negative-mass Schwarzschild violate energy conditions and fail the null boundary Penrose property, so composite.py's negative-mass regime lies outside this whole family of theorems.

audits.lacked_data: The theorems take no empirical input, so no datum the authors lacked can move them. Cassini's roughly 50x improvement over Viking (Will, arXiv:1403.7377, READ) confirms GR's solar delay but is not an input. What came later was mathematics, and it strengthened or extended the result: Galloway's no-null-line version (footnote 1), Page-Surya-Woolgar 2002, which confirms that generic + completeness + NEC is the route to a non-negative delay, and Paternain-Woolgar 2026 on rigidity. The gap sits on the tree's side. It cites Theorem 1 for 'the NEC alone gives no advance against a reference geometry, Schwarzschild radial transit included', which the paper does not claim. The paper itself shows the main obstacle to that claim: there is no invariant reference identification, and the VBL result can be reversed by a gauge choice. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: every step that can be checked here re-derives (eq.7, eq.8, eq.13 in 4D). The one discrepancy (the literal n x n reading of eqs.11-13, and the 1/2 in 'any dimension') is notational and leaves the proof valid.
audits.grade_evidence: The source stands as published. It was read in full; eqs.7-8 and eq.13 in 4D were machine-checked; no counterexample was found; the one discrepancy is notational. The tree's use is narrowed. (a) driven.py:116-118 and foliation.py:237-239, 314-317 and 613-614 drop the null generic condition and null geodesic completeness, and add a reference-geometry comparison the theorem does not make. Their Schwarzschild radial example (foliation.py:305-317) fails the null generic hypothesis at every sampled point (F1) and is null-incomplete. The paper also argues against the VBL flat-comparison reading that the tree pairs it with (eqs.6-8, E1/E2). (b) composite.py's use of eq.(13) is inside the valid domain (4D, 2x2 screen; A2, C1) and stands. Its 'sign-blind' claim is the owner's first-order reading, confirmed at O(M) (C2), and is not a claim of Gao-Wald. Neither (a) nor (b) refutes the paper. But the tree's 'standing ... never an advance' cannot be attributed to gr-qc/0007021 as written.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS for the foliation/driven use would need the citation restated with Theorem 1's real hypotheses (NEC + null generic + null geodesic completeness, or no null line) and its real conclusion (fastest null geodesics between far events avoid any compact set). It would also need 'Shapiro always a delay' and the reference comparison dropped, or else Theorem 2 cited only for asymptotically AdS spacetimes with fixed boundary geometry. The sign of the Schwarzschild excess would need a different source. WRONG would need a spacetime satisfying H1-H3 in which a fastest null geodesic between arbitrarily far p,q enters a fixed compact K; none is known, and the proof re-checks. OPEN does not apply, since the paper was read in full.

verifiers.reason:
I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and re-ran it. It reproduces its output exactly: '12/12 checks true'. The substance of the audit survives, but the count overstates what was checked.

(1) Two of the 12 are not checks. A3 and C3 are hard-coded rec(...,True,...) printouts, so the script makes 10 real assertions, not 12.

(2) C1 is a tautology. Its residual is (th/2)^2 + (-Rkk - trB^2)/2 + (S2 + Rkk)/2. Rkk cancels, so all it tests is the 2x2 matrix identity tr B^2 = sigma^2 + theta^2/2 for a symmetric B. It never touches the ODE or the Weyl field. My V1 gives a residual of 2e-13 for 1000 random B with random Rkk and no evolution at all. So C1 does not test eq.(13) against anything.

I replaced it with a genuine check (V2). It evolves A'' = -TA with a random Weyl part plus a Ricci part of either sign, takes G = sqrt(det A) numerically, and gets G'' by finite difference.
- On a 2x2 screen (n=4), eq.(13) holds to 8e-8 for both signs of Rkk.
- On 3x3 and 4x4 screens (n=5, 6) it fails, with residuals of 18.5 and 49.5. A3's formula (n-4)(n-2)D'^2/(4D^2) predicts 18.75 and 50 at lambda=0.2.
- So the audit's claims A1-A3 (1/2 holds only for n=4; the correct object is (det A_perp)^(1/(n-2))) are now independently confirmed, not just asserted.

(3) The source discrepancy is confirmed at source (alphaXiv page text). Eq.(11) defines A^mu_nu with sums over all Greek indices, and G = sqrt(det A). Page 6 says 'our results hold in any spacetime dimension'. So B1/B2 (the literal n x n reading gives det A = lambda^2 det A_perp and G''=2 in flat space) are a fair literal reading. B2's block-triangular structure (T k = 0, k_a T^a_b = 0) is physically correct.

One small point the audit did not record: Lemma 1(iii) says 'G''<0 by eq.(13)', but the NEC gives only G''<=0. That suffices given G'(lambda1)<0. It is a misprint-level discrepancy and moves nothing.

(4) Vacuity and encoding of the rest:
- E1 discriminates: changing the coefficient from 2 to 3 makes sympy report unequal (V4).
- E2 checks only one admissible g, but the paper's claim holds for every admissible g by a two-line argument (V3b). For r<=1, r g' < 2r <= 2 <= 2+g; for r>=1, g=r.
- E2's hypothesis bites: with g=r^2 everywhere (g'<2 violated), the radial h(k,k) goes positive, to +0.125 (V3).
- F1 discriminates: 0 on radial rays, 0.43-0.74 on tangential ones. That matches radial being a principal null direction of Schwarzschild (Petrov type D), so the radial rays foliation.py times fail the null generic condition.
- D1's closed form is right.
- C2 is exact: in vacuum T = diag(a,-a), so -T is T with the axes swapped.

(5) The tree's citations check out at the stated lines: driven.py:116-118, foliation.py:235-239, 309-317 and 613-614, and composite.py:18-29, 52-53 and 357-360.

The text quoted in the reverify command sits at those lines, and the 'hypothesis_drift' readings hold against the source text I read myself: Theorem 1 needs NEC + null generic + completeness, makes no reference comparison, and the authors' caveat is on pp.5 and 10. Against the VBL result, eqs.(6)-(8) say it can be reversed in any compact region.

Nothing I found moves the grade. The paper STANDS as published, with a notational discrepancy. The tree's use is NARROWED, because it drops the null generic and completeness hypotheses and adds a reference-geometry comparison the theorem does not make. The corrections are to the audit's evidence count: 10 real checks, not 12; C1 is a tautology, replaced by V2; E2 is a sample, backed by the analytic V3b. The outcome is unchanged.

audits.name: ANEC over a complete null geodesic holds (Klinkhammer 1991; Wald & Yurtsever 1991); saturated by the vacuum

source.located: Klinkhammer, PRD 43, 2542 (1991) and Wald & Yurtsever, PRD 44, 403 (1991): neither is on arXiv. Both were read through exact restatements: Fewster-Roman gr-qc/0209036v2 Sec. II.D p.9 and endnote [41]; Fewster-Olum-Pfenning gr-qc/0609007v3 Sec. I pp.2-3; Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815v2 Sec. 4.3 pp.35-36 and eq. (85) p.29; Visser gr-qc/9409043 p.1 and p.3 (which quotes W-Y's note added in proof, p.415); Graham-Olum 0705.3193 p.2.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries returned full page text for gr-qc/0209036 (pp.1-14), gr-qc/0609007 (pp.1-12), 0705.3193 (pp.1-8), gr-qc/9409043 (pp.1-6) and 0910.5925 (pp.1-11), selected pages of 1610.05308, and pp.1,5,29-30,33-37,52,58 of 2003.01815. The two 1991 papers themselves: NAMED-NOT-READ.

audits.published_statement: As restated, since the 1991 papers are not on arXiv. Fewster-Roman gr-qc/0209036 p.9, eq. (II.35): the ANEC, int dlambda <:T_ab:l^a l^b>_omega(gamma(lambda)) >= 0, was "established by Klinkhammer [21] at least for a dense set of states in the Fock space of the Minkowski vacuum, and by Wald and Yurtsever [22] for a large subclass of Hadamard states". Fewster-Olum-Pfenning gr-qc/0609007 p.2: "In n-dimensional Minkowski space, the ANEC was proved for the scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling for a dense set of states in the Fock space of the Minkowski vacuum [Klinkhammer]; namely, all finite linear combinations of finite particle-number states of bounded momentum ... [Wald-Yurtsever] establishes the ANEC in four-dimensional Minkowski space for a restricted class of Hadamard states of the minimally coupled scalar field ... In general globally hyperbolic two-dimensional spacetimes, [W-Y] established the ANEC on complete achronal null geodesics for the minimally coupled free scalar field. This holds for arbitrary Hadamard states in the massless case, and a restricted class of Hadamard states for nonzero mass." Kontou-Sanders p.36: "In four dimensions, Wald and Yurtsever argued that the ANEC cannot hold for all states of a massless field in all spacetimes." Visser gr-qc/9409043 p.1: "it is now realised that in general the ANEC must fail. See the 'note added in proof' on page 415 of [W-Y]". W-Y's form of the condition (Kontou-Sanders eq. 85) is a lim inf over widening C^1_0 test-function windows. The titles are "General proof of the averaged null energy condition for a massless scalar field in two-dimensional curved space-time" (W-Y) and "Averaged energy conditions for free scalar fields in flat space-times" (Klinkhammer). Fewster-Roman pp.9-10 show that their own states obey ANEC: phi -> 0 (II.37) and psi -> 2 pi f(0) int u^2 C(u,u) du >= 0 (II.38).
published_hypotheses: H1 FIELD: a free scalar field. Klinkhammer: massless or massive, any curvature coupling xi. W-Y: minimally coupled in 4D Minkowski, massless in the 2D curved general proof. The electromagnetic field came later (Folacci 1992).

H2 BACKGROUND: Klinkhammer: n-dimensional Minkowski space. W-Y: 4D Minkowski (restricted class of states) and globally hyperbolic 2D curved spacetime (general proof). Neither proves a 4D curved result, and W-Y's note added in proof says ANEC fails for generic perturbations of Minkowski in 4D.

H3 STATES: Klinkhammer: a dense set in the Minkowski-vacuum Fock space, namely finite combinations of finite-particle states of bounded momentum. W-Y: a large or restricted subclass of Hadamard states in 4D Minkowski; all Hadamard states for the massless field in 2D.

H4 GEODESIC: a complete, affinely parametrised null geodesic. It must be achronal in the 2D curved theorem; in Minkowski every null geodesic is achronal. Klinkhammer gives negative results along non-geodesic curves and along chronal geodesics in compactified flat space.

H5 FORMULATION: either a lim inf over widening test-function windows (W-Y) or an absolutely convergent integral, with <T_ab> normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum, so the vacuum gives 0 by construction.
H6 TEST FIELD: no back-reaction; the semiclassical Einstein equation is not imposed.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED, BACKGROUND (bounds.py:147-149, :96): the claim line names no background. The canonical entry lists 'flat background implied', and bounds.py:136-141 is about 4D Minkowski, so the implication can be read from context. The sources prove the result on Minkowski, on 2D curved spacetime, and (later) on flat tubes. It fails on complete achronal geodesics in 4D curved spacetime: Urban-Olum 0910.5925, re-derived here, and Visser gr-qc/9409043.

WIDENED BY GLOSS (bounds.py:90, :406): ANEC is counted among 'statements about quantum field theory on a fixed background'. That is wider than what was proved: on a generic fixed 4D curved background ANEC fails for test fields (Visser; Urban-Olum; Visser gr-qc/9604008 on chronal geodesics; winding geodesics in the FOP cylinder spacetime).

DROPPED, FIELD CONTENT (bounds.py:147-149): the cited results are free-scalar theorems. Later work covers interacting QFT in Minkowski (Faulkner et al. 1605.08072; Hartman et al. 1610.05308), but the tree cites Klinkhammer and W-Y, not that work.
DROPPED, STATE CLASS (bounds.py:147-149): the tree names no class of states (dense Fock states for Klinkhammer; a restricted Hadamard class for W-Y in 4D).

DROPPED, ACHRONALITY: harmless in Minkowski, where it holds automatically. It matters in any curved or compactified use, where winding (chronal) geodesics violate ANEC (FOP Sec. IV; Graham-Olum Sec. II).

ATTRIBUTION INCOMPLETE (bounds.py:148): W-Y is cited as a co-proof of 4D ANEC. Their general proof is 2D curved, their 4D result covers Minkowski for a restricted class of states, and their note added in proof (p.415, as quoted by Visser gr-qc/9409043 p.1) says ANEC fails for generic perturbations of Minkowski in 4D.

SATURATION (bounds.py:96, K=0 at :44/:296): the vacuum gives exactly 0 in Minkowski by construction. It does not in curved space: the conformal vacuum of a conformally flat 4D spacetime gives a negative ANEC integral (Urban-Olum eq. 42, re-derived here). K=0 is sound only under the Minkowski hypothesis.

Z-SLOT GLOSS (bounds.py:30, :194): Z=1 reads 'timelike or null -- a QEI exists' and seats ANEC there. Along null lines in 4D no QEI exists (Fewster-Roman). The tree already records this as a candidate index fault at bounds.py:147-155; it is noted here, not re-judged.

rederivation.outcome: All four checks agree with the sources (exit 0). A (sympy): in flat space, for any coupling xi, k k T = (k.dphi)^2 - xi (k.d)^2 phi^2. The xi term is a total derivative along the null line, so ANEC does not depend on xi, as FOP state. B (numeric model, 3 modes in a truncated Fock space, not a proof): the vacuum gives exactly 0 at every window length L. The lowest eigenvalue of the windowed null energy is -0.32 at L=0.5, -4.4e-7 at L=4 and 0 at L=32: negative on a finite window, going to 0 as the window covers the whole line. C (sympy): Fewster-Roman's explicit states give ANEC(alpha) = 4 L0^3 f0 alpha^(2 sigma-7)/(315 pi (alpha^(2 sigma-6) + 128 pi^4)), which is positive and falls toward 0 (1.45e-7 at alpha=0.2, 2.29e-8 at alpha=0.005, sigma=3.75) while their segment average diverges to minus infinity. D (sympy): Urban-Olum eqs. (39)-(42) re-derived from (37)-(38). The ANEC integral is (ab - 2a^2) 16 beta sqrt(2 pi)/r^3, which is negative for b > 2a (-2.12e-7 at a=0.01, b=0.05, r=1), in the vacuum, on a complete achronal geodesic of a conformally flat 4D spacetime.

later_literature.what: Along null geodesics in 4D Minkowski there is no quantum inequality, yet their own states obey ANEC. A quantum inequality does hold along timelike worldlines in any globally hyperbolic spacetime.

Proves ANEC for a complete geodesic inside a flat tube whose causal structure is its own (which forces achronality). This covers Casimir plates at a finite distance; winding geodesics in the cylinder spacetime still violate.

In 4D, a non-zero scale anomaly lets a choice of renormalisation scale violate ANEC, which makes violation generic. Minkowski, conformally flat, Einstein and all 2D spacetimes escape this argument. Quotes W-Y's note added in proof.
States that ANEC is violated in curved spacetime and proposes self-consistent achronal ANEC as the weaker condition.

Contradicts only an unrestricted-background reading, not the 1991 theorems: ANEC and achronal ANEC are both violated in a conformally flat 4D spacetime, by excited states and by the vacuum (eq. 42, re-derived here). Test field only.

later_literature.ref: Hartman, Kundu & Tajdini 1610.05308; Faulkner, Leigh, Parrikar & Wang 1605.08072
later_literature.what: ANEC in Minkowski space for interacting QFT in d > 2. Hartman et al. note that the earlier derivations were restricted to free or superrenormalizable theories, or to two dimensions.
Review that restates the scope of both 1991 results and notes that achronal ANEC has no known physically reasonable counterexample.
Derives achronal ANEC from the generalized second law under semiclassical gravity.

audits.lacked_data: No measured datum enters the 1991 theorems, and the right-hand side of the bound is exactly zero, so no later measurement can move the flat-space result. That is evidence against M's hypothesis for this result. What the authors lacked was later calculation, not data. First, the 4D curved-space violations: Visser 1995 (scale anomaly), Visser 1996 (Boulware vacuum, chronal geodesics) and Urban-Olum 2010 (re-derived here). Second, the interacting-QFT proofs in Minkowski (2016-17). The violations do not refute the authors: W-Y's own note added in proof says ANEC fails generically in 4D curved spacetime, and Klinkhammer's title restricts his result to flat spacetime. The interacting proofs extend the result. So the later work changes how far the tree's unqualified wording can be taken, not what the authors concluded. Still open: whether achronal ANEC holds for self-consistent semiclassical solutions.
audits.grade_evidence: In Minkowski space, under the stated field and state classes, ANEC >= 0 holds and the vacuum gives exactly 0. The checks agree (A-C), including Fewster-Roman's printed consistency check. The tree's use is wider than that. bounds.py:147-149 names no background, field or class of states, and bounds.py:90 and :406 count ANEC among statements about QFT on 'a fixed background'. On a curved 4D background ANEC fails even on complete achronal geodesics: Urban-Olum eq. (42), re-derived here, gives a negative vacuum value, and Visser's scale-anomaly argument makes failure generic. So the result holds on a smaller class than the tree's wording covers, and K=0 ('saturated by the vacuum') is sound only in Minkowski. The grade is not WRONG: nothing refutes the published theorem, and within the 'flat background implied' hypothesis the tree's claim stands. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no measured datum enters.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: bounds.py states the hypotheses where it uses the result (Minkowski or a flat achronal tube; which fields; which states), limits the 'fixed background' gloss accordingly, and reads K=0 as 'saturated by the Minkowski vacuum'. To WRONG, for the tree's application rather than the theorem: a consumer applies ANEC >= 0 or vacuum saturation to a curved 4D warp geometry. To OPEN: a direct reading of PRD 43 2542 and PRD 44 403 that differs from the four restatements, which agree with each other.

The audit stands. My copy of the script (verify/rederive/anec-klinkhammer-wald-yurtsever.py) exits 0 and reproduces every printed number: B's minimum eigenvalue is -0.3198 at L=0.5, -4.42e-7 at L=4 and 0 at L=32; C gives 1.4498e-7 and 2.2923e-8; D gives -2.1165e-7.

Encoding, check by check:

(A) An exact sympy identity for the null contraction of the xi-coupled flat-space stress tensor. The vacuity guard works: with a timelike k=(1,0,0,0) or k=(2,0,0,1) the identity fails, so the check really depends on k being null. One hypothesis is left unstated: "the xi term integrates to a boundary term" needs d<phi^2>/dlambda to vanish at both ends of the line. That is a named gap, not a fault.

(B) A toy, correctly labelled "not a proof". Vacuum saturation there is true by construction, because the operator is normal-ordered. The limit going to 0 is forced by having discrete modes with u = l.k >= 0. The vacuity guard is informative. Put in sign-indefinite frequencies, as a spacelike line gives (u = k_x), and the minimum eigenvalue stays negative at L=32: -1.43, and -15.9 for a tuned pair u2 = -u1. So B does test the one ingredient it models, that l.k >= 0 kills the delta(u+u') term. B also passes on a timelike line, which is consistent with AWEC. It cannot represent curvature or chronality, so it is no evidence about the background hypothesis, and the audit does not use it that way.

(C) A faithful encoding of Fewster-Roman's printed consistency check. I checked it against the source: eq. II.24 with nu=1, B from II.26, C = 1/(24 pi^2 Lambda0^4) from II.27, N from II.28, and psi from II.38 with the min{v,v'} double integral. sigma = 3.75 lies inside FR's window (3.5, 4), and the exponents 2sigma-7 and sigma-4 are FR's. The sign cannot fail, because C >= 0 by FR's construction. What C actually verifies is the dependence on alpha. Two cosmetic points. The printed ANEC(alpha) keeps a factor f0 that FR's II.36 divides out (harmless, since f0=1 in the numerics). And "segment average diverges to minus infinity" is checked only through the sign of its exponent.

(D) I re-derived this independently, from the source rather than from the audit's eq. (38) (anec_D_independent.py). I built the curvature of g = e^{2 omega} eta from scratch with MTW conventions and applied eqs. (28), (31) and (32), with gamma = -2 beta. I kept the R_{;ab} term with its Christoffel symbols and the affine factor Omega^{-2}. To O(epsilon^2) the ANEC integral is exactly (ab - 2a^2) 16 beta sqrt(2 pi)/r^3, which is eq. (42). The R_{;vv} piece integrates to 0 only when the affine factor is kept. Without it the piece gives 12 sqrt(2 pi) a(b-2a)/r^3, so Urban-Olum's step of dropping R_{;ab} is right, but it depends on affine parametrisation. Vacuity: flat space (a=b=0) gives 0, and so does b=2a.

The checks were never meant to verify the 1991 theorems themselves. A continuum-QFT proof is not a finite check, and the theorems are READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT (Klinkhammer and W-Y NAMED-NOT-READ), as the audit says. The grade rests on two things: the hypothesis drift at bounds.py:90, :96, :147-149 and :406, which I confirmed by grep, and the curved-background vacuum counterexample D, which I have now confirmed by a second, independent route. Nothing found moves the grade to STANDS, WRONG or OPEN. NARROWED stands.

verifiers.reason:
Row 1, no measured inputs, STANDS. The right-hand side of the bound is exactly zero: Urban-Olum 0910.5925 eq. (1) and p.2, and Fewster-Roman eq. II.35. The only constants anywhere in this chain are computed ones, so no datum could move the flat-space theorem. moves_conclusion='no' follows.

Row 2, the anomaly coefficient. The value is correct, but part of the source citation is wrong. Visser gr-qc/9409043 eqs. (6) and (10), read in full, define 'a' only as a symbol: the C^2 coefficient in the trace anomaly, which Visser says is the same coefficient as in the scale anomaly. Visser prints no number. The number 1/(2880 pi^2) is READ at Urban-Olum p.3 ("a tiny number such as 1/(2880 pi^2)"). beta = -1/(5760 pi^2) is READ at UO eq. (29). Page 1982 and Birrell-Davies 1982 are the sources that Visser (refs 11, 13) and UO (refs 15, 19) cite, so value_then 'known (Page 1982; Birrell-Davies 1982)' holds as cited. That Visser's a equals 1/(2880 pi^2) is COMPUTED here, not read: (c - a_E)/16pi^2 = 1/(2880 pi^2) and a_E/16pi^2 = 1/(5760 pi^2), with the standard c = 1/120 and a_E = 1/360, which were used, not read at source.

'Sets the size of the violation, not its sign' is imprecise. For fixed (a, b), the sign of UO eq. (42) flips with the sign of beta; my re-derivation gives exactly the printed form, -2.12e-7 flipping to +2.12e-7. What does not depend on beta is whether a violation exists: only beta != 0 is needed, because b > 2a or b < 2a can be chosen, and Visser can choose either sign of ln Omega. moves_conclusion='no' still follows.

'Enters only the later curved-space violations, not the 1991 theorems' is right for the 4D coefficient, with two small qualifications. First, W-Y's own 1991 note added in proof is already a 4D violation built on fourth-order curvature terms (Visser p.4). Second, W-Y's 2D theorem depends on the 2D anomaly term 1/(12 pi) for its positivity (UO eqs. 46-51). That is also a computed constant, so the no-datum conclusion is unaffected.

lacked_data answers M's hypothesis with evidence, not presumption. The bound's right-hand side is zero, there is no measured input, and the 4D failure is recorded in W-Y's own note (Visser p.1). Visser 1996's Boulware result on chronal geodesics is confirmed at UO p.2. These points count against M's hypothesis for this result, and the audit says so.

These are citation and wording discrepancies, not refutations. Neither changes the grade: NARROWED rests on the tree's scope, which is a background-hypothesis problem, not a data problem. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, correctly. The audit's rederive script exits 0.

audits.name: Existence of geodesic (Gaussian normal, Phi = 0) slicing

source.located: Gaussian normal coordinates / geodesic slicing, classically G. Darmois (1927), Wald, General Relativity (1984) sec 3.3 and Lemma 9.2.1, and Smarr & York, PRD 17, 2529 (1978). None of these has an arXiv copy. Read in E. Gourgoulhon, '3+1 formalism and bases of numerical relativity', arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007): sec 3.3.3 eq (3.18), sec 4.4.2 pp.61-62, sec 9.2.1 pp.152-153.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/0703035. The review states the result itself, so it is the source read. Darmois 1927, Wald 1984 and Smarr-York 1978 are NAMED-NOT-READ (cited there as refs [105], [265], [247]). A title search for Smarr-York returned an unrelated paper (2107.06551) that only cites it.

audits.published_statement: Gourgoulhon gr-qc/0703035 pp.61-62: 'we set N = 1 (4.75), beta = 0 (4.76) in some neighbourhood [of] a given hypersurface Sigma_0 ... Such coordinates are called Gaussian normal coordinates. The foliation away from Sigma_0 selected by the choice (4.75) of the lapse function is called a geodesic slicing ... the worldlines of the Eulerian observers are geodesics ... g = -dt^2 + gamma_ij dx^i dx^j. In general it is not possible to get a Gaussian normal coordinate system that covers all M. This results from the well known tendencies of timelike geodesics without vorticity ... to focus and eventually cross ... (cf. Lemma 9.2.1 in [Wald]). However ... provided that the neighbourhood is small enough, this is always possible.' Eq (3.18): a = D ln N, so N = 1 means geodesic observers. Sec 9.2.1 p.152: 'this type of foliation can become pathological within a finite range of t'. The geodesic slicing from the t_S = 0 Schwarzschild slice 'hits the singularity at t = [pi] m'.
published_hypotheses: a smooth spacelike hypersurface Sigma_0 is GIVEN; the slicing is generated by the geodesics normal to THAT Sigma_0 (p.62)
LOCAL: exists only 'in some neighbourhood' of Sigma_0 'small enough', i.e. until the normal geodesics focus or cross; not global in general (p.62, p.152; Wald Lemma 9.2.1 / Raychaudhuri)
lapse and shift are free gauge choices that leave the physical solution g unchanged; 'the only things to avoid are coordinate singularities' (p.61)

audits.published_statement: quant-ph/0504143 eq. (15): 'the asymptotic form of T_xx near the boundary z = 0 is one half the corresponding expression for U in this limit, which was found in Ref. [14]: T_xx ~ (1/2) U ~ (sqrt2 omega_p/(128 pi)) (1/z^3), as z -> 0.' Units: Lorentz-Heaviside, hbar = c = 1. The origin is quant-ph/0204125 eq. (37): 'U ~ (sqrt2 omega_p/(64 pi)) (1/z^3)', with <E^2> ~ sqrt2 omega_p/(32 pi z^3) and <B^2> ~ -5 omega_p^2/(96 pi z^2) (eq. 38). So sqrt2/(128 pi) is the coefficient of the TRANSVERSE pressure T_xx, and U's coefficient is twice it. In the same paper T_zz, the normal pressure, is exactly independent of z (eq. 13): the planar normal stress does not diverge at all.
published_hypotheses: H1 planar geometry: vacuum gap 0<z<a between two half-spaces. Eq. (15) is the z -> 0 (z << a) limit, where the position-dependent term dominates and reduces to the single-interface result

H2 collisionless plasma model eps(omega) = 1 - omega_p^2/omega^2 (no damping). 0204125 conclusion: 'collisionless Drude model ... generic form ... at high frequencies ... should lead to the same limiting forms near an interface'

H3 SHARP (step) boundary between dielectric and vacuum. 0504143 p.7: 'this singular behavior ... can be viewed as due to the assumption of a sharp boundary at z = 0'. 0204125 Sec. 3.4: 'The divergence of U is not considered to be physical'
H4 zero temperature: eq. (15) is the T = 0 expression; finite temperature enters only through eqs. 9-12 and 23-24
H5 asymptotic regime omega_p z << 1: the leading term of a Taylor expansion in 1/u (0204125 Sec. 3.4)
H6 non-magnetic media (mu = 1), isotropic, homogeneous, local (no spatial dispersion)
H7 Schwinger-DeRaad-Milton source-theory Green's-function formalism, renormalised by subtracting the empty-space (no-wall) term

audits.published_statement: As restated in quant-ph/0106045 p.25, eqs 2.36-2.37: for two perfectly conducting parallel plates of area S -> oo at separation a, the renormalised vacuum energy is E0ren(a) = -(c hbar pi^2/(720 a^3)) S, with the Minkowski contribution in the gap subtracted. The force is F(a) = -dE/da = -(pi^2/240)(hbar c/a^4) S. Mostepanenko 2021 pp.1-2: 'two parallel, electrically neutral ideal metal plates at zero temperature ... F_IM(a) = -pi^2 hbar c/(240 a^4) ... E_IM(a) = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^3). This is the Casimir energy per unit area.' The LOCAL energy density is not Casimir's 1948 statement but Brown-Maclay 1969. Sopova-Ford p.1 restates it: 'for perfectly conducting plates, one has a constant negative vacuum energy density'. Their eq (52) gives U = -pi^2/(720 a^4) in the limit omega_p -> oo.
published_hypotheses: Perfect conductors: E_t|S = H_n|S = 0 on both plates (review eq 2.27). Review p.154: 'valid only for perfect conductors of infinitely high conductivity ... for sufficiently high frequency any metal becomes transparent'.
Infinite plane-parallel plates, S -> oo (review eq 2.29).
Zero temperature (Mostepanenko 2021 p.1). Review p.79: the thermal effect is negligible for a << hbar c/(k_B T).
A free quantised EM field in the gap with two polarisations, renormalised by subtracting the Minkowski vacuum in the same volume (review eq 2.33).

For the local density (Brown-Maclay via Sopova-Ford) perfect conductivity is again assumed. A dispersive wall adds a positive position-dependent term that diverges at the interface. The midpoint density is then negative only for omega_p a > ~99, i.e. a > 1.3 um at 14.8 eV (Sopova-Ford eqs 50-51).

Real metals reach the ideal limit only for a >> lambda_p; the perturbation expansion is valid for a >= lambda_p (review pp.155-156). Below a few nm the Casimir force is the non-retarded van der Waals force, F = -H/(6 pi a^3) (Mostepanenko 2021 p.2; review eq 4.27).

audits.lacked_data:
Casimir (1948) lacked any measurement: Sparnaay's 1958 attempt was only 'not contradicting', and the parallel-plate test at 15% came in 2002. He also lacked the optical response of real plates, which Lifshitz supplied in 1956. Having these data does not change his conclusion within its hypotheses. The ideal coefficient is re-derived exactly here, and the 2002 coefficient agrees at -0.45 sigma. The Drude/plasma puzzle concerns few-percent real-material corrections, not the ideal limit.

What the later data do change is the domain. The formula is the a >> lambda_p limit, and the tree uses it at 10 nm, 1 nm, 0.1 nm and 0.37 l_P. There the plasma-model interaction energy is 11%, 1.3% and 0.13% of the ideal value, and the midpoint local density is positive.

So M's hypothesis holds here in a form that does not help the device. The missing data narrow where the formula applies but do not make it wrong, and every correction lowers |rho| and enlarges the shortfall. The energy density itself has never been observed (Sopova-Ford p.16), so calling it 'MEASURED' is a status-word discrepancy, not a refutation.
audits.grade_evidence:
The result as published STANDS on its own hypotheses. Script sections A-C re-derive it symbolically, the tree's numbers reproduce (D), no datum has moved (E), and the only parallel-plate measurement read agrees (pull -0.45 sigma).

The tree's use covers a larger class than the result does:
(1) It drops the perfect-conductor condition a >> lambda_p and evaluates the formula at 10 nm, 1 nm and 0.1 nm (achievable.py:124-141, 532-547; candidates.py:129-135). There the plasma-model Lifshitz result is 0.111, 0.0130 and 0.00132 of the ideal energy.
(2) It calls the energy density MEASURED (achievable.py:31, 417-419; candidates.py:73-74). Only the force is measured: 0.5-3 um for parallel plates, above ~120 nm for sphere-plate.
(3) Its KIND pass (candidates.py:78) holds only for a >~ 1.3 um in Al. At the gaps it prices, the plasma-model midpoint density is positive (G).

It is not WRONG, because there is no counterexample to the published result. Every narrowing lowers the available |rho|, so the tree's refusals stand unchanged or stronger. Its numbers are ideal-plate upper bounds, not physical Casimir values.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS: the owners limit the use to ideal plates, relabel the density as an inferred ideal-plate QFT value (the force is what is MEASURED), and present the nm rows as upper bounds. WRONG: a computed contradiction of the ideal coefficient, which the symbolic re-derivation rules out. OPEN: does not apply, because every load-bearing piece was read and checked.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction) for casimir-1948-parallel-plates, graded NARROWED
verifiers.reason:
I tried to refute the grade and could not. NARROWED stands. The reasons follow, with one numeric caveat.

Read at source through alphaXiv:
- quant-ph/0106045 p.25 eqs (2.36)-(2.37) give E = -c hbar pi^2 S/(720 a^3) and F = -(pi^2/240)(hbar c/a^4) S. Eq (4.31) gives the same ideal limit.
- p.154 reads verbatim: 'The original Casimir result (1.3) is valid only for perfect conductors of infinitely high conductivity ... for sufficiently high frequency any metal becomes transparent'.
- p.161 gives lambda_p(Au) = 136 nm (omega_p = 9 eV) and lambda_p(Al) = 107 nm. p.220 uses lambda_p(Al) = 100 nm. The sphere-plate measurement range there is 120-950 nm. Eq (4.27) gives the non-retarded law F = -H/(6 pi a^3), and eq (5.73) gives H_Au = 4.4e-19 J.
- quant-ph/0204125: eq (50) is a negative z-independent term plus a positive z-dependent term. Eq (51) reads 'a > a_c = 99/omega_p = 1.3 um (14.8 eV/omega_p)'. Eq (52) gives U = -pi^2/(720 a^4) in the limit omega_p -> oo, citing Brown-Maclay. The conclusion reads 'The existence of an attractive Casimir force is not an indicator of whether the energy density at the center ... is actually negative'. p.16 reads 'no clear way has been found to directly observe the local energy density'.

Every quotation the audit relies on is accurate. Casimir 1948 and Brown-Maclay 1969 are correctly marked NAMED-NOT-READ. The tree lines it cites (achievable.py:31, 124-141 and 417-419; candidates.py:73-78, 118-149 and 351-394; overturn.py:274-283) say what the audit says they say.

Checks I computed independently (verify/refute/casimir-indep.py, mpmath, my own Lifshitz integrand rather than the auditor's):
- The plasma-model Au interaction-energy ratio eta_E at omega_p = 9 eV is 0.919, 0.525, 0.1099, 0.01287 and 0.001299 at 1000, 100, 10, 1 and 0.1 nm. That matches the audit's 0.920, 0.529, 0.111, 0.0130 and 0.00132 to about 1%.
- Bressi: the theoretical coefficient is K_C = 1.3001e-27 and the pull is -0.445 sigma. This is arithmetic on the numbers the audit quotes; I did not open quant-ph/0203002 myself.
- Al a_c = 99 hbar c/(14.8 eV) = 1.32 um.
- The auditor's re-derivation script exits 0 with ALL PASS.

Why it is not STANDS:
- The tree evaluates the formula at 10 nm, 1 nm, 0.1 nm and 0.37 l_P, where the source's own hypothesis (a >= lambda_p, perfect conductor) fails.
- It calls the density MEASURED, but only the force is measured.
- Its KIND pass rests on a sign that, with dispersive plates, holds only for omega_p a > ~99. At the tree's gaps omega_p a is about 0.75 or less.

Why it is not WRONG: the published ideal-plate result is re-derived exactly and agrees with the only parallel-plate measurement (Bressi 2002). Nothing contradicts it within its own hypotheses.

Why it is not DATA-DEPENDENT: for passive planar media the Lifshitz reflection coefficients satisfy r^2 <= 1. So |E| is at most the ideal value in every material model, and no datum could raise |rho| above the tree's number.

Caveat (a discrepancy in the auditor's numbers, not in the grade): the plasma model leaves out interband transitions and is used here below the range the review gives it ('micrometer domain'). The non-retarded Hamaker law with the review's H_Au = 4.4e-19 J gives a real/ideal ratio of 0.0269 at 1 nm and 0.00269 at 0.1 nm. That is about 2x the audit's 0.0130 and 0.00132. So the audit's '760x' and 'x76.7 -> 2.15e54' figures depend on the model by roughly a factor of 2 at nm gaps: about 370x and x37 on the Hamaker estimate. At 0.1 nm no continuum model is valid at all. These figures should be labelled plasma-model estimates. The direction still holds: every correction lowers |rho| and enlarges the shortfall. Neither the grade nor the tree's refusals move.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: rerun script_path, check its encoding against the published statement, and run a vacuity guard
verifiers.reason:
I re-ran the audit's own script from a copy in verify/rederive/. It gave ALL PASS: 39 checks, exit 0, in 3.9 s rather than the 15 s the audit states. Every printed number matches the audit: eta_E(Au) = 0.111, 0.0130 and 0.00132; the root at 96.6; Al a_c = 1.288 um; the crossover 0.369917 l_P; the Bressi pull -0.45 sigma. The one IntegrationWarning at 1 nm also recurs.

Checking the encoding against the published statement:
(A) The zeta mode sum is the real derivation, not a toy.
(B) It takes the review's Abel-Plana intermediate (2.36) and differentiates it to get (2.37).
(F) The plasma-model Lifshitz integrator is written correctly: the variables, Jacobian and reflection coefficients all check. It matches review eq 5.60 to four digits at 1 um.
(G) I read quant-ph/0204125 eq 50 at source again through alphaXiv. The script's integrand transcribes it faithfully, including (34a) and (34b), the t^2 term, the (1-t^2) term and the e^{-ua} cosh factor, with the prefactor 1/(2 pi^2).

Weak spots in the encoding, none of which moves a conclusion:
(i) Three of section C's checks prove nothing. The Brown-Maclay check is only (E/A)/a, so it assumes the density is uniform. The Sopova-Ford 56+57 check cancels by construction, because the transcribed ± terms are opposite. The traceless check is just 1+1+1-3.
(ii) The paper gives about 99 (eq 51) and about 100 in its text, both read off a figure. The script's root is 96.6. Since the transcription is exact, the gap is in reading the figure or in quadrature accuracy.
(iii) Section F uses lambda_p(Al) = 100 nm, which is 12.4 eV. Section G uses 14.8 eV, which is 84 nm. The two sections are inconsistent here, but the headline numbers use Au.

My own checks (vacuity_guard.py, 15 checks, ALL PASS, 2.7 s):
(1) I derived the uniformity that section C assumes. I built explicit TE and TM mode fields and checked them symbolically against Maxwell's equations and the conducting-plate boundary conditions. Per mode, TE+TM gives |E|^2+|B|^2 = 2, independent of z, so T00 = (E/A)/a follows. The vacuity guard fails as it should: with TE alone the density depends on z.
(2) Vacuity guard on A: the Boyer spectrum (n+1/2)pi/a fails the -pi^2/720 check and gives +7/8 of it. So the check depends on the perfect-conductor hypothesis and is not vacuous.
(3) With the hypothesis restored (lambda_p = 1 pm), the audit's F integrator returns eta_F and eta_E = 0.9999992 and 0.9999994.
(4) An independent analytic non-retarded plasma formula, eta_E = 45 a (omega_p/c) J / pi^4 with J = ∫ Li3((1+2u^2)^-2) du, gives 1.3162e-2 at 1 nm (the audit has 1.3033e-2) and 1.3162e-3 at 0.1 nm (the audit has 1.3159e-3). This confirms the value that raised the warning.
(5) Sopova-Ford p.1, READ, says the positive term has its minimum at the gap centre. Computed at omega_p a = 0.75 (Al at 10 nm), a^4 U is +0.0575, +0.0757, +0.1622 and +0.5630 at z/a = 0.5, 0.4, 0.3 and 0.2. So the density in the gap is positive everywhere, not only at the midpoint. At omega_p a = 200 the midpoint value is -0.00688, as the paper's figure shows.

The owner lines were read (without editing): achievable.py:31, 124-141 and 417-419; candidates.py:70-86, 126-150 and 351-394; overturn.py:274-283. Each audit citation matches, including 'MEASURED', 'The measured effect', '10 nm (state of the art)', the missing 'ideal' qualifier at overturn.py:278, and the owner's own words 'outside the domain of the theory'.

Conclusion: the published result STANDS on its hypotheses, now with the uniformity of the local density derived rather than assumed. The tree's use drops a >> lambda_p, uses MEASURED for a quantity only inferred, and relies on a sign that reverses at the nm gaps it prices. That is correctly graded NARROWED, not WRONG. Every correction lowers the available |rho| in the gap, so the tree's refusals are unchanged or stronger.

One residual limit: all of this is inside the collisionless plasma model. Sopova-Ford call the divergence at the interface unphysical, so densities at the wall itself are not covered.

verifiers.lens: THE DATA CLAIM: each data_at_publication row and the lacked_data answer, checked at source (quant-ph/0106045 pp.154-167, 220, 224-229; quant-ph/0203002 pp.1-10) plus CODATA through scipy.constants
verifiers.reason:
No row is refuted. The grade and the direction of every moves_conclusion hold. One row's numbers depend on the plasma model, and one citation mixes two different aluminium values.

ROWS THAT CHECK OUT AT SOURCE
(1) Coefficients pi^2/720 and pi^2/240: unchanged. Bressi p.2 gives K_C = pi h c/480, which is the same pi^2/240 coefficient.
(2) hbar: scipy (CODATA) gives 1.0545718176461565e-34. The tree's 1.054571817e-34 differs by -6.13e-10 relative, as the audit says.
(3) c: exact.
(4) G: 6.6743(15)e-11, as the audit says.
(5) Bressi measurement: K_C = (1.22 +- 0.18)e-27 N m^2 (p.6 eq 4). The range is 0.5-3.0 um at 15% (abstract), and the fitted exponent is 5.0 +- 0.1 (Fig. 4 caption). The pull is -0.44 against the paper's 1.3e-27 and -0.45 against the exact value 1.3004e-27, so this is rounding only. Two things the audit leaves out, neither of which moves anything:
- The fit uses only the 9 smallest gaps, 0.5-1.1 um.
- The plates were chromium-coated, not ideal. The 15% agreement therefore does not resolve the 10-20% finite-conductivity correction.
The row's conclusion (it confirms the force law where measured and says nothing at 10 nm) stands.
(6) Lambda: internal, reproduced by the audit's own script.
(7) lacked_data: Bressi p.2 quotes Sparnaay 1958 verbatim: 'do not contradict Casimir's theoretical prediction'. Lifshitz 1956 is cited as ref [10].

M'S HYPOTHESIS IS ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE, NOT PRESUMED
Two pieces of missing data were identified: the measurement and the optical response of real metals. Supplying them leaves the ideal coefficient standing (re-derived symbolically; 2002 agreement at -0.45 sigma). They narrow the domain to a >~ lambda_p. The review says so explicitly: 'valid only for perfect conductors' (p.154), and the perturbation expansion holds for a >= lambda_p (pp.155, 162).

DISCREPANCIES IN THE AUDIT'S OWN DATA (recorded, not repaired)
(a) The lambda_p row's efficiency numbers are plasma-model figures, and the review warns that model omits interband absorption (p.159). They are eta_E(Au) = 0.111, 0.0130 and 0.00132, the overstatement 'x9 to 760x', and the scalings 'x76.7 -> 2.15e54' and 'x27.6'.
- The review's own optical-data Hamaker constant is H_Au = (4.4 +- 0.2)e-19 J (eq 5.73, p.166).
- My plasma-model Lifshitz integral at 9.0 eV gives 2.12e-19 J, a ratio of 2.07.
- In the non-retarded regime that makes real-data eta(1 nm) about 0.027 and eta(0.1 nm) about 0.0027.
- The ideal formula then overstates |E| by about 37x at 1 nm and about 370x at 0.1 nm, not 77x and 760x.
- The 1 nm shortfall becomes about 1.0e54 rather than 2.15e54, and the 0.1 nm corridor factor becomes about 19 rather than 27.6.
- At 10 nm the overstatement is probably below 9x. That figure was not computed here.
The direction is unchanged: every model gives |E| below the ideal value, so the tree's shortfalls still only grow. The magnitudes should carry a named hypothesis ('plasma model'), or H_Au should replace them at nm gaps.
(b) At 0.1 nm, below the interatomic spacing, continuum Lifshitz theory is itself outside its domain. The 0.00132 is an extrapolation and needs that named hypothesis.
(c) The row pairs 'lambda_p(Al) ~ 100 nm' (review p.220) with 'hbar omega_p(Al) = 14.8 eV' (Sopova-Ford). These disagree: 14.8 eV corresponds to 83.8 nm. The review also gives 107 nm (11.5 eV, p.161) and 12.5 eV (p.160).
- The Al crossover a_c = 1.29 um holds only for 14.8 eV. With 11.5 eV it is 1.66 um.
- The midpoint density is positive at the tree's 10 nm and 1 nm gaps under every one of these values, so conclusion (3) stands.
- The review's own Au plasma frequency is inconsistent too: 9.0 eV on p.160, 11.5 eV on p.229. That is the source's discrepancy, not the audit's.
(d) moves_conclusion 'Yes' on the lambda_p row is defensible. It moves the tree's numbers but not its refusals, and it should say exactly that.

VERDICT
None of this reaches the grade. The published result STANDS on its hypotheses, and the tree's use is NARROWED.

The sentence massform uses is in Sec. 1 after eq. (3), printed p.2 = PDF p.3 (massform's 'p.2' is the printed page). So the two owners cite the same PDF under different page conventions. audits.published_statement: Conclusions (printed p.27): 'We find that, for M_h = 125 GeV, lambda(M_Pl) = -0.014+-0.006, see eq. (64). The exact vanishing of lambda(M_Pl) is excluded at 2 sigma. Moreover, the smallness of beta_lambda at high energy implies that lambda remains negative in a relatively large energy range. Indeed, we find that, for M_h = 125 GeV, the instability scale develops at 10^{11+-1} GeV. Quantum tunneling is sufficiently slow to ensure at least metastability of the EW vacuum, see fig. 5. ... beta_lambda ... vanishes at a scale of about 3 x 10^17 GeV.' Sec. 1 (printed p.2): 'M_h [GeV] > 129.4 + 1.4((M_t - 173.1)/0.7) - 0.5((alpha_s(M_Z) - 0.1184)/0.0007) +- 1.0_th (2). Combining in quadrature the theoretical uncertainty with the experimental errors on M_t and alpha_s we get M_h > 129.4 +- 1.8 GeV (3). From this result we conclude that vacuum stability of the SM up to the Planck scale is excluded at 2 sigma (98% C.L. one sided) for M_h < 126 GeV.' Fig. 4 caption: 'The instability scale Lambda_I at which the SM potential becomes negative ... 1 sigma bands in M_t = 173.1 +- 0.6 GeV, alpha_s(M_Z) = 0.1184 +- 0.0007, M_h = 125.66 +- 0.34 GeV ... The theoretical error is not shown and corresponds to a +-1 GeV uncertainty in M_h.'
published_hypotheses: The Standard Model alone, extrapolated to the Planck scale. The paper says it 'ignores possible new (unknown) UV threshold effects occurring near the Planck scale' (printed p.27). No new physics, and gravity is not included.
NNLO: three-loop running for the gauge, top Yukawa and Higgs quartic couplings; two-loop matching keeping the leading alpha_s, y_t and lambda effects; two-loop effective potential.

Lambda_I is defined as the field value where the two-loop RG-improved potential V_eff = lambda_eff(h) h^4/4 turns negative (eq. 51, Fig. 4). The paper names no gauge and does not discuss the gauge dependence of this value.

Inputs: M_t = 173.1 +- 0.7 GeV treated as the pole mass, with a +-Lambda_QCD ~ 0.3 GeV ambiguity (eq. 61, p.16); alpha_s(M_Z) = 0.1184 +- 0.0007 (eq. 58); alpha_em^-1 = 127.937 and sin^2 theta_W = 0.23126 (eq. 55); M_h = 125 GeV for the p.27 sentences.
The '+-1' in 10^{11+-1} is a parametric ~1 sigma band. Fig. 4 draws 1 sigma bands in M_t, alpha_s and M_h, and the theory error is not shown. It is not a bound.
The '2 sigma' is one-sided. It combines the 1.0 GeV theory error in quadrature with the experimental M_t and alpha_s errors, and eq. (2) is linear in M_t and alpha_s about 173.1 and 0.1184.

Sec. 4.2 (printed p.21), for xi|H|^2 R: unitarity is violated at M_Pl/xi, and the new physics there is 'naturally expected' to 'affect the scalar potential above M_Pl/xi in an uncontrollable way'. Keeping the SM potential shape above that scale is an assumption the authors call 'questionable'. verifiers.reason:
The grade NARROWED holds under this lens. Every value_then and value_now is right at source, and M's hypothesis is answered with computed evidence in both directions. Four discrepancies in the prose are recorded below. None of them moves the grade.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED AT SOURCE
(1) M_t then. 173.1 +- 0.7 GeV is eq. (61), and the +-Lambda_QCD ~ 0.3 GeV ambiguity is on printed p.16. M_t now. 2401.08811 Table I gives 172.4(7) for the cross-section mass (M_t^sigma) and 172.57(29) for the MC mass (M_t^MC), both labelled PDG 2024.
(2) alpha_s. 0.1184 +- 0.0007 is eq. (58). Now it is 0.1180(9) in Table I.
(3) M_h. The p.27 sentence uses 125 GeV. Fig. 4 uses 125.66 +- 0.34. Now it is 125.20(11). The shift of +0.14 in log10 Lambda_I is re-derived from Buttazzo eq. (67).
(4) Critical top mass. Hiller Table I gives 171.10 GeV (lambda_eff > 0). Eq. (2) inverted at (125.20, 0.1180) gives 170.86 +- 0.5 GeV, re-derived here.
(5) Lambda_I now. Hiller p.3 gives Lambda_0,eff ~ 5.3e11 GeV in Landau gauge, and his footnote says it is gauge-dependent. Buttazzo eq. (67) is READ with exactly the coefficients the script uses (9.5, 0.7, -1.0, +0.3), and so is Lambda_I ~ 13 Lambda_V in Landau gauge. Recomputed, this gives 11.25 (M_t^MC) and 11.42 (M_t^sigma). 1608.06765 confirms two points: h_I ~ 1e11 is not gauge invariant, with an uncertainty 'of up to two orders of magnitude'; and a large-n Lambda_I ~ 1e11 is 'rather close' to the Landau-gauge h_I.
(6) The statements that M_t^sigma is -1.9 sigma and M_t^MC is -5.1 sigma from stability are Table I verbatim. Hiller's own summary is 'the fate of the standard model vacuum remains an important open question'.
(7) lacked_data. Degrassi Table 1 does carry the O(Lambda_QCD) top-mass error (+-0.6 GeV on M_h). It is also printed that 'the dominant uncertainty is experimental and comes mostly from the measurement of M_t'. So 'a settled meaning of M_t' is genuinely the datum they lacked. Hiller ends: 'Sharpening its [the MC mass's] interpretation would hence also be a useful endeavor.'
Every moves_conclusion verdict follows from these numbers, including the 'no' on Lambda_I.

DISCREPANCIES (recorded, not repaired)
(a) M_t row and grade_evidence. They say 'Hiller's full analysis gives 5.1 sigma and 1.9 sigma' and 'stability is excluded at 5.1 sigma with the MC mass'. That over-represents the source. Table I gives a one-observable-at-a-time shift, with every other input held at its central value. Hiller's own combined statement (Sec. II.B, Fig. 2) is different: with M_t and alpha_s uncorrelated and added in quadrature, the MC mass 'indicates a 3 sigma tension', and M_t^sigma gives 'less than 2 sigma'. The CMS correlated input gives -1.5 sigma. The audit's own eq. (2) route gives 2.58 and 1.68 sigma, which agrees with Hiller's combined 3 sigma and <2 sigma. So the DATA-DEPENDENT sub-finding stands (below 2 sigma with M_t^sigma, above with M_t^MC). The figure 5.1 should read 'single-parameter shift, about 3 sigma combined'.
(b) alpha_s row. It says 'M_h,crit falls by 0.29 GeV'. That is a sign error. By eq. (2), -0.5*(0.1180 - 0.1184)/0.0007 = +0.286, so M_h,crit rises by 0.29 GeV. A lower alpha_s makes stability harder, consistent with Hiller's upward shift of +3.7 sigma. The script's C5 numbers (128.63 and 128.29) already contain the rise, so only the row's prose is wrong. 'Only slightly' still holds.
(c) lacked_data. It says 'Lambda_I = 10^11.25 to 10^11.72 by three independent routes'. The third route (~1e11) is 10^11.00, so the span is 10^11.0 to 10^11.72. That is still inside 10^(11+-1). Two qualifiers are also missing from that route:
- The 1608.06765 large-n Lambda_I is computed at 2013-era inputs (M_t = 173.34, the best fit of their ref. [5]), not at PDG 2024.
- It carries a model-dependent factor g/sqrt(2) (eq. 31, with g = 1 taken).
Also, the Buttazzo route is not independent of Degrassi: the author group overlaps, and it uses the same Landau-gauge lambda_eff.
(d) Critical top mass row. It is labelled value_then, but it is the 2012 formula evaluated at 2024 inputs, not a value published in 2012. Degrassi's own 2012 figures are M_t <= 171 GeV for lambda(M_Pl) = 0 (p.19) and 171.083 GeV (Fig. 7, M_h = 125).
Minor: Degrassi is internally inconsistent. Figs. 1, 4 and 6 draw M_t = 173.1 +- 0.6, while eq. (61) gives +-0.7. This is a source discrepancy, not an audit error.

M'S HYPOTHESIS
It is answered with evidence, not presumed. The authors did lack a settled M_t and its meaning. That datum decides whether the one-sided 2 sigma survives, and today the answer is split: 1.68 sigma with M_t^sigma, about 2.6 to 3 sigma with M_t^MC. It does not move Lambda_I. One caution against reading it in M's favour: Degrassi stated the 2 sigma as conditional on the 2012 inputs, and eq. (2) is explicitly parametric in M_t. M_t has since moved by less than 1 sigma(2012). So nothing published was wrong; a data-conditional qualifier moved within its own stated uncertainty. The audit's words 'partly borne out' are acceptable only with that reading.

WHY THE GRADE STANDS

source.located: J.L. Friedman, K. Schleich, D.M. Witt, 'Topological Censorship', PRL 71 1486 (1993), arXiv:gr-qc/9305017v2 (9 Jun 1995). Pages used: the abstract; p.3 (ANEC definition and Theorem 1); pp.4-5 (Lemmas 1-2 and their proofs); pp.5-7 (proof of Theorem 1 and the Penrose-Sorkin-Woolgar alternate proof); pp.8-9 (the withdrawn v1 Theorem 2, which fell to Burnett gr-qc/9504012, and the semiclassical remark).
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true) on arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9305017: the whole v2 text was read. Also read at source for comparison: Galloway-Schleich-Witt-Woolgar gr-qc/9902061 pp.1, 3-6, 8-11 (Thm 2.1, Thm 2.2 and the remark after them); Graham-Olum 0705.3193 pp.1-8 (whole paper); Schleich-Witt gr-qc/9903061 pp.1-12 (whole). Galloway CQG 12 L99 (1995), Borde CQG 4 343 (1987) and Tipler PRD 17 2521 (1978) are NAMED-NOT-READ; they are known here only through the GSWW, FSW and Graham-Olum restatements.

audits.published_statement: FSW v2 p.3 defines ANEC this way: 'A spacetime satisfies ANEC if the integral of T_ab k^a k^b is nonnegative along every inextendible null geodesic with affine parameter lambda and corresponding tangent k^a.' The theorem reads: 'Theorem 1. If an asymptotically flat, globally hyperbolic spacetime (M, g_ab) satisfies the averaged null energy condition, then every causal curve from J- to J+ is deformable to gamma_0 rel J.' Here gamma_0 is a timelike curve from J- to J+ lying in a simply connected neighbourhood of J. The abstract states the theorem with the pointwise null energy condition instead. The Lemma 2 proof (p.5) says: 'ANEC and theta < 0 imply that every outward null geodesic from the outer trapped surface T has a conjugate point within finite affine parameter length.' On p.8 the authors add that 'any energy condition which implies that outward directed null congruences with theta < 0 have conjugate points will suffice', and they leave the semiclassical case open (citing Wald-Yurtsever). On p.4 they note: 'If the Poincare conjecture is false, the theorem does not prevent one from probing fake 3-spheres.'
published_hypotheses: H1 asymptotic flatness: there is a conformal completion with Omega vanishing on J and a nonvanishing null gradient. J = J+ U J-, each part S^2 x R with complete null generators; completeness in the future direction is not required (p.2).
H2 global hyperbolicity: M = D(Sigma) for a Cauchy surface Sigma (p.2).
H3 ANEC on EVERY inextendible null geodesic: INT T_ab k^a k^b dlambda >= 0 (p.3). The abstract states the pointwise NEC instead.
H4 (implicit) the Einstein equations hold, so a condition on T_ab is a condition on R_ab k^a k^b. GSWW gr-qc/9902061 p.8 makes this explicit.

H5 (implicit in the proof) the conjugate-point step needs the integral along the HALF-geodesic that starts on the trapped surface. Galloway 1995 and GSWW Thm 2.1(iii) state the condition in that form: INT_0^inf Ric >= 0 along every future-complete null geodesic. GSWW call it 'a modified form of the ANEC'.
H6 the source is classical: FSW treat semiclassical validity as a question, not a result.
The theorem is about ACTIVE censorship only, i.e. causal curves from J- to J+. Passive detection is allowed, as in the RP^3 geon. The v1 Theorem 2 is withdrawn in v2 as false.
The fake-3-sphere caveat depends on the Poincare conjecture, which was open in 1993-95.
hypothesis_drift: higgs.py:124 ('A WORMHOLE NEEDS ANEC, by topological censorship') drops H1 (asymptotic flatness) and H2 (global hyperbolicity). It names no form of the energy condition: FSW's whole-line H3, the half-line H5 that the proof actually needs, or whole-line ANEC plus the null generic condition. It also leaves H4 unstated. In its own context (the nonminimal xi phi^2 R coupling, Barcelo-Visser) the condition that enters the proof is on the effective R_kk, which is what Barcelo-Visser eq. (2.6) computes, so this omission changes nothing there. The contrapositive only puts the ANEC failure on SOME null geodesic, not specifically on the radial throat geodesic that Barcelo-Visser integrate. The higgs.py conclusion rests on Barcelo-Visser, read at source, not on FSW.

anecscope.py:32-33 ('what the topological-censorship and no-wormhole results actually use') and anecscope.py:170 ('what topological censorship actually uses') attribute achronal ANEC to FSW, but FSW's H3 covers every inextendible null geodesic, not only achronal ones. The achronal form is Graham-Olum 0705.3193 Theorem 1, and that theorem ADDS two hypotheses the tree drops. (a) The spacetime must be simply connected, so it only rules out wormholes between different asymptotically flat regions, not wormholes back into the same region (p.5). Ford's counterexample shows why: a throat longer than the outside distance between its mouths makes every through-throat path chronal. (b) The null generic condition. The version also assumes self-consistency. anecscope drops H1 and H2 as well.
necindex.py:242 ('Graham-Olum; topological censorship uses it') makes the same attribution as anecscope.py:170. It is not a canonical owner; recorded only.

index3.py:61 ('ANEC forbids any shortcut, so no portal either') claims more than the theorem gives. The theorem needs H1 and H2, and in its achronal form it does not cover shortcuts back into the same universe. Not a canonical owner; recorded only.

TARGET-1-RESULT.md:174 ('geodesic-integrated ANEC positive ... That is the condition topological censorship actually uses') does not say which geodesics. The corrected theorem needs either the half-line integral on every future-complete null geodesic near J, or whole-line ANEC plus the generic condition, not ANEC on a sampled family. Not a canonical owner; recorded, not graded.

No drift, recorded as evidence the other way: launcher.py:249-256 restates FSW correctly, and its step from pointwise NEC to averaged NEC holds for both the whole-line and half-line forms. cosmo.py:11 names 'asympt. flat + glob. hyp.' correctly.
