verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (adversarial, both directions) for gr-qc/9305017, Friedman-Schleich-Witt topological censorship
verifiers.reason:
I tried to refute the NARROWED grade and could not. I read the sources myself and every point the grade rests on holds.

1. FSW v2, read in full. On p.3, ANEC is defined over "every inextendible null geodesic", meaning the whole line. The Lemma 2 step on p.5 relies on "ANEC and theta<0 imply ... conjugate point", which is a statement about the half-geodesic that starts on T. It cites Borde. On p.8 FSW themselves say that any condition giving conjugate points for theta<0 congruences "will suffice". So the literal definition and the step do not match.

2. The literature confirms the gap at source. GSWW gr-qc/9902061, which includes two of the three FSW authors, says on p.3 that FSW holds "ultimately, in the modified form used below -- see [6]". Their Thm 2.1(iii) on p.8 uses the half-line integral from 0 to infinity. On the same page they say that "ANEC" usually means the integral over geodesics that are complete both to the past and the future. Their p.11 remark gives the alternative repair: whole-line ANEC plus the generic condition, argued through a null line. So this is not a restatement or a misprint. Check C is also sound: theta=-c e^{-lam} is an exact solution by construction, and the backward branch can make the whole-line integral nonnegative while the half-line integral is -c(c+4)/4. I reran the script and it exits 0.

3. Graham-Olum 0705.3193, read in full, confirms the rest.
   - Lemma 1 on p.3 needs the generic condition.
   - Theorem 1 on p.5 adds simple connectivity.
   - The Ford counterexample on pp.5-6 is a same-universe wormhole.
   - p.7 says the Galloway/Roman singularity theorems use the half-geodesic.

   The drift the audit reports in the tree is at the lines it names. higgs.py:124 states no hypotheses. anecscope.py:32-33 and :170 credit achronal ANEC to topological censorship without saying simply connected or generic. launcher.py:249-256 and cosmo.py:11 state the result correctly.

4. Nothing here pushes the grade toward WRONG. No spacetime is known, or shown here, that meets the corrected hypotheses and still violates censorship.

Nothing pushes it toward STANDS either. As published, the proof needs a stronger or extra hypothesis, and the tree's wording claims a wider class than the theorem proves.

Weaknesses that do not move the grade:
- The z3 part of check E is vacuous. It only tests d/L<1 <=> d<L and does not model spacetime geometry. Ford's example stands on Graham-Olum pp.5-6, read at source, not on E.
- E3, the existence of K, is trivial linear algebra.
- FSW's literal Theorem 1 (whole-line ANEC, no generic condition) is neither proven nor refuted in anything I read, so the truth of that exact statement is OPEN. NARROWED is still the right grade: it means the result is proven only with a stronger or added hypothesis.
- FSW p.8 already names the conjugate-point property as what the proof needs. That partly anticipates the repair and softens "incomplete as published", but it does not change the literal whole-line definition on p.3.

The Lemma 2 proof on p.5 says 'ANEC and theta < 0 imply that every outward null geodesic from the outer trapped surface T has a conjugate point'. GSWW gr-qc/9902061 p.8 Thm 2.1(iii) uses INT_0^inf Ric >= 0 on future-complete null geodesics and calls it 'a modified form of the ANEC'. p.3 says FSW holds '(ultimately, in the modified form used below -- see [6])'. C works at the level of the Raychaudhuri ODE: zero shear, and one R_kk profile on one geodesic. Zero shear is the worst case, so that choice is legitimate. The vacuity guards discriminate. My scripts are in verify/rederive/fsw9305017/, a private subfolder, because another verifier overwrote a shared vacuity.py in verify/rederive/. audits.name: Goedel 1949: an exact Lorentzian (Einstein) solution containing closed timelike curves

source.located: K. Goedel, Rev. Mod. Phys. 21, 447 (1949), which has no arXiv copy. It is restated exactly in: Kajari-Walser-Schleich-Delgado arXiv:gr-qc/0404032 Sec.3.1 eq.(15), with the field-equation relations after eq.(18); Buser-Kajari-Schleich arXiv:1303.4651 eq.(1), Sec.2.1 and Sec.5 p.27; Verma-Aluri-Mota-Obukhov arXiv:2506.00860 eq.(1) (misprinted there); Luminet arXiv:2101.08592 pp.1-6.
source.via: Goedel 1949 itself is NAMED-NOT-READ. The statement, the hypotheses and both charts were READ in gr-qc/0404032 (pp.6-10), 1303.4651 (pp.3-7, 27-29), 2506.00860 (pp.1-3) and 2101.08592 (pp.1-6). Every formula used here was re-derived in sympy (E1-E3). That includes the dy^2 coefficient that the 2506.00860 restatement misprints: the field equations force it (E1a'').

audits.published_statement: As restated: 'in 1949 Kurt Goedel derived an exact solution of Einstein's field equations, in which a homogeneous mass distribution rotates around every point in space. This solution shows rather unusual properties such as closed time like world-lines' (gr-qc/0404032 p.2). Line element (gr-qc/0404032 eq.15): ds^2/(4a^2) = dt^2 - dr^2 - (sinh^2 r - sinh^4 r) dphi^2 - dz^2 + 2 sqrt2 sinh^2 r dphi dt. It solves R_mn - g R/2 = kappa T + Lambda g for a perfect fluid with kappa(rho + p/c^2) = 1/(a^2 c^2) and kappa p = Lambda + 1/(2a^2); for dust, Lambda = -1/(2a^2). 'a homogeneous solution with trivial topology R^4 yet contains CTCs through every point' (hep-th/0209114 p.3). 'infinite, non-expanding ... matter rotates relative to the compass of inertia with the angular velocity 2(pi G rho)^(1/2)' (2101.08592 p.1).
published_hypotheses: Einstein's field equations with a cosmological constant: R_mn - g R/2 = kappa T + Lambda g
Source: pressure-free perfect fluid (dust) with rho > 0 and comoving u = d_t, and Lambda = -1/(2a^2) < 0 ('pressureless dust balanced by a negative cosmological constant', hep-th/0209114 p.13)
Stationary and spatially homogeneous (five Killing vectors), not static, not isotropic; non-expanding, shear-free, rigidly rotating with Omega_G = c/(sqrt2 a)
Manifold R^4 with trivial topology: the CTCs do not come from an identification
Four spacetime dimensions
The CTCs are not geodesics: 'a proper acceleration has to be applied' (1303.4651 p.27)
Goedel did not offer it as a model of our universe, since it has no redshift (1303.4651 p.3)
hypothesis_drift: ADDED DIMENSION, supplied by a trivial construction rather than by Goedel (latticectc.py:82-83, "there exists a 5D Lorentzian metric containing a CTC -- Goedel 1949"). Goedel's solution is 4D. The 5D statement follows at once: Goedel x R, with a flat fifth direction, is Lorentzian and carries the same CTC (E5a). An exact 5D Goedel analogue in minimal supergravity also exists (hep-th/0209114 eq.3.29; E5c, E5e). The attribution is loose; the statement is true.

WEAKENED: the owner at latticectc.py:82-83 takes only the bare existence of a Lorentzian metric with a CTC. That needs neither Goedel nor any field equation: flat space with a periodic time already has one (2101.08592 p.4; E7; the causal-lattice case of D21). So 'never in doubt' is accurate for the statement as used. Goedel's actual content is stronger: an exact Einstein solution on R^4, with positive-density dust and CTCs through every point (E1, E2, E3).

THE LABEL UNDERSTATES THE SOURCE (latticectc.py:141-144, CODIM1_CTC_REFUSAL '... NEC-violating on the CTC slice -- Goedel-class, not a braneworld'; mirrored at LEDGER.md:44 and :117). Goedel's source satisfies the NEC and the WEC (E4a, E4b), and his metric solves the field equations with a specified source (E1f). The refused metric has no field equation and violates the NEC (latticectc.py:76-86), so it falls below Goedel's class rather than inside it. This is a discrepancy of description, and it strengthens the refusal's 'adds nothing': a NEC-satisfying 5D CTC metric already exists (E5b, Goedel x R, with the stress tensor read off its own Einstein tensor; E5c/E5c'', GGHPR with a Maxwell source).

DROPPED, with no effect on the use: homogeneity (CTCs through every point), R^4 topology, the non-geodesic character of the CTCs, and the dust plus negative-Lambda source. Bare existence needs none of them.

MISPRINT IN A SECONDARY SOURCE (not in the tree, not in Goedel): 2506.00860 eq.(1) prints e^{2x} dy^2 with coefficient 1. As printed the metric is degenerate, det g = 0 (E1a'). Requiring dust plus Lambda forces the coefficient 1/2, uniquely (E1a''). This is recorded as a discrepancy, not an error, and the tree does not use that paper.

audits.lacked_data: In 1949 Goedel lacked the CMB and every vorticity limit built on it, the causal-structure machinery (Hawking-Ellis 1973; chronology protection 1992), brane and higher-dimensional frameworks, and string corrections. He did have Hubble's expansion, and he said himself that his model lacks it. On the evidence here, having the later data does not change the conclusion, and the evidence runs both ways. For stability: the result is closed-form and uses no data, it is re-derived exactly (E1, E3), and the CTC survives the brane generalisation at effective-equation level (Barrow-Tsagas, E6). Against physical relevance: observation disfavours global rotation (limits cited, NOT read), and some Goedel-type solutions with extra sources avoid CTCs. Those are different solutions, though, and they bear on whether nature realises Goedel's universe, which the tree never claims. The tree uses only 'a Lorentzian metric with a CTC exists'. No datum can move that, and it holds even without Goedel (E7).

audits.published_statement: (A) Sahlmann-Verch 2000, Thm 5.1: 'Let omega in P and let omega_2 be the two-point distribution of omega. Suppose that WF(omega_2^(P)) = empty = WF(omega_2(P)), and suppose also that the symmetric part or the anti-symmetric part of the two-point distribution is smooth at causal separation. Then it holds that WF(omega_2) subset R.' Here P is the set of finite convex combinations of ground states or KMS states at beta > 0, taken for the flow of an everywhere-timelike Killing field on a globally hyperbolic stationary spacetime. From p.23: 'for the canonically quantized scalar Klein-Gordon field, WF(omega_2) subset R implies WF(omega_2) = R and thus the two-point function of every strictly passive state is of Hadamard form' (citing Radzikowski). On quasifreeness SV say only (p.19) that ground and KMS states 'turn out to be quasifree in examples'. (B) Sanders 2013, Thm 6.2, stated for V > 0: '(i) There exists a unique extremal C^1 beta-KMS state with vanishing one-point function ... (ii) [it] is quasi-free, regular ... (iv) Any D^2 beta-KMS state is Hadamard ... (v) Any extremal beta-KMS state ... is of the form eta*_rho omega_0 for some gauge transformation of the second kind'. (C) Khavkine-Moretti Def. 15 and Thm 9(b): a two-point function is Hadamard when it differs locally from the Hadamard parametrix by a smooth function, and two Hadamard two-point functions differ by a C^infinity function.
published_hypotheses: SV Thm 5.1: the spacetime is globally hyperbolic and stationary, and the flow is generated by an everywhere TIMELIKE, future-pointing Killing field
SV Thm 5.1: the state is strictly passive, i.e. a finite convex sum of ground states or KMS states with beta_i > 0 (beta = 0 excluded)
SV Thm 5.1: omega_2 is a distribution and a bisolution up to C^infinity
SV Thm 5.1: the symmetric or the antisymmetric part of omega_2 is smooth at causal (spacelike) separation

SV p.23 / Radzikowski: passing from WF subset R to Hadamard form is done for the CCR scalar Klein-Gordon field. Khavkine-Moretti Thm 9 states it for any m^2 and xi in d = 4, and their Remark 23 records a gap in Radzikowski's original proof, filled by Sahlmann-Verch 2001 and by Khavkine-Moretti
SV: quasifreeness is not derived; they say only 'quasifree in examples'
Sanders Thm 6.2 requires V > 0, which in Minkowski means m > 0; the massless field is outside the theorem. Its uniqueness holds only among extremal C^1 KMS states WITH VANISHING ONE-POINT FUNCTION
PSV 1806.02124: a KMS state taken along a flow that is spacelike at x is not Hadamard at x

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (exit 0): 19 checks, including 3 controls built to fail. K1 (KMS): detailed balance (1+n)e^{-beta w} = n and the strip identity W+(t-i beta) = W+(-t) hold exactly in sympy; the control with the Boltzmann factor fails as it should. K2 (Gaussian): in the one-oscillator Gibbs state, <x> = <x^3> = 0 and <x^4> = 3<x^2>^2 to 1e-12. K3 (kernel): g(0) = pi^2/30 and the tail -3/(2 pi^2 u^4) are exact; the mode integral matches the coth closed form to 3.5e-28; ||g^2||_1 = 0.0522114036827681 against 180(zeta6-zeta7)/pi^3 = 0.0522114036827682; the control with tanh fails. K4 (Hadamard, elementary form): W_beta - W_0 is regular at coincidence with value 1/12 = <:phi^2:>, has no pole on the light cone, matches its integral representation to 3e-19, and every derivative is bounded by a finite moment Gamma(j+2)zeta(j+2). So W_beta - W_0 is C^infinity and the state is Hadamard, without relying on Radzikowski's microlocal equivalence. K5a (control): the 1+1 massless thermal difference diverges. K6: a constant shift preserves KMS at the two-point level, so zero mean is a choice.

later_literature.what: Proves the KMS state exists, is quasifree, is unique among extremal C^1 states with zero one-point function, and that D^2 KMS states are Hadamard, but only for V > 0. The massless state the tree uses falls outside it and is covered instead by SV Thm 5.1 and check K4.

A KMS state along a flow that is spacelike at x is not Hadamard at x. It restates that KMS states for timelike Killing flows satisfy the microlocal spectrum condition. It excludes only states the tree does not use.

Gives the definitions of quasifree and Hadamard states and the Radzikowski theorem (any m^2 and xi, d = 4). Remark 23 records a gap in Radzikowski's original proof, filled later by SV 2001 and by the authors.
Relates passivity (and so KMS) to QWEIs and the microlocal spectrum condition.
KMS states for different inertial frames are disjoint; this does not bear on the property of a single inertial KMS state.

audits.lacked_data: The result is a theorem with no empirical input, so M's hypothesis has no datum to act on here. Evidence for it not biting: nothing in the statement depends on a measurement, so no later measurement can move it. Evidence against a naive STANDS: what the authors lacked was not data but finished proofs and scope. SV 2000 did not derive quasifreeness, Sanders 2013 derived it only for V > 0 (so the massless case is outside), and Radzikowski's 1996 equivalence had a proof gap that was filled later (Khavkine-Moretti Remark 23). None of these changes the conclusion for the tree's state. The massless 3+1 Planck state is quasifree by construction, KMS by K1, and Hadamard by K4, which uses neither Sanders' V > 0 nor the microlocal equivalence.
audits.grade_evidence: The claim at noise.py:111-114 is true of the state the tree builds. KMS is re-derived exactly (K1). The state is Gaussian by construction, and the Wick relation <x^4> = 3<x^2>^2 is checked (K2). Hadamard is READ at source for KMS states of timelike flows (SV Thm 5.1 with Radzikowski via Khavkine-Moretti Thm 9; Sanders Thm 6.2(iv) for m > 0) and re-derived directly for m = 0 in 3+1 (K4). The kernel, g(0), the tail and ||g^2||_1 are all re-derived (K3). No datum enters. The tree leaves four hypotheses unstated (m = 0 for the kernel, 3+1, an inertial timelike KMS flow, zero mean as a choice); all four hold in its setting and none shrinks the class it uses, so the grade is not NARROWED. Two discrepancies are recorded but are not errors: the 'Stefan-Boltzmann' label is the one-scalar value, half the photon value, and T1's failure is shown only for m = 0.

It would become WRONG only if K1, K3 or K4 failed on re-run. OPEN would apply to a claim that every massless KMS state is zero-mean or quasifree. No source read here proves that, and K6 argues against it.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction) for thermal-state-kms-hadamard, graded STANDS
verifiers.reason:
I could not refute STANDS in either direction.

(1) Sources, read myself through alphaXiv.
- Sahlmann-Verch math-ph/0002021v2, Thm 5.1 (p.20). The audit quotes it correctly, and the hypotheses match: globally hyperbolic and stationary spacetime; the flow is generated by an everywhere timelike, future-pointing Killing field; the state is in P, a convex combination of ground or KMS states with beta_i > 0, and p.6 says outright that "beta_i = 0 is not admitted!".
- The p.23 remark is quoted exactly: "for the canonically quantized scalar Klein-Gordon field, WF(omega_2) subset R implies WF(omega_2) = R and thus the two-point function of every strictly passive state is of Hadamard form, see [35]".
- The quasifree hedge on p.19 is also exact: ground and KMS states "turn out to be quasifree in examples".
- Sanders 1209.6068v2, Thm 6.2 (p.37). It is stated for V > 0 and says what the audit quotes: (i) a unique extremal C^1 beta-KMS state with vanishing one-point function, (ii) it is quasi-free, (iv) any D^2 beta-KMS state is Hadamard, (v) the gauge-transform form. The massless case is therefore correctly placed outside Sanders.

(2) Re-run. The auditor's script gives 19 PASS, ALL PASS, exit 0.

(3) My own independent check, kms_indep.py, written separately from the auditor's script:
- g(0) = pi^2/(30 beta^4) from the coth kernel.
- The tail limit u^4 g(u) -> -3/(2 pi^2).
- The mode integral INT d^3k/(2pi)^3 k n(k) equals pi^2/30 at beta = 1 to 30 digits. So g(0) is the energy density of one real scalar, and the 'Stefan-Boltzmann' label is the one-scalar value, half the photon value, as the audit says.
- <:phi^2:> = 1/12 to 30 digits.
- The 3+1 infrared moments INT k^(1+j) n dk are finite for j >= 0. Every derivative of W_beta - W_0 is therefore dominated by a finite integral, so W_beta - W_0 is C^infinity on R^4. The Minkowski vacuum is exactly the Hadamard parametrix, so the thermal state is Hadamard directly, without Radzikowski's equivalence or Sanders' V > 0.

(4) Hypothesis drift. I checked each unstated hypothesis for a narrowing:
- m = 0 kernel: the property holds for all m >= 0.
- 3+1 dimensions: this is the tree's setting throughout.
- Inertial, timelike KMS flow: satisfied.
- Zero mean: a choice the tree states explicitly. It is not forced by KMS, since a constant shift solves the massless equation and is time-invariant.
None of these shrinks the class the tree uses at noise.py:111-114 (T1_SURVIVES_SMEARING, D22), so NARROWED is not supported. No datum enters, so DATA-DEPENDENT does not apply. Nothing failed on re-run, so WRONG does not apply.

Minor, and not grade-moving: Sanders Thm 6.2(v) prints 'eta*_rho omega_0' where omega^(beta) is presumably meant. The audit quotes the source verbatim, which is correct practice. The audit's recorded discrepancies (the scalar-versus-photon label, and T1's failure shown only for m = 0) are rightly recorded as discrepancies and not as errors.

verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN: I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it. It gives 19 PASS, 'ALL PASS', exit 0 (about 10 s). The numbers match the audit: K3c worst relative error 3.5e-28, ||g^2||_1 = 0.0522114036827681 against 0.0522114036827682, K4b' 3.09e-19.

VACUITY GUARD (verify/rederive/vacuity.py). Every load-bearing check fails when its hypothesis is negated.
- K1: the strip identity fails for the vacuum (n = 0), for Fermi-Dirac, for the wrong temperature 1/(e^{2bw}-1), for Boltzmann, and for the opposite strip sign W+(t+i beta). It holds only for Planck with the physically correct sign.
- K2: the ratio <x^4>/3<x^2>^2 is 0.556 for Fock |1>, 0.670 for a uniform mixture and 0.878 for a non-Gibbs diagonal state. It is 1.000000 only for the Gibbs state.
- K4: regularity at coincidence and absence of a light-cone pole both fail with the wrong vacuum coefficient 1/(4 pi), with no subtraction, and with an asymmetric kernel. Both pass only for the true W_beta - W_0.
- I also checked the dominated-derivative step behind K4b: sampled sup|sinc^(j)| is at most 1/(j+1) for j = 0..5. With Gamma(j+2)zeta(j+2) < infinity for every j >= 0, analytically, dominated convergence gives W_beta - W_0 in C^infinity on R^4. In Minkowski with m = 0 the vacuum W_0 equals the Hadamard parametrix, so this is a genuine elementary proof of the Hadamard property, not a toy.
- The kernel closed form checks out independently: d^3/du^3 of INT sin(ku) n dk = (pi/2)coth(pi u) - 1/(2u) gives the tree's g. Also g(0) = <:phidot^2:> = rho for one minimally coupled massless scalar, since for m = 0 the gradient term <:(grad phi)^2:> equals <:phidot^2:>.

WEAKNESSES (recorded; none moves the grade):
(1) K2's <x> = <x^3> = 0 is vacuous. X has zero diagonal, so it holds for any diagonal density matrix. Only <x^4> = 3<x^2>^2 discriminates, and it is a single-mode, fourth-order toy. Quasifreeness of the tree's state is true by construction, as the audit itself says.
(2) K6 is a tautology. F = c^2 contains no t, so the identity holds for any t-independent F; my probe F = 7 also passes. The physical point is still correct: the shift automorphism commutes with time translation. But that point is argued, not checked.
(3) K1 checks KMS only at the two-point level, mode by mode. Lifting it to a KMS state rests on the standard result that a quasifree state whose two-point function is KMS is itself KMS. The audit neither names nor reads that result, so 'KMS re-derived exactly' overstates the scope a little.
(4) K5a's claim that '3+1 is load-bearing' is about the infrared behaviour of phi itself. In 1+1 the massless vacuum is also IR-divergent, and the phidot kernel the tree actually uses is finite in 1+1: INT k n dk / pi = pi/6. So 3+1 is load-bearing for the phi state and for the constants, not for the energy-density kernel as such.

None of these touches the claim at noise.py:111-114. The massless 3+1 Planck state with respect to an inertial timelike flow is Gaussian by construction, KMS at the two-point level (checked and discriminating), and Hadamard (checked and discriminating, and also READ at SV Thm 5.1). So STANDS is supported, and the audit's own conditions for changing the grade (NARROWED or OPEN) are correctly stated.

audits.name: Von Neumann entropy of a maximally entangled qubit pair = 1 bit

source.located: C.H. Bennett, H.J. Bernstein, S. Popescu, B. Schumacher, 'Concentrating Partial Entanglement by Local Operations', arXiv:quant-ph/9511030v1 (21 Nov 1995; Phys. Rev. A 53, 2046 (1996)). The definition is at p.4 eq. (4) and the sentence after it. The ebit is defined at p.2, LOCC non-increase is at p.6, and the pure-state-only caveat is at p.16 (sec. V). Cross-read in Horodecki^4, 'Quantum entanglement', arXiv:quant-ph/0702225v2: pp.49, 58 eq.(153), 65-67. The teleportation classic, Bennett et al. PRL 70, 1895 (1993), is NAMED-NOT-READ: only its restatement in quant-ph/9511030 p.2 was read.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on quant-ph/9511030 (all 21 pages verbatim) and on quant-ph/0702225 (pp.1, 20, 49, 58, 60, 65, 66, 67 verbatim)

audits.published_statement: quant-ph/9511030 p.4: 'The entanglement of a partly-entangled pure state can be naturally parameterized by its entropy of entanglement, defined as the von Neumann entropy of either rho_A or rho_B, or equivalently as the Shannon entropy of the squares of the Schmidt coefficients. E = -Tr rho_A log2 rho_A = -Tr rho_B log2 rho_B = -sum_i c_i^2 log2 c_i^2. (4) ... The quantity E ... ranges from zero for a product state (eg theta = 0) to 1 ebit for a maximally entangled pair of two-state particles (eg theta = pi/4).' p.2: 'the consumption of one shared ebit, together with the transmission of a two-bit classical message, can be substituted for the transmission of one qubit.' p.6: 'neither the measurement of k nor any other local processing by one or both parties can increase the expected entropy of entanglement'. p.16: 'entropy of entanglement is a good entanglement measure for pure states ... No similarly simple entanglement measure is known for mixed states.'
published_hypotheses: H1 The bipartite state Psi(A,B) is PURE (eq. (2)). For mixed states, S(rho_A) and S(rho_B) are not the entanglement (p.16, counterexample of classically correlated spins).
H2 The bipartition is fixed, and E is the entropy of either reduced state. The two entropies are equal for pure states by the Schmidt decomposition (eq. (3)).
H3 The logarithm is base 2 and the unit is the ebit (eq. (4), p.2).
H4 'Maximally entangled' means all Schmidt coefficients are equal. For d=2 that gives exactly 1 ebit, and in general log2 d (p.4).
H5 The operational meaning (concentration yield and dilution cost) is asymptotic under LOCC. The value E itself is a closed-form function of a single copy.
H6 Under LOCC the expected E does not increase (p.6). This is a monotone. Conservation holds only asymptotically, for reversible pure-state concentration and dilution (abstract, p.16).
hypothesis_drift: KEPT: transit.py:78-85 (entropy2) computes -sum l log2 l over the eigenvalues of the 2x2 reduced state. At transit.py:315 it is applied to ptrace_first(rho_from(BELL)), where BELL=(|00>+|11>)/sqrt2 is defined at transit.py:90. That state is pure with equal Schmidt weights, so H1-H4 are kept.

NOT STATED AT SITE (purity, H1): transit.py:138 'CHANNEL_BITS_BEFORE = 1.0 # entanglement entropy of a Bell pair' carries no purity qualifier; the hypothesis is named only in the canonical entry. For a mixed channel, S(rho_B)=1 bit for every Werner weight p, including the separable range p<=1/3 (rederive C7). This matters only if R11 (specthm.py:1168; LEDGER.md:177) is applied to a physical, imperfect channel.

ADDED FRAMING (H6 overstated): transit.py:24, 213, 221 and 283 call 'channel entanglement 1 bit before, 0 after' a 'CONSERVATION LAW'. The published law is non-increase of expected entanglement under LOCC (quant-ph/9511030 p.6; quant-ph/0702225 eq.(155)). Across the A|B cut, entanglement goes 1 -> 0, which is not a conservation. Rederive C6 shows the ebit is TRANSFERRED to a reference R, never multiplied, and that is what forces one pair per transit. This is a discrepancy of wording, not a refutation.

SOURCE READ. I read quant-ph/9511030 myself through alphaXiv, all 21 pages. Every quotation the audit relies on matches the text word for word:
- p.4, eq.(4): E = -Tr rho_A log2 rho_A, and "1 ebit for a maximally entangled pair of two-state particles (eg theta = pi/4)", with log2 d in general.
- p.2: one ebit plus a two-bit classical message substitutes for one qubit.
- p.6: no local processing "can increase the expected entropy of entanglement".
- p.16: E is "a good entanglement measure for pure states ... No similarly simple entanglement measure is known for mixed states", with the classically-correlated counterexample.
- The abstract says "asymptotically conserves".

The audit's hypotheses H1-H6 are faithful to that text. I cross-read quant-ph/0702225 p.58 eq.(153) (normalization E((Phi+)^n) = n), eq.(155) (non-increase), pp.65-66 (uniqueness) and p.67 (E_D = E_F = E_C = E_R = S(rho_A) for pure states). All of these confirm the audit.

One small imprecision, which does not move the grade:
- Horodecki lists normalization among "other possible postulates", not required axioms.
- "Unique" there means that the regularization of any measure that is monotone, asymptotically continuous and normalized equals S(rho_A). It does not mean a single-copy identity.

The audit conditions its sentence on "normalized" monotones, so it is not wrong. The Bennett et al. 1993 teleportation paper is correctly marked NAMED-NOT-READ; only its restatement at p.2 of quant-ph/9511030 was read.

THE TREE'S USE. I checked the code directly.
- transit.py:90 defines the exact pure state BELL = (|00>+|11>)/sqrt2.
- transit.py:78-85 (entropy2) is -sum l log2 l over the eigenvalues of the 2x2 reduced state.
- transit.py:315 applies it to ptrace_first(rho_from(BELL)).

So the use sits inside H1-H4: the state is pure, the bipartition is fixed, the log is base 2, and the Schmidt weights are equal. No measured datum enters.

I re-ran the rederivation script: REDERIVE PASS, 14/14. transit.py --selftest gives SELFTEST PASS. The Werner computation (C7) is correct. For rho = p|Phi><Phi| + (1-p)I/4, the partial-transpose eigenvalues are (1+p)/4 three times and (1-3p)/4 once, so the state is separable for p <= 1/3, yet S(rho_B) = 1 for every p. The purity hypothesis therefore does carry weight.

LEDGER.md:177 states that binding conditionally ("transit.py's four results bind it IF it is carried by teleportation as an unknown quantum state"). specthm.py:1168 only reports statuses. - In the tree's favour: across the full Alice-lab|Bob cut, counting a reference R on Alice's side, entanglement is exactly 1 before and 1 after (rederive C6: R-B ends with 1 ebit). The audit already records it only as a discrepancy of wording, "not a refutation", and cites C6's transfer, so it does not over-represent the point either way. The declared constants CHANNEL_BITS_AFTER = 0 and A = I/2 are correctly flagged as declared rather than computed, and both are confirmed by C4 and C5.

WRONG would require a pure, equal-weight two-qubit state whose reduced entropy is not 1. That is excluded symbolically. STANDS holds.

source.located: H. Kodama, 'Conserved energy flux for the spherically symmetric system and the back reaction problem in the black hole evaporation', Prog. Theor. Phys. 63, 1217 (1980). audits.published_statement: Hayward gr-qc/9408002 App. B, pp.19-20: 'Kodama introduced vectors k and j which may be defined, up to orientation, by k = curl r (B1) and g(j) = -T(k) (B2) where the curl refers to the two-dimensional quotient space-time. It follows that g(k,k) = 2E/r - 1 (B3) ... k is spatial in trapped regions and causal otherwise ... Fixing the orientation so that k and j are future-causal for untrapped spheres ... (B4a,b). Thus k is tangent to the constant-r hypersurfaces (B5a) ... 4 pi r^2 j = curl E (B6) ... both k and j are covariantly conserved (B7) ... By Gauss' law, any such conserved current u has a charge ... independent of Sigma (with fixed boundaries) ... Q_j = INT *T(k,v) = INT_0 E' dzeta = E (B8b). The charge Q_j is the definition of energy of Kodama [53].' Abreu-Visser 1004.1456 pp.3-4: k^a = eps_perp^{ab} nabla_b r (24); nabla_a k^a = 0 (30); J^a = G^{ab} k_b with nabla_a J^a = 0 (31), 'a purely geometrical statement ... not related to the Bianchi identities'; J^a = -(2/r^2) eps_perp^{ab} nabla_b m (39). Sec. IX: the fixed-r flux taken without the W factor integrates to the Brown-York energy U = r0(1 - sqrt(1-2m/r0)) (81).
published_hypotheses: Spherical symmetry: a warped product of a (1+1) Lorentzian base with round 2-spheres, areal radius r > 0 (Hayward p.2; Abreu-Visser eq.1; Kinoshita eq.15).
Four spacetime dimensions for the classic statement (Kinoshita generalises to D dimensions).

Conservation of k and of J = G.k is a geometric identity that uses no field equation (Abreu-Visser eq.31; Kinoshita p.6). Reading J as an energy current, with its charge as matter energy, needs G = 8 pi T (Kinoshita p.1; Hayward B2 uses T).
No cosmological constant, for the charge to equal the Misner-Sharp mass of matter (Kinoshita eq.23).

Orientation fixed so that k and j are future-causal on untrapped spheres; k is timelike only where the sphere is untrapped. Normalisation |k|^2 = |1 - 2m/r| (Hayward B3; Abreu-Visser eq.56). The Kodama energy depends on this normalisation.
Hayward's (B8b), as written, integrates from a regular centre. The charge between two spheres is the difference of E by Gauss' law and needs no centre.
Units G = c = 1.

UNCERTAINTY: normal-material values lie within value +- U 'with great certitude'.

audits.published_statement: Barcelo-Visser abstract (p.1): 'We demonstrate that a non-minimally coupled scalar field with a positive curvature coupling xi > 0 can easily violate all the standard energy conditions, up to and including the averaged null energy condition (ANEC).' Sec. 2.2 (p.5), eq. (2.6): 'G_mn k^m k^n = (1/kappa)[T^eff]_mn k^m k^n = [phi'^2 - xi (phi^2)''] / (kappa - xi phi^2) >= 0. This condition is clearly satisfied by minimally coupled scalars. However, for xi != 0 it can be violated in a number of ways: For xi < 0 any local minimum of phi^2 violates the NEC while for xi > 0 and |phi| small, [meaning |phi| < (kappa/xi)^(1/2)], any local maximum of phi^2 violates the NEC. Finally for xi > 0 and |phi| large ... any local minimum of phi^2 violates the NEC.' Also p.5: the NEC 'is the weakest pointwise energy condition, that is, when it is violated the WEC and SEC are violated too.' FFKPS sec. I (p.3): 'delta L = xi R phi^2 allow violations of the NEC even at the classical level'; 'At the classical level, the effective NEC can be violated by non-minimal coupling of either sign ... However, the effective ANEC ... is satisfied' (under their EFT field-range assumption); 'non-minimal coupling can be eliminated by a combined conformal transformation and field redefinition ... to the Einstein frame, where the NEC is obeyed.' FO 0708.2450 p.1: the classical stress-energy tensor 'does not satisfy the weak energy condition (WEC) at non-minimal coupling, i.e., xi != 0'.
published_hypotheses: BV: a classical (unquantised) real scalar field; the analysis is 'completely classical' (p.5)
BV: action (2.1) with -1/2 xi R phi^2 in the matter Lagrangian, mostly-plus signature, kappa = 1/(8 pi G_N), four dimensions
BV: the energy conditions are imposed on the EFFECTIVE stress tensor T^eff (2.3), i.e. on the Einstein tensor of the metric g in (2.1) (Jordan frame). This requires kappa - xi phi^2 != 0
BV: pointwise conditions along an affinely parametrised geodesic. The NEC statement does not depend on V
BV: the statement is EXISTENTIAL: the NEC 'can be violated' at configurations meeting the sign condition, not at every configuration
BV: the NEC can be violated for any xi != 0, of either sign. 'All standard energy conditions up to ANEC' is claimed for xi > 0, and violating ANEC needs |phi| > (kappa/xi)^(1/2)
FFKPS: the violation is of the 'effective NEC' in the Jordan frame; the Einstein-frame metric obeys the NEC
FO 0708.2450: the classical WEC fails for xi != 0 (Birrell-Davies conventions)
hypothesis_drift: SOURCE DROPPED: candidates.py:159-160 cites no source for the classical statement. Its wording is almost verbatim FFKPS 2309.10848 sec. I p.3, a paper the tree cites 21 lines later (candidates.py:180-181). The underlying result is Barcelo-Visser gr-qc/0003025 sec. 2.

MODALITY STRENGTHENED: candidates.py:159-160 says 'violates the NEC and WEC' where FFKPS says 'allow violations' and BV says 'can be violated'. Read literally as true of every configuration it is false: constant phi saturates the NEC rather than violating it, and at a strict extremum of phi^2 one extremum type NEVER violates in each case (rederive C1). The tree's use needs only existence (KIND gate at candidates.py:168; CANDIDATES kind=True at candidates.py:453).

I says the Einstein frame obeys the NEC, and rederive E8 computes this on a backreacted solution. The tree names the Jordan frame elsewhere (candidates.py:406-407) but does not attach it to line 159.

xi != 0 LEFT IMPLICIT at candidates.py:159. This is harmless: the pointwise NEC can be violated for either sign of xi. The FO claim that follows (candidates.py:163) is for xi > 0 only; the classical claim is not so restricted.

At each of 13 zero crossings Hdot = (2xi-1) phidot^2/(2kappa) > 0, so G_kk = -2 Hdot < 0. A boosted observer sees G_vv = -5.86 < 0. E8 (control): along the same solution the Einstein-frame Hubble rate never increases. F: FFKPS eq. (13) as printed has the opposite sign of the R_kk phi^2 term from contracted BV (2.2). audits.lacked_data: The result is a classical identity, BV (2.6), plus the existence of configurations that meet its sign condition. No empirical datum enters it: V drops out (B1), the case analysis is pure algebra (C), and violating witnesses exist both as an on-shell test field at any amplitude (D) and as a backreacted solution (E). What BV lacked in 2000 (the 2012 Higgs discovery, current G, any measured xi) cannot move it. G only moves the field threshold, and the claim holds for every xi != 0. Later work did qualify the result, but with concepts, not data: the Einstein-frame NEC holds (FFKPS; computed in E8), and averaged conditions hold under field-range limits. These limit what the violation buys, not whether it exists. The one discrepancy found, BV's prose swapping maxima and minima, is corrected in FFKPS 2023 and is misprint-class. M's hypothesis therefore finds no missing datum that changes this conclusion.
audits.grade_evidence: The mathematics stands. The stress tensor is conserved (A1), (2.6) re-derives exactly (B), and NEC/WEC violation is exhibited both for an on-shell Minkowski test field (D) and for a backreacted, sub-Planckian FRW solution (E). The grade is NARROWED because candidates.py:159-160 states the result on a larger class than the sources do, in three ways. (i) It says 'violates' where the sources say 'can violate'/'allow violations': constant phi saturates the NEC, and at an extremum of phi^2 one type never violates (C1). (ii) It drops the Jordan-frame/effective-NEC hypothesis; the Einstein-frame NEC holds (FFKPS; computed in E8). (iii) It cites no source. The narrowing does not move the tree's use: the KIND gate (candidates.py:168, :453) needs only the existence of violating configurations, which holds. The grade is not over-represented in M's favour either: BV's prose swap (C3) and FFKPS's sign slips (A2, F2) are recorded as discrepancies, not refutations. It is not WRONG, because D and E are witnesses. The sources were read from cached alphaXiv texts because alphaXiv was over quota.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: candidates.py:159-160 reworded as existential ('can produce NEC/WEC violations'), for the Jordan-frame metric, citing BV gr-qc/0003025 sec. 2.2 or FFKPS 2309.10848. I tried to break the NARROWED grade in both directions and could not.

Source. alphaXiv answered live this time (answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/0003025v2), so I read Barcelo-Visser at source rather than from the auditor's cache. BV (2.1) carries -1/2 xi R phi^2. (2.2), (2.3), (2.5) and (2.6) read as the audit quotes them. The abstract says 'can easily violate'. p.5 says 'can be violated in a number of ways' and that the NEC is the weakest condition, so WEC and SEC fail with it. The analysis is 'completely classical'. The cached FFKPS text says 'allow violations ... even at the classical level' (line 79), 'either sign' (114) and 'Einstein frame, where the [NEC is obeyed]' (120).

Against a downgrade to WRONG. Independent sympy (verify/refute/nmc_check.py) confirms the on-shell Minkowski witness. phi = c + eps(t^2+z^2) has box phi = 0, and BV (2.2) at G = 0 gives T_kk(0) = -8 xi c eps. That is a violation at any amplitude, matching the audit's D. The FRW zero-crossing identity also checks by hand. At phi = 0, (phi^2)'' = 2 phi'^2, so -2 kappa Hdot = (1-2xi) phidot^2 and Hdot = (2xi-1) phidot^2/(2 kappa), which is positive for xi = 1 (E). The auditor's script re-ran at 29 PASS, 0 FAIL.

The max/min swap claim is correct, and it is correctly graded as a discrepancy, not a refutation. At a strict extremum of phi^2 with phi != 0, phi' = 0, and the sign of G_kk is sign(-xi (phi^2)'') / sign(kappa - xi phi^2). That gives:
- xi < 0: violation at a MAXIMUM
- xi > 0, small field: violation at a MINIMUM
- xi > 0, large field: violation at a MAXIMUM

That is the exact reverse of BV's p.5 prose in all three cases. BV's own equation (2.6) and the existence claim are untouched.

Against an upgrade to STANDS. The strongest counter-argument is physics idiom: 'X violates the NEC' conventionally means the theory admits violating configurations. Also, drift (ii), the frame, is weaker than presented. A statement written with 'delta L = xi R phi^2' already fixes the Jordan-frame presentation, since the Einstein frame has no such term. And a dropped citation (iii) is a provenance defect, not a narrowing of the result. Even so, drift (i) survives on its own. The tree drops FFKPS's 'allow' and BV's 'can', and emphasises 'violates ... AT THE CLASSICAL LEVEL' in capitals. Read literally, that is false for constant phi (saturation) and for one extremum type in each case. Under M's rule against over-representation, this counts as a stated class larger than the source's. So NARROWED stands, on (i) chiefly; (ii) and (iii) only reinforce it.

Minor point: the audit counts three narrowing ways. Only (i) is a narrowing in the strict sense; (ii) is largely implicit in the statement and (iii) is provenance. This refines the audit's reasoning and does not change the grade.

Scope of this check: I did not re-read FO 0708.2450 or FFKPS eqs. (7)-(18) at source, and I did not re-check the FFKPS eq. (13) and trace-sign discrepancies (A2, F2) beyond the auditor's own script passing them. None of these bears on the grade.

audits.published_statement: Eq.(21): 'we obtain sigma_piN = (59.1 +- 1.9 +- 3.0) MeV = (59.1 +- 3.5) MeV'. The first error is from the piN amplitude and the second from the low-energy theorem. sigma_piN = sigma(0), with sigma(t) = <N(p')| m-hat (uu + dd) |N(p)> and m-hat = (m_u+m_d)/2. Eq.(24): 'sum_{q=u,...,t} f_q^N = 2/9 + 7/9 (f_u^N + f_d^N + f_s^N) = 0.305 +- 0.009'. Both are quoted READ in sigma-term-scan.json and at massform.py:1344-1357.
published_hypotheses: H1 Cheng-Dashen low-energy theorem D+(0, 2M_pi^2) = sigma(2M_pi^2) + Delta_R, with |Delta_R| <~ 2 MeV from a resonance-exchange estimate (eq.(8)); Delta_D - Delta_sigma = -1.8(2) MeV (eq.(12)).
H2 Isospin-violating corrections (eq.(17)) are applied both to the scattering lengths and to the low-energy theorem. The isospin limit is defined with the CHARGED pion mass and the proton mass.
H3 Pionic-atom scattering lengths a^{1/2} = 169.8(2.0) and a^{3/2} = -86.3(1.8) x 10^-3 M_pi^-1 (eq.(18)); g^2/4pi = 13.7(2); Roy-Steiner equations solved below s_m = (1.38 GeV)^2.

H4 In eq.(24) the heavy-quark contribution (c, b, t) is (2/9)(1 - f_l), i.e. (2/27)(1 - f_l) per heavy quark. The rederivation shows 2/27 = 2/(3 beta0) with n_l = 3, which is leading order in alpha_s and in the heavy-quark limit.
H5 In eq.(24) f_s is a lattice input (Junnarkar-Walker-Loud 2013, per the sibling reading). Inverting 0.305 gives f_s = 0.0435, i.e. sigma_s = 40.8 MeV, with an implied uncertainty of 10.3 MeV.
H6 The f_q^N are scalar COUPLINGS: Higgs- or WIMP-nucleon couplings. The heavy-quark entries are effective couplings obtained through the trace anomaly, not quark-mass contributions to m_N.

NARROWED holds, and reading the source makes the case for it stronger. Several of the audit's sub-claims need correcting, but none of them moves the grade.

1. The source was read directly (alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1506.04142v2, all six pages returned). The quotes the audit took via restatement match the paper:
- eq.(21), p.4: sigma_piN = (59.1 +- 3.5) MeV; the abstract on p.1 gives (59.1 +- 1.9 +- 3.0).
- eq.(24), p.5: 2/9 + 7/9(f_u+f_d+f_s) = 0.305 +- 0.009.
- eq.(12): Delta_D - Delta_sigma = -1.8(2) MeV. eq.(8): |Delta_R| <~ 2 MeV. eq.(18): 169.8(2.0) and -86.3(1.8). g^2/4pi = 13.7(2). s_m = (1.38 GeV)^2.
- The isospin limit uses the proton mass and the charged-pion mass (p.3).
- f_s is taken from ref.[48], Junnarkar and Walker-Loud.
So read_status should be upgraded to READ.

2. Corrections to the audit:
- (a) The item "NOT RE-READ: is N the proton, the neutron or an average" is now settled. The paper says eq.(24) is "averaged over proton and neutron". The tree applies the one number to the average nucleon, which is consistent, so that hypothesis on the tree side goes away.
- (b) The tree's "p.4" citation for eq.(21) is right. The sibling audit's "p.1, eq.(21)" is loose: p.1 carries the value but not the equation label.
- (c) H1 cites the low-energy theorem as eq.(8). The theorem is eq.(7); eq.(8) is the Delta_R bound. This is a label slip.
- (d) The implied f_s is confirmed. JWL eq.(30), READ, gives f_s = 0.043(11), i.e. 40(10) MeV. Eq.(23) plus that f_s reproduces the sum as 0.3046 +- 0.0089. The error on eq.(24) is almost entirely the f_s error.

3. The narrowing. HRKM do not state the order of the 2/9 heavy-quark term anywhere in the paper. It is the leading-order SVZ coefficient, 2/(3 beta0) with n_l = 3. The one higher-order correction I found READ at source is larger than the error HRKM quote:
- Hill-Solon eq.(61), READ, gives f_c = 0.083 - 0.103 lambda at O(alpha_s^3). At HRKM's f_l this is 67.6 MeV, against 62.1 MeV at leading order (a ratio of 1.088). That cuts the pull against RQCD 16's 70(4) MeV from -1.96 to -0.59. So most of the ~2 sigma charm gap the audit flagged is a perturbative-order effect, which is exactly the hypothesis the audit named.
- Charm alone moves the sum by +0.0058 (+0.65 sigma).
- My rough NLO estimate, using Hill-Solon eq.(101) for c and b with assumed alpha_s inputs, gives 0.314 (+1.0 sigma).
- JWL's own eq.(31) O(alpha_s^3) coefficients (0.08896, 0.08578, 0.08964) give 0.343 (+4.2 sigma). Hill-Solon say the reference those coefficients come from disagrees with the correct result beyond leading order, so treat 0.343 as contested and do not quote it as a finding.
- HRKM's quoted +-0.009 does not include this truncation. The audit's later-literature row on these corrections can move from NAMED-NOT-READ to READ.

4. Why not the other grades:
- Not WRONG: the paper states a correct leading-order formula, and its number reproduces from its own inputs. A missing truncation error is a discrepancy, not a refutation.
- Not STANDS: the tree (massform.py:347-353, confirmed by grep) never names the leading order or the charged-pion convention, and the paper does not name the order either.
- Not DATA-DEPENDENT: the largest variant, 0.343, is still below the 0.496 that C2 needs, and the rederive script passes (exit 0) with the tree clean.

5. What is still OPEN: I did not verify the alpha_s inputs to my NLO estimate at source. I have not settled which higher-order heavy-quark coefficient set is right; Hill-Solon and the JWL reference disagree beyond leading order.

audits.published_statement: AS CAPTURED BY THE TREE (massform.py:1111-1115), not re-read here. Tye-Wong eq.(1.2): 'Using the known Higgs vacuum expectation value v = 246 GeV, W Boson mass m_W = 80 GeV and the Higgs Boson mass m_H = 125 GeV, we obtain V(Q) ~ 4.75 TeV (1.31 sin^2(m_W Q) + 0.60 sin^4(m_W Q)), E_sph = max[V(Q)] = V(pi/(2 m_W)) = 9.11 TeV'. Funakubo-Fuyuto-Senaha eq.(10): 'E_sph = g_2 v V(pi/2) ~ 9.08 TeV.' The third value, '9.0 TeV (with U(1))', is held as E_SPH_TEV['Tye-Wong, with U(1)'] = 9.0 (massform.py:1475-1476). The TW-FFS-esph capture gives no locator for it, so where it appears in either source is unverified.
published_hypotheses: H-CLASSICAL: E_sph is the energy of a static classical saddle of the Yang-Mills-Higgs energy functional, with tree-level potential and couplings and no loop correction to the energy. This is implied by the formula E = (4 pi v/g) B / g_2 v V(pi/2); not read at source this session.
H-T0: zero temperature, vacuum vev. Inputs as captured for TW: v = 246, m_W = 80, m_H = 125 GeV.

H-SU2 (theta_W = 0, g' = 0): the tree labels TW's 9.11 'pure SU(2)', and FFS's formula as captured contains only g_2. Computed here: the pure-SU(2) saddle gives 9.111 TeV at TW's printed inputs and 9.079 TeV at 2014-era PDG inputs. Adding U(1) at O(g'^2) gives 9.018 and 8.99 TeV. So 9.08 is the theta_W = 0 value. This is INFERRED BY COMPUTATION, not read.

H-ANSATZ: TW's V(Q) is the energy along a one-parameter path (a Manton-type noncontractible loop). Its maximum, at Q = pi/(2 m_W), is the sphaleron. The sin^2 and sin^4 coefficients are printed to two decimals.
H-FERMIONS-ABSENT: fermions (including the top quark) do not act back on the bosonic saddle. Standard assumption; not read.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED (not named where the value is used): E_SPH_USED = 'Funakubo-Fuyuto-Senaha' (massform.py:1477) and 'At 9.08 TeV the barrier is 3226 times ...' (massform.py:540) both rest on theta_W = 0 (the U(1) hypercharge left out), and neither says so. The dict key for 9.11 says 'pure SU(2)' (massform.py:1475); the key actually used does not. The only marker is the contrast with '9.0 TeV (with U(1))' at massform.py:539-540. Computed at the tree's own inputs (m_W = 80.362, v = 246.2196, m_H = 125.20): the pure-SU(2) value is 9.083 TeV. The O(g'^2) U(1) correction is -0.98 % with on-shell sin^2 theta_W and -1.03 % with MSbar 0.23122, giving 8.99 TeV. With U(1), '3226 times' becomes about 3195-3197 and '3246 Mc^2' becomes about 3214 Mc^2.

DROPPED (not named): H-CLASSICAL and H-T0. The 9.08 is a classical, tree-level energy at zero temperature. massform.py:538-543 puts it under 'OVER THE BARRIER', apart from the thermal regimes, and line 182 says the vev sets the height, so no use at finite temperature was found. But nowhere does the tree name the tree-level status (no radiative correction to E_sph) as a hypothesis. The size of that correction is NOT computed here.

DISCREPANCY in how the tree reads its own divergence note (massform.py:904, 5199-5202). The tree records '4.75 x 1.91 = 9.07, not 9.11', which is correct arithmetic, and explains it as 'the prefactor is rounded: 9.11/1.91 = 4.770'. Computed here at TW's printed inputs: the prefactor 4 pi v/g = 4 pi (246)^2/160 = 4.7529 TeV, which the printed 4.75 rounds correctly, and the saddle's B = 1.9170. So the 0.4 % gap sits in the printed coefficient pair (1.31 + 0.60 = 1.91 against 1.917), not in the prefactor. This is a rounding discrepancy at misprint level in the source's two-decimal coefficients. It is recorded, it is not a refutation, and nothing downstream uses 4.770.

NO DRIFT: the tree states 'E_sph is a barrier HEIGHT, not a rest-mass cost' and 'whether that energy is recovered is not computed' (massform.py:541-543, 2143-2145). The hypothesis 'whether barrier energy is recovered' is therefore named, as the canonical entry records.

rederivation.outcome: This check does not depend on either source. The Klinkhamer-Manton spherically symmetric SU(2) Yang-Mills-Higgs saddle, which is exact for theta_W = 0, was solved as a boundary-value problem (scipy solve_bvp, tol 1e-8, status 0). B is stable to 5 digits under L 60->120, eps 1e-3->1e-4 and n 4000->8000. At TW's printed inputs (v=246, m_W=80, m_H=125): B = 1.9170 and E_sph = 9.111 TeV, matching TW's 9.11. At 2014-era PDG inputs (246.22, 80.385, 125.09): 9.079 TeV, matching FFS's 9.08. At PDG 2024 inputs and at the tree's inputs: 9.082 and 9.083 TeV. The U(1) effect at O(g'^2) was computed as the linear response of the hypercharge field to the sphaleron current K_i = (v^2/2) h^2 (1-f)(-y,x,0)/r^2, derived symbolically in 1612.05431-1505.03690-esph.km_current.py. It is -1.02 % at TW inputs (9.018 TeV) and -0.98 % at current inputs (8.99 TeV), matching '9.0 TeV (with U(1))' to its printed precision. Tree arithmetic: 9.08 TeV/(3 m_p) = 3225.8, so 3226 checks; the tree's own function returns 3245.68, so 3246 Mc^2 checks. SIDE OBSERVATION, belonging to key klinkhamer-manton-1984 and not this one: the same solver gives B(m_H->inf) = 2.706 and B(m_H/m_W=0.02) = 1.531. B rises with m_H, so B(0) <= 1.531. The range as restated in hep-ph/9603208 eq.(2.11) (via the tree) is 1.56-2.72, a gap of 0.6 % at the top and at least 1.9 % at the bottom. Recorded, not a refutation: the restated endpoints come from 1984-era numerics, and nothing in this key uses them. The run at m_H/m_W = 20 hit the mesh limit without converging, so it is excluded and not reported.

audits.lacked_data: Historically the missing datum was the Higgs mass: Klinkhamer-Manton (1984) could only bound B between 1.56 and 2.72 because m_H was unknown. Tye-Wong (2015) and Funakubo-Fuyuto-Senaha (2016) both came after the 2012 discovery and used m_H ~ 125 GeV. Since then m_H has moved from 125.09 to 125.20 GeV, the m_W average has moved from 80.385 to 80.369 (with CDF's contested 80.434), and v is fixed by G_F. Recomputed with each of these, E_sph(SU2) stays between 9.074 and 9.083 TeV, a 0.1 % spread. No datum the authors lacked changes the conclusion, which is evidence against M's hypothesis for THIS result. What does limit the conclusion is hypotheses, not data: (i) the 9.08 the tree uses is the theta_W = 0 value, and including U(1), which the authors had the data for, lowers it by about 1 % to 8.99 TeV; (ii) E_sph is a classical tree-level energy, and radiative corrections to it are not computed here; this is a named open hypothesis (H-CLASSICAL), not a data gap; (iii) a modification of the Higgs potential beyond the Standard Model would move B, but no such datum exists, so there is no evidence either way.
audits.grade_evidence: The numbers themselves hold up. An independent numerical solution of the SU(2) Yang-Mills-Higgs saddle gives 9.111 TeV at Tye-Wong's printed inputs, 9.079 TeV at 2014-era inputs (FFS's 9.08), and 8.99-9.02 TeV with U(1) at O(g'^2) (the tree's 9.0). Current PDG data move E_sph by at most 0.1 %. The tree's derived figures are arithmetically correct: 3226 (3225.8) and 3246 Mc^2 (3245.7). The narrowing: the value the tree USES (E_SPH_USED = FFS 9.08, massform.py:1477 and 540) is the pure-SU(2) saddle and holds only for theta_W = 0, and that hypothesis is not named on the used value; only the 9.11 key says 'pure SU(2)'. In the Standard Model, with g' != 0, the O(g'^2) value is 8.99 TeV, so '3226 times' becomes about 3195-3197 and '3246 Mc^2' about 3214 Mc^2. This does not change S11 ('E_sph ~ 9 TeV') or SR5 at their stated order of magnitude. The classical, tree-level, zero-temperature status (H-CLASSICAL, H-T0) is also not named, and the size of the radiative correction is not computed here. CAVEAT, not flattened: neither source could be read at source this session (alphaXiv quota and egress block). The verbatim wording and page locators rest on the tree's own capture (massform.py:1109-1115). The grade rests on the computation, which does not depend on the sources.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names theta_W = 0 (U(1) left out) on E_SPH_USED and on the 3226 and 3246 sentences, or switches to the with-U(1) value. To OPEN for the attribution: a read of 1505.03690 or 1612.05431 at source showing printed values, inputs or gauge content that differ from the tree's capture, for example FFS's 9.08 including U(1) at different inputs. The computation here makes that unlikely, since with U(1) at FFS-era inputs the value is 8.99. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a computed radiative correction to the classical sphaleron energy larger than about 1 %, or a confirmed shift in m_W or m_H of order 1 % (none exists). WRONG would need a demonstrated saddle lower than the claimed values by more than rounding, and the independent solve rules that out at these inputs.

verifiers.reason:
The NARROWED grade survives. Reading both sources makes it stronger rather than weaker. The audit also needs several status corrections: much of what it marked NAMED-NOT-READ or INFERRED is now READ.

(1) Tye-Wong's eq.(1.2) on arXiv p.3 matches the tree's capture at massform.py:1111-1115 word for word: v=246, m_W=80, m_H=125, V(Q) ~ 4.75 TeV (1.31 sin^2 + 0.60 sin^4), E_sph = 9.11 TeV, m = 17.1 TeV. Funakubo-Fuyuto-Senaha's eq.(10) on p.2 matches too: 'E_sph = g_2 v V(pi/2) ~ 9.08 TeV'. Both page locators are correct. The source read_status should be READ, not NAMED-NOT-READ.

(2) H-SU2 is READ at source in both papers, not just inferred by computation. TW p.5 says: 'we ignore the U(1) gauge field (i.e., set Weinberg angle theta_W = 0)'. FFS p.1 says: 'Since the effect of a U(1)_Y contribution on the sphaleron energy is a few %, we neglect it.' So the 9.08 the tree uses is the theta_W = 0 value by the source's own statement. The drift the audit found is real: E_SPH_USED at massform.py:1477 and 'At 9.08 TeV the barrier is 3226 times' at massform.py:540 do not name theta_W = 0, while the 9.11 key does say 'pure SU(2)'.

(3) The audit said the '9.0 TeV (with U(1))' value had no locator. It does: TW p.4 says 'turning on the U(1) coupling (sin^2 theta_W = 0.23) will lower the sphaleron energy by about a percent. So it is reasonable to use E_sph = 9.0 TeV in phenomenological studies', citing Manton, Klinkhamer-Laterveer (Z.Phys. C53, 1992) and Kunz-Kleihaus-Brihaye. It is repeated on pp.26 and 28. It is a rounded phenomenological estimate built on a cited ~1 % shift, not a saddle solved at finite theta_W. The tree's 'READ value' label is accurate as a quotation. It does not say the value is an estimate, but that is minor.

(4) The two sources differ slightly. TW puts the U(1) effect at 'about a percent' and FFS at 'a few %'. The auditor's own O(g'^2) computation gives -0.98 to -1.03 %, which agrees with TW. This is recorded as a difference between the sources, not a refutation of either.

(5) FFS independently corroborates the auditor's reading of the tree's divergence note (massform.py:904, 5199-5202). FFS prints the same coefficients to three decimals: beta_1 = 1.313, beta_2 = 0.603, summing to 1.916. That matches the auditor's solved B of 1.9161-1.9170. And 4 pi v^2/(2 m_W) = 4.7529 TeV at TW's inputs, which 4.75 rounds correctly. So the 9.07-versus-9.11 gap comes from TW rounding its coefficients to two decimals. The tree's explanation, 'the prefactor is rounded: 9.11/1.91 = 4.770', points at the wrong factor. This is a misreading at rounding level, recorded and not a refutation, and nothing downstream uses 4.770.

(6) The limitations are partly named in the sources themselves. TW p.29 says E_sph 'will be shifted if there are 2 Higgs doublets, or via quantum corrections or modified Higgs potential, topics not discussed'. FFS p.4 says 'we have not taken thermal corrections into account'. So H-CLASSICAL and the non-SM-potential hypothesis are READ as open in the sources. That fits the audit's finding that the tree drops them, and it does not change the grade.

(7) The numbers were recomputed from the auditor's output. The tree's 3226 (3225.8) and 3246 Mc^2 (3245.7) are correct. At the tree's inputs the SU(2) value is 9.083 TeV, and 8.99 TeV with U(1). Current data move E_sph by no more than 0.1 %.

Why this is NARROWED and not STANDS. The tree does print '9.0 TeV (with U(1))' in the same sentence as the 9.08. But its derived figure '3226 times' is quoted to four significant figures on the theta_W = 0 value without naming that hypothesis, and both sources say explicitly that the physical value is lower. Why it is not WRONG or DATA-DEPENDENT: the external values reproduce to within rounding, and no moved datum shifts them by more than 0.1 %. I re-ran the audit's script from a copy in verify/rederive/. It reproduces every printed figure in about 20 s: B = 1.9170 and 9.111 TeV at Tye-Wong's inputs; 9.079 TeV at 2014-era inputs; 9.082 TeV at PDG-2024 inputs; 9.083 TeV at the tree's inputs; 9.074 TeV at CDF's m_W. With U(1) at O(g'^2) the shift is -1.02 % at TW's inputs and -0.98 % at current inputs (9.018 and 8.993/8.990 TeV). The tree's own arithmetic gives 3225.8, so 3226 checks, and massform returns 3245.68, so 3246 Mc^2 checks.

ENCODING: the script solves the real problem, not a toy. I re-derived its ODEs from the Klinkhamer-Manton reduced energy and they are the correct Euler-Lagrange equations. The Higgs mass is entered correctly (lam/g^2 = m_H^2/(8 m_W^2)) and the prefactor is right (4 pi v/g). The spherically symmetric ansatz is exact by symmetry when theta_W = 0. A sympy check in v_norm.py gives sum|d_i U chi|^2 = 2/r^2, which produces the functional's h^2(1-f)^2 term at the same normalisation (A = -(i/g) f dU U^-1, D = d - igA) used for the hypercharge current. It also confirms Im(chi^dag U^dag d_i U chi) = (-y,x,0)/r^2 and div K = 0, so the Coulomb-gauge Green's-function solution is valid. The O(g'^2) formula dE = -(g'^2/2) double-integral K.K/(4 pi |x-y|) follows from minimising the energy quadratic in the hypercharge field B. The B^2|Phi|^2 term and the back-reaction of the SU(2) fields enter only at O(g'^4), the latter because the solution is stationary.

INDEPENDENT CHECK, no ODE solver: v_newton.py discretises the reduced energy on a compactified grid and minimises it by damped Newton with a sparse Hessian. Grid sizes N = 1000/2000/4000 with Richardson extrapolation give B = 1.91701 (TW), 1.91606 (2014-era) and 1.91631 (PDG-2024). These match solve_bvp to 5 digits, with residual |grad| about 1e-12. The lowest Hessian eigenvalue is positive, so the solution is the minimum of the reduced functional. A second route to the U(1) shift, a spherical-Bessel transform, matches the audit's Green's-function value to 4 digits (-1.0220 % and -0.9814 %). The two routes share the formula, so this checks the numerics, not the physics.

(1) PDG 2024 summary table (pdg.lbl.gov):

TW p.4 reads: "turning on the U(1) coupling (i.e., Weinberg angle sin^2 theta_W = 0.23) will lower the sphaleron energy by about a percent. So it is reasonable to use E_sph = 9.0 TeV". The audit's computed O(g'^2) shift of -0.98 to -1.03 % agrees with TW's "about a percent". FFS's "a few %" is looser than both. The audit's two re-derived extremes are confirmed at source. read_status should move from NAMED-NOT-READ to READ.

(2) The audit misread what the family in eq. (22) is. ϑ is the BULK launch angle of a one-hop signal, x = t cos ϑ, z = t sin ϑ (eq. 21). v is the speed along the boost axis x'' only. That puts Proxima on +boost and GW170817's propagation on −boost, whatever the word 'extremised' means.

SOURCE, NOW READ: the audit's premise that the source was unreadable no longer holds. alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries worked for me on 2208.09014v3, and it returned the full text of pp.1-17. Eq. (22), p.8, verbatim in content: v = Δx''/Δt'' = (γ cos ϑ − B)/(1 − Bγ cos ϑ), 'which is extremized at cos ϑ = ±1'. Here ϑ is the launch angle of a BULK ray in the x–z plane (x = t cos ϑ, z = t sin ϑ, eq. 21). It is not a direction on the brane. GKLP eqs. (23)-(24) show that eq. 22 at cos ϑ = 1 equals eq. 20, v = γ(1+Γ²B²β²)/(1−Γ²Bγβ²). Eq. 22 at cos ϑ = −1 equals eq. 25, w = −γ(1+Γ²B²β²)/(1+Γ²Bγβ²). I confirmed both identities in sympy (indep.py). There is no symbol 'g' in eq. 22, so reading the tree's 'g -> 1' as γ -> 1 is consistent.

ENCODING: the script checks the extremes exactly (check B), and those are what the tree uses. So for the tree's use, the encoding is the theorem and not a toy. The audit's published_statement is partly wrong, though. Eq. 22's interior is a family over bulk launch angles, not 'late-time front velocities' over brane directions. The audit's own condition for moving to OPEN ('a reading at source showing that its family is not the direction-on-the-brane family') is therefore met literally. It does not move the grade: the interior is never used, and the extremes are the published eqs. 20/25, re-derived exactly.

Two drift items need correcting. (1) 'Extremised' at branelink.py:81/:278 is GKLP's own word: it means extremising over ϑ, which yields eqs. 20/25. It is not an extremisation over sky geometry. The antipodal assumption is still made, but only implicitly: the tree pairs eq. 20 (forward, toward Proxima) with eq. 25 (backward, GW170817) on one boost axis. Its substance stands. (2) The 'NOT CHECKABLE HERE' item is now settled as above.

The off-axis front behind check F, τ(c) from γ²Γ²(τ+Bc)² = Γ²(c+Bτ)² + 1 − c², is the script's own first-principles extension. It is not GKLP's. It is consistent with GKLP's eq. 8: the identification has zero brane component in the preferred frame, and the front is t' = r'/γ (verified in check A). Polychronakos's 3-D result was not read to confirm it.

VACUITY: one check is vacuous. Check A's isotropy line is a hard-coded chk(..., True), although the fact itself is READ at GKLP eq. (8). The rest discriminate. A perturbed eq. 20 (denominator sign flipped) fails the match. At β=0 the front speed is 1. Most important, a rebuilt check F (vacF.py) with the propagation directions set antipodal (χ=180) returns B(1 s) = 0.9993876305, which is the tree's figure, and the 'real > tree' check is False. With χ = 138.46146 it returns 0.9994645711. So F really does discriminate the geometry.

INDEPENDENT ARITHMETIC: I solved GKLP eqs. 20/25 in closed form, without the script's root-finding (indep.py). It gives B(1 s) = 0.999387630477388 and B(T/2) = 0.999999935192595. At the tree's 0.999999925167 the saving fraction is 0.4, which is exact in the limit: e² = 8d gives δ/e = 1/4, so τ = 0.75/1.25 = 0.6. This confirms the tree's T/2 figure is an 8th-decimal discrepancy in its own linearisation. It is not a fault of GKLP.

Grade: NARROWED stands. GKLP's extremes STAND, now READ at source, and the 1 s figure is correct under the tree's hypotheses. The tree states the antipodal floor as sufficient: on the real sky the price is 0.9994645711. It also misstates T/2. verifiers.reason:
The alphaXiv quota had recovered, so this time all three sources were READ at source.

GKLP 2208.09014v3, eq. (22), p.8, verbatim: v = Δx''/Δt'' = (γ cos ϑ − B)/(1 − Bγ cos ϑ), 'which is extremized at cos ϑ = ±1'. At cos ϑ = 1 it equals eq. (20), shown by their eqs. 23-24. Sympy here gives eq.22(cos=-1) − eq.25 = 0 identically.

GKLM 2206.13590v2, eq. (39), p.12, quotes GW170817: −3e-15 ≤ Δc/c ≤ +7e-16. The hedge sentence matches branelink.py's quote: 'If we entertain the possibility that these are bulk degrees of freedom'.

Abbott et al. 1710.05834 (ApJL 848 L13), sec. 4.1, eq. (1): the same band, from Δt = 1.74 ± 0.05 s over D = 26 Mpc. That distance is 'the lower bound of the 90% credible interval'. The upper bound assumes simultaneous emission.

DATA ROWS. All three were recomputed independently in verify/data/gklp-eq22-data.py, at 40 digits.
(1) d: 1.74 s·c/26 Mpc = 6.502e-16, which rounds up to 7e-16, as the audit says. At 1.74 + 0.05 s it is 6.69e-16, still ≤ 7e-16. One literature search (discover_papers, recency) found no second GW+EM lag. 2307.13099 measures v_g from inter-detector delays, far weaker. So 'unchanged' holds, with the audit's own caveat that the search was not exhaustive. The counterfactual reproduces: 40 Mpc gives d = 4.2263e-16 and B(1 s) = 0.999524146. Abbott's GW-only distance is 40 (+8/−14) Mpc. So 'moves: No (4th decimal)' follows.
(2) Proxima: parallax 768.0665 mas gives 4.24646 ly, and 4.2465 ly × 31557600 s = 134009348.4 s, both as stated. The parallax itself was taken from a snippet, not read at a Gaia source, here or by the audit.
(3) Sky: AT2017gfo is at 13h09m48.085s, −23°22'53.343" (Coulter, as cited in Abbott). Against Proxima J2000 the separation is 41.53854°, so the propagation directions are 138.46146° apart; (1+cos sep)/2 = 0.874255.
I then checked the real-sky price independently, by a different method from the audit's check F. I solved the exact boosted cone Γ²(uc+B)² + u²s² = γ²Γ²(1+Buc)², which is GKLP eq. 9 applied to the isotropic preferred-frame front, with γ fixed by u(GW direction) = 1+d and the in-plane boost direction optimised (verify/data/gklp-eq22-sky.py). At 180° it gives B(1 s) = 0.999387630477, the tree's figure. At 138.46° it gives 0.999464571099, with the boost 41.53° off the Proxima line. That matches the audit's 0.9994645711 to 10 digits. So row 3's 'Yes in quantity, not in kind' follows.

LACKED_DATA is answered with evidence, not presumed. Eqs. 21-22 are pure kinematics and use no datum (READ). The companion GKLM already prints the GW170817 bound (READ). So the authors did not lack the one datum the tree feeds in, and M's hypothesis gets no support for this result. The extremes re-derive exactly.

CORRECTIONS THE AUDIT NEEDS. None of them overturns the grade.
(a) read_status should move from NAMED-NOT-READ to READ (2208.09014v3 p.8). published_statement can now quote eq. (22) verbatim.
(b) The two OPEN residuals close.
- There is no symbol g in eq. (22). The tree's 'g -> 1' is most plausibly ASCII for γ → 1, which is the linearisation the audit already flags.
- 'Extremised' is over ϑ, the BULK emission angle of the trajectory x = t cos ϑ, z = t sin ϑ. It is not a direction on the brane. The family gives speeds along the boost axis x'' only, and its extremes are the ±x'' fronts.
(c) The audit's 'To OPEN' trigger ('family is not the direction-on-the-brane family') is therefore met literally, but it should not fire. The tree uses only the two extremes, and those are confirmed. The real-sky narrowing never used eq. 22's interior: it is an extension beyond GKLP, re-derived here from the boosted cone. The reading actually strengthens drift item 1. GKLP gives front speeds only along ±x'', so putting GW170817 'backward' and Proxima 'forward' in GKLP's extremised formula presumes the two directions are antipodal on one axis, and on the real sky they are not.

GRADE. NARROWED stands on the data. No datum has moved. GKLP's formula STANDS at source. The tree's '0.999387630 buys one second' is a necessary floor stated as sufficient: the real-sky price is 0.9994645711 with a fixed boost direction. The T/2 figure 0.99999993 is an arithmetic discrepancy inside the tree, as the audit reports. It was not re-checked here because it lies outside this lens.

audits.published_statement: pulsed_ignition sect. 1.1: 'charges ten 100 nF energy storage capacitors ... in parallel through 1 MOhm ... up to +50 kV DC'. Component table: 'Storage Capacitors 10x 100 nF / 60 kV'. Output: 'V_out = 10 x 50 kV = 500 kV at 10 kA', '~12 ns', 'Charging Supply +50 kV, 20 kW'. Header: 'PEAK POWER: 10 Petawatts'. Sect. 2.1: 'femtosecond pulses (30 fs duration)', 'spot diameter of 0.1 mm ... intensities exceeding 10^20 W/cm^2'. Power flow: 'The 500 kV output pulse drives an array of eight CPA laser heads'. Chronology: 'Optical Intensity Spikes to Planck Threshold'. Blueprints: 'Flywheel Rotor Diameter: 1.8 meters Carbon-Fiber Wrapped Beryllium-Copper', '[C/E] Dual Rotors ... 85,000 RPM Counter-Rotating', '20 Tesla' stator 2.1 m, shell 2.5 m. Cost doc: 'Operating a 1.8-meter flywheel at 85,000 RPM', 'rotational kinetic energy storage (85,000 RPM rotor)', '25-30 ft vertical ceiling', '1.5-3 MW utility feed'. transient_metric table: 100 kg ~1.48e-25 m, 8.98e18 J; 5,000 kg ~7.42e-24 m, 4.49e20 J; 100,000 kg ~1.48e-22 m, 8.98e22 J. Sect. 4.1: 'relativistic surface velocities', 'muon-catalyzed fusion (muCF) starter cell'.
published_hypotheses: These are design specifications, not measurements: no figure carries an uncertainty, a test or a data source.
50 kV is printed as a ceiling ('up to'), and the capacitors are rated to 60 kV.
1e20 W/cm^2 is printed as a floor ('exceeding'), and the same document prints a 10 PW peak power.
30 fs is the seed oscillator's pulse duration; no amplified duration is printed separately.
The power flow puts the laser heads downstream of the Marx pulse.
The table's r_s = 2GM/c^2 and E = Mc^2 are stated as exact, and its entries carry '~'.
The folder itself calls the rotor 'rotational kinetic energy storage', but prints no rotor mass or thickness.
hypothesis_drift: ADDED, warpfolder.py:40-44 and ledger.py:1632-1634 (S9): the tree treats Marx + laser as the device's whole energy store. The folder also prints a rotor it calls kinetic-energy storage, a 20 T stator, a 3 MW feed and a muCF starter cell, and none of them is counted. Bounding the rotor by the printed tip speed and the printed 30 ft ceiling gives 3.08e12 J (solid Be-Cu disc) or 1.69e13 J (osmium thin rim). The device-wide shortfall at 100 kg is then at least 5.7 to 6.5 orders, not 15.8; a 1 m-thick Be-Cu disc gives 7.43 orders. The 15.8 orders is the pulsed-ignition subsystem's shortfall.

ADDED, warpfolder.py:287-288: the laser is summed with the Marx bank even though the laser is downstream of it. This double-counts in the document's favour: Marx alone gives 15.857 orders against the tree's 15.782.

READING, warpfolder.py:214-215: 'up to +50 kV' and 'exceeding 1e20' are taken at face value. The document's own ceilings (60 kV rating, 10 PW peak) give 1800 + 300 = 2100 J, or 15.63 orders. 10 PW over the 0.1 mm spot is 1.27e20 W/cm^2, so 'exceeding' is bounded by the document's own figure. R_charge*C = 0.1 s makes 50 kV at 109 ms a ceiling rather than a certainty.

ADDED, warpfolder.py:25 and :526-531: the document's 'Optical Intensity Spikes to Planck Threshold' is read as the Planck energy. The document says intensity. Against the Planck intensity (1.39e118 W/cm^2) the shortfall is 98 orders, and even the Schwinger limit (2.3e29 W/cm^2) is not reached. False holds under both readings, and the tree's reading is the more generous one.

STRONGER THAN CITED, warpfolder.py:218-219: the pairing of 1.8 m with 85,000 RPM is READ outright in cost_and_location. For the counter-rotating pair the relative speed is 5.3e-5 c (gamma-1 = 1.4e-9), still not relativistic.

MODEL, warpfolder.py:326-328: burst speed sqrt(sigma/rho) is the thin-rim limit. For a solid isotropic disc (nu = 0.3) the limit is about 1.56x higher and the over-limit factors fall from 4.25x/19.45x to 2.73x/12.49x. The rotor is still over its limit. sigma and rho carry status ORDER and do not come from the folder (warpfolder.py:224-227).

CONFIRMED, NOT DRIFT, warpfolder.py:232-236 and 504-516: the third-row E is 8.98e22 against Mc^2 = 8.98755e21, a ratio of 9.9916. The mantissa is the exact 3-s.f. truncation of the true value, so this is an exponent slip, and it is correctly recorded as an internal inconsistency. Every table figure is truncated, not rounded, to 3 s.f.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis has little to act on here. The authors are a 2026 assistant session writing design specifications, and the parameters are inputs they chose, not measurements made on incomplete data. The one external datum they used, G, has not moved (CODATA 2018 = 2022), and the table matches it to 3-s.f. truncation. What changes the picture is data the tree left out, not data the authors lacked: the folder's own rotor ('rotational kinetic energy storage'), 20 T stator, 3 MW feed and muCF cell. Counting them lowers the 100 kg shortfall from 15.8 orders to a floor of 5.7-6.5 orders, set by the printed dimensions. The muCF cell has no printed size; filling the whole rotor with solid DT and burning all of it (1.96e18 J) still leaves the budget 0.66 orders short. So the sign of 'short on its own numbers' survives, and the evidence does not overturn the tree's conclusion; only its stated magnitude is a subsystem figure. The evidence against M's hypothesis here: every printed number is transcribed exactly, and the single misprint was already classified correctly.
audits.grade_evidence: The printed parameters STAND as READ: every constant at warpfolder.py:212-220 and 235 matches the Drive text of 2026-09-26, and the x10 third-row cell is confirmed as an exponent slip, handled as a discrepancy rather than a refutation. The tree's use of them is narrower than stated. 'The device stores 1,486 J ... short by 15.8 orders' (warpfolder.py:22-23, 40-44) and S9's 'its own printed hardware stores 1486 J' (ledger.py:1632) hold only for the pulsed-ignition subsystem. That rests on an added hypothesis, because the folder names its 85,000 RPM rotor as kinetic-energy storage; bounding the rotor by printed dimensions gives >= 5.7 orders device-wide (computed, D3a). Two further scope points: the rotor over-limit factors 4.2x/19.4x are thin-rim values (2.7x/12.5x for a solid disc, still over), and the Planck-threshold test reads energy where the document says intensity (it fails either way). No boolean reverses: ENERGY_BUDGET_IS_CONNECTED, REACHES_PLANCK_THRESHOLD, ROTOR_IS_RELATIVISTIC, ROTOR_IS_WITHIN_MATERIAL_LIMITS and TABLE_1E5_ROW_IS_CONSISTENT all stay False. What narrows is the stated magnitude, and the scope of 'device'.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS if the tree scopes 1486 J / 15.8 orders to the ignition subsystem, or adds the rotor, stator and feed stores with the bound computed here, and labels 4.2x/19.4x as the thin-rim model. The budget's sign would move toward OPEN only if a folder document printed a rotor mass or muCF fuel load approaching 9e18 J; none of the eight does. WRONG would need a mis-transcribed printed figure, and there is none.

I could not refute the grade in either direction. Two of my four arguments clip details of the narrowing, the third is a stale citation, and the fourth is a small inconsistency.

Source read. On 2026-10-02 I read all four parameter documents myself through the Google Drive connector (read_file_content): pulsed_ignition 1TrZc7CB..., schematics_and_blueprints 1bugkRaE..., cost_and_location 1iRdiHDc..., transient_metric 1zv_kkVd.... These are 2026 Drive documents, not arXiv papers, so alphaXiv does not apply. Every figure the audit quotes is in the text verbatim:
- Marx bank: ten 100 nF capacitors, 1 MOhm, 'up to +50 kV DC', '10x 100 nF / 60 kV', '+50 kV, 20 kW', '~12 ns', 500 kV at 10 kA.
- Laser and focus: 'PEAK POWER: 10 Petawatts', '30 fs' (a seed-oscillator figure only), 0.1 mm spot, 'exceeding 10^20 W/cm^2'.
- Power flow: 'The 500 kV output pulse drives an array of eight CPA laser heads'.
- Chronology: 'Optical Intensity Spikes to Planck Threshold'.
- Blueprints: rotor 1.8 m 'Carbon-Fiber Wrapped Beryllium-Copper', '[C/E] Dual Rotors Relativistic Field Shearing 85,000 RPM Counter-Rotating', stator 2.1 m at 20 T, shell 2.5 m.
- Cost and location: 'Operating a 1.8-meter flywheel at 85,000 RPM', 'rotational kinetic energy storage (85,000 RPM rotor)', 25-30 ft ceiling, 1.5-3 MW feed.
- Payload table: as quoted, including the 8.98e22 cell.
- Sect. 4.1: muCF starter cell, and 'relativistic surface velocities'.

The constants at warpfolder.py:212-220 and 235 are therefore transcribed exactly, so a WRONG grade has no footing. The x9.9916 third-row cell is an exponent slip, and the tree already records it as a discrepancy.

Why STANDS fails. transient_metric 4.1 places the counter-rotating rotor inside the energy chain: its shear 'focus[es] the magnetic stress tensor ... triggering the initial micro-singularity collapse'. The cost document also names the rotor as kinetic-energy storage. So 'the device stores 1,486 J' (warpfolder.py:22-23) and S9's 'its own printed hardware stores %.0f J' (now ledger.py:1689-1690, not :1632) leave out a store the folder itself declares. My recomputation (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Method-Works/6d820e7d-6d3c-5ac7-8067-527dc14c2847/scratchpad/d67/verify/refute/wfpp_check.py) matches the audit:
- tip speed 8011.06 m/s;
- Be-Cu disc filling the 30 ft height: 3.08e12 J, 6.47 orders short;
- osmium rim: 1.69e13 J, 5.73 orders short;
- 1 m Be-Cu disc: 7.43 orders;
- 20 T field over the shell volume: 7.14e9 J;
- Marx 1250 J, laser 235.62 J, 10 PW on the spot = 1.27e20 W/cm^2;
