The rederive script also passes all 55 assertions. No boolean reverses, and S9 is refused on a second, independent count as well (the inverted reconstruction mechanism). The narrowing is of magnitude and of what 'device' covers, which is NARROWED and not WRONG.

Points against the audit, none of which moves the grade:
(1) The 5.7-6.5 order floor uses the most generous reading. The document's own chronology says the rotor reaches 85,000 RPM at T+100 ms, and the 3 MW feed it lists does not power a rotor drive. On that reading the rotor holds at most 3e5 J and the shortfall is about 13.5 orders. The folder is inconsistent with itself, so the device-wide magnitude depends on which reading you take. Under every reading, though, it is less than 15.8 orders, so the narrowing holds.
(2) The MODEL drift applies the solid isotropic-disc correction to T1000 as well as Be-Cu. That is wrong for the printed construction: the carbon fibre is a wrap at the outer radius, which is a thin rim. Its hoop stress is rho*v^2 = 18.0x its strength, or 4.25x in speed, so the tree's 4.2x is the right model for the wrap. The solid-disc correction holds only for the Be-Cu core (19.4x to 12.5x). The 'label 4.2x/19.4x as thin-rim' condition in what_would_change_the_grade is therefore overstated for the T1000 figure.
(3) The audit cites ledger.py:1632-1634 for S9. In the current file S9 is at :1686-1706.
(4) The audit argues the laser is downstream of the Marx bank and so not additive, then sums the two ceilings (1800 + 300 = 2100 J) anyway. This is harmless, because it only errs in the document's favour.

I re-ran the script and it reproduces the audit's result. Run from the original location, all checks pass (T1-T8, G-T, C1-C3, G-C, K1-K5, G-K) and it exits 0. The source text matches its recorded md5 (8f3ba9f58345e3a4f72902e8369df2f4). I also searched the saved page text directly. p.11 prints 'Recently we argued ... smallest local radius of curvature and/or the distance to any boundaries in the spacetime [23]. An explicit example of the validity of this assumption ...'. p.2 prints 'we recently argued [23] that if one is willing to restrict the choice of sampling time ...' and 'we proved that the inequality Eq. (1) holds in the case of the Casimir effect ...'. Eq.(48) is printed as -3/(16 pi^2 t0^4) 'for all t0'. The Kontou-Olum Eq.(130) and its intro sentence ('none of these results have been explicitly proven'), the Fewster-Smith 'heuristic appeals to the equivalence principle ... lacks full mathematical justification', and the Kontou-Sanders 'first QEIs with explicitly curvature dependent bounds' all occur verbatim in the saved caches.

ENCODING. The result is a qualitative extrapolation, so no theorem can be encoded. The finite checks that are possible were done. T is real string matching against the saved v2 text; it was not re-read at source, so provenance rests on the md5 and the transcript. C1/C2 and C3 are exact closed-form Casimir cases: a constant density checked against the flat QIs Eq.(48) and Eq.(1). The audit picks the EM plates, whose density is constant and gauge-invariant. That is the right choice, because a minimally coupled Dirichlet scalar's density varies with position. K1 reproduces K-O's printed 3.76 exactly, as 3 sqrt(pi/2) = 3.7599. This is a genuine discriminating check: with the other Gaussian convention, exp(-t^2/2t0^2), the constant is 3 sqrt(pi)/4 = 1.329.

VACUITY (my script verify/rederive/vacuity_9607003.py). Each check fails when its hypothesis is negated:
- V1: T5 fails if the tree's quotation keeps the boundary clause.
- V2: T1 fails on a p.11 with the clause stripped out.
- V3: the Lorentzian sampler is normalised (integral = 1), so the constant-density premise of C1 holds exactly.
- V6: once the clause is satisfied (t0 = 0.1a) the flat EM QI holds, so the C check can go either way.

MINOR DISCREPANCIES. None changes the grade, and none is a refutation.
(1) Missing source gives a false ALL PASS. SRC is a relative path (HERE/../src). Run from any copy, the script prints 'SKIP T*' and still reports ALL PASS with exit 0, so a missing source passes silently. The audit's reverify_command runs from the original location, where this does not arise.
(2) K4 uses a looser bound than it needs. It takes R_max >= G_00/3. Since G_00 = R_00/2 + sum R_ii/2 in an orthonormal frame, sup |G_00|/R_max = 2 (V5), so the tighter bound is G_00/2. The ratio at t0 = b is then >= 1312, not >= 874. The audit's figure is a valid but conservative lower bound, and the conclusion is unchanged.
(3) The noise.py quotation is not the same as achievable.py's. noise.py:186-187 quotes 'sampling time ... much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature' with an internal ellipsis. The quotation ends mid-sentence with no period and no 'we recently argued'. It does drop the boundary clause, but it is not 'the same quote' as achievable.py:226-230, which closes with a period.
(4) The boundary clause does not bear on the tree's verdict. C1/C2 show the clause is load-bearing for the SOURCE's claim. The corridor's issue is curvature, not boundaries, so dropping the clause is a quotation-fidelity discrepancy, not a weakening of the tree's verdict. The audit says as much ('What rests on it survives').
(5) C3 is arguably a literal counterexample. A flat periodic identification has neither curvature nor a boundary, yet the flat QI fails there for t0 > 0.5425 L. Read literally, without an implied global-topology hypothesis, the remark is contradicted. Grading C3 as incompleteness rather than WRONG is reasonable for a qualitative 'argued' remark, but it is the strongest point in M's favour.

GRADE. NARROWED is supported on two grounds. On the source side, Kontou-Olum prove the extrapolation only in a narrower class (geodesic, compact-support sampler, bounded Ricci derivatives, renormalisation constants a and b), and C3 exposes a topology scale that neither clause names. On the tree's side, the boundary clause is dropped and the word order altered. Not WRONG: there is no counterexample within the proved class, and K-O confirm the flat leading term. Not OPEN: the passage was read and checked here.

There is one data_at_publication row, and it says the result is a qualitative scope extrapolation with no measured input (value_then/value_now n/a, moves_conclusion: no). I read gr-qc/9607003 p.1-3 and pp.10-11 in the saved alphaXiv page text, and its md5 matches the entry (8f3ba9f5...). The p.11 sentence ('Recently we argued that such bounds should also hold ... [23]') contains no number at all. The QI it extends, Eq.(48) -3/(16 pi^2 t0^4) 'for all t0', is derived in closed form. The numbers the audit does use are all theory, and I recomputed them independently. The EM plate threshold t0 <= (135/pi^4)^(1/4) a = 1.085010 a. The periodic-scalar cap is 0.542505 L. For the Gaussian sampler, INT (g'')^2 = 3 sqrt(pi/2)/t0^3 = 3.75994, which matches Kontou-Olum Eq.(130)'s printed leading 3.76 (line 4128 of the saved 1410.0665 text). M's hypothesis is answered with evidence, not assumed. On whether data was missing, the source has no measured input to be wrong, and that is what lacked_data says. Fewster-Smith 0702056 (line 7156): 'heuristic appeals to the equivalence principle ... lacks full mathematical justification'. K-O intro (line 46): 'none of these results have been explicitly proven'. That is evidence for 'incomplete in 1996: it lacked proof'. audits.name: Geroch (1967) topology-change theorem, with Borde's causally compact generalisation (gr-qc/9406053, Theorem 1): kinematic, no T_ab or field-equation assumption; topology change forces a closed timelike curve

source.located: Geroch, J. Math. Phys. 8, 782 (1967). There is no arXiv copy. It is restated exactly as Theorem III.2 of Pisana, Shoshany, Antoniou, Kauffman, Lambropoulou, arXiv:2505.02210v4 (sec. III.A, with Definition 6). Borde, arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, restates and generalises it as Theorem 1 (sec. IV; misconception list in sec. IX; escapes in IX.A-C).
source.via: This stage, answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content and discover_papers all returned 'quota exceeded', and the egress proxy refuses arxiv.org directly (403). I read from full texts that an earlier stage of this workflow cached in the d67 scratchpad: src/gr-qc_9406053.txt (md5 17c67ada52d92fc44065246ef92fee8c, header 'arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1 30 Jun 1994') and 2505.02210.txt (md5 9eebbb418dc3def4701cd4b9fd83633c, header 'arXiv:2505.02210v4 [gr-qc] 20 Apr 2026'). Borde 1994 is READ in full at the relevant sections. Geroch 1967 itself is NAMED-NOT-READ at source and is READ only through those two restatements: Borde paraphrases Geroch, while 2505.02210 states it as a theorem. The discover_papers search for later literature was NOT RUN for the same quota reason, so the later-literature list comes from the restating papers' own citation trails. It is a floor, not a search.

audits.published_statement: Geroch, as restated in 2505.02210 Thm III.2: 'Let W be a compact spacetime whose boundary is the disjoint union of two compact spacelike 3-manifolds, Sigma_i and Sigma_f. If W has no CTCs, then Sigma_i and Sigma_f are diffeomorphic, and, furthermore, W is topologically equivalent to Sigma_i x [0,1].' Def. 6 there defines a spacetime as a 4-manifold 'together with an everywhere non-degenerate time-orientable Lorentzian metric'. Borde Theorem 1: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).' Borde: 'By "causality violation" it is meant that there is at least one closed timelike curve.' Borde sec. IX: 'Neither Geroch's original theorem, nor its mild generalization in section IV, assume anything about the energy-momentum tensor, or indeed about a field equation - the results are purely kinematical.'
published_hypotheses: M (W) is an interpolating manifold: connected, smooth, Hausdorff and paracompact, with boundary S1 u S2. In Borde's generalisation the boundary may also include T, a compact timelike tube [Borde sec. II.A]

A smooth Lorentz metric that is non-degenerate everywhere on M, with S1 and S2 spacelike. T, if present, is timelike, with a timelike field tangent to it whose integral curves run from S1 to S2 [Borde II.A; 2505.02210 Def. 6]
Time-oriented, or time-orientable [Borde Thm 1 '(time-oriented)'; 2505.02210 Def. 6]. Borde secs. VII and IX: a non-time-orientable metric avoids the CTC only when one of the boundaries is empty

Geroch: W is compact, with compact (closed) spacelike boundary components. This is the closed-universe case; Borde reports that Geroch also covers the externally Lorentzian case. Borde: M is causally compact (the closure of I(p) is compact for every p), which a compact M satisfies trivially
Geroch, as restated in 2505.02210, is in dimension 4 (3-manifold slices). Borde's Theorem 1 assumes nothing about dimension
No energy condition, no field equation and no geodesic-completeness assumption
The conclusion is a CTC somewhere in M, the interpolating region. Nothing locates it more precisely
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED: time-orientability. create.py:64-66, specthm.py:1146-1148 (R10(e)), specthm.py:1843 (the GEROCH-BORDE fact, whose hyps are ['H_cc'] only) and ledger.py:626-628 (D24) all state the result with causal compactness as its only hypothesis. Borde's Theorem 1 is stated for a '(time-oriented)' spacetime. The cost here is small: Borde sec. IX says a non-time-orientable metric avoids the CTC only when one boundary is empty, and a throat created inside an existing space has neither boundary empty. The drop would matter only for creation from nothing.

DROPPED: a smooth Lorentz metric that is non-degenerate everywhere on the interpolating region. The tree never lists this hypothesis (create.py:64-66; specthm.py:614-615 H_cc; specthm.py:1843). create.ESCAPES (create.py:211-220) also leaves out Borde's escape IX.C, 'Degenerate metrics', where Borde reports Sorkin, Ashtekar and Horowitz and writes: 'Horowitz has shown that it is possible to construct reasonable topology-changing spacetimes if degenerate metrics are allowed. So, this might well prove to be the correct approach'. The tree's three escapes are IX.A, IX.B and the Euclidean path integral. Borde's own three 'within the general Lorentzian framework' are IX.A, IX.B and IX.C. So ledger.py:630-631, 'one of Borde's three escapes, and none stays inside Lorentzian GR without a pathology', matches Borde's count but not his list. It holds only if a degenerate point counts as a pathology, and the tree does not say so. Borde notes that curvature cannot be computed at such a point and the causal structure may be undefined there. This matters because M's own mechanism puts a singular throat at the creation site (M-S1A-P3, DOCKET 66).

WEAKENED, in the tree's favour: the inference 'SO EXOTIC MATTER CANNOT HELP' (create.py:60, create.py:340) and the flag EXOTIC_MATTER_HELPS_CREATION = False (create.py:186; ledger.py:628-629; specthm.py:1148-1149; the gate of the GEROCH-BORDE fact at specthm.py:1838-1841). The theorem supports something narrower: exotic matter cannot remove the forced CTC (z3 returns unsat for that in the re-derivation). It does not support 'exotic matter cannot help creation'. Borde IX.B names energy-condition violation as the way past his dynamical obstruction, condition (ii) of Theorem 3, the half-integral null convergence condition: 'there might be violations of the energy conditions large enough to allow assumption (ii) to be violated. Some discussions of wormhole creation are, for example, based precisely on large violations of the energy condition'. He adds that this 'would not affect the presence of causality violations'. create.ESCAPES[1] (create.py:215-217) carries only the other half of IX.B ('altering Einstein's equation ... fairly severe'). 2505.02210 then builds exactly that case: a non-singular wormhole nucleation with CTCs that 'violates all the standard energy conditions'. The flag is right about the CTC and goes too far about creation.

NOT A DRIFT. 'Geroch's closed-universe argument' (create.py:64) is the wording of Borde's abstract. specthm's 'ctc' literal (specthm.py:1844) matches Borde's definition of causality violation, at least one CTC. The W-create-cc note (specthm.py:1654-1657), that the forced CTC 'lies in the interpolating region', matches the theorem. The four quoted constants (BORDE, BORDE_SINGULARITY, BORDE_DYNAMICS, BORDE_CAUTION) and the phrases 'only to be had at a price', 'a very wide range of situations', 'highly undesirable feature' and 'fairly severe' all occur verbatim in the source (re-derivation part A).

SCOPE THE TREE KEEPS HONEST. D24 (ledger.py:626-627) and R10(e) are restricted to 'CAUSALLY COMPACT INTERPOLATING SPACETIMES', and theorems_apply_to_enlargement() = False. Both match the source. R10(e) says 'whether reasonable excludes the source a throat needs is not determined here', and that is accurate: Borde's 'reasonable' means Theorem 3's conditions, (i) generic and (ii) half-integral NCC, not the weak energy condition.

data_at_publication.quantity: None. This is a theorem about differential topology and causal structure, with no numerical input
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. No measured datum enters the statement or the proof. The only integers are topological (Euler characteristics), and part C re-derives them

rederivation.outcome: 51 checks, 0 FAIL; output is in rederive/geroch-1967-topology-change.out. The theorem is a continuum result, so it is NOT machine-checked as a whole. What was checked: (A) every quotation the tree carries is verbatim in the cached Borde text, and 2505.02210 Thm III.2 plus Def. 6 (non-degenerate, time-orientable) restate Geroch's statement. (B) create.ESCAPES has 3 entries, with no 'degenerate metrics' entry and no energy-condition route, whereas Borde places IX.A, IX.B and IX.C 'within the general Lorentzian framework'. (C) The Reinhart-Sorkin rule in sympy integer arithmetic. Wormhole nucleation S^3 -> S^1xS^2 by one 1-handle has chi(W) = -1, so it admits no Lorentz metric. W#CP2 has chi = 0, which is the Misner trick 2505.02210 uses. chi(M#V) = chi(M)+chi(V)-2. The n=3 rule forbids every genus change. The 2-D trousers have chi = -1 and the cylinder chi = 0. (D) Borde's own 2-D example, built explicitly: cylinder [-1,1]xS^1 with V = x d_x + (1-x^2) d_theta and g = h - 2 V_flat V_flat / h(V,V). det g = -1 everywhere, V is timelike everywhere and the boundary circles are spacelike. The circle x=0 is a closed timelike curve (g = -1). Past integral curves have no past endpoint and wind onto that circle. This is an instance of Theorem 1's conclusion and of its proof mechanism, an imprisoned integral curve accumulating on a CTC. (E) A slit flat cylinder. It has a global time function (g^{-1}(dt,dt) = -1, so no CTC), and the slice Euler characteristic goes from 0 to 1. That is topology change without a CTC once causal compactness fails; that H_cc fails there is argued, not computed. (F) z3. First, the finite core of the proof: for an acyclic successor map on n = 3, 5 and 7 cells, 'some orbit never exits' is unsat, and the vacuity guard with cycles allowed is sat. Second, the propositional split between the two theorems. Thm1 + created + cc + exotic + no CTC is unsat: exotic matter cannot remove the CTC. Thm3 + Einstein + NCC + generic + created + cc is unsat. created + cc + Einstein + exotic is sat, with ctc True in the model: the theorems do not exclude exotic matter as a route to creation consistent with Einstein's equation, but the CTC comes with it.

later_literature.what: Generalises Geroch from compact M to causally compact M (Theorem 1: any dimension, no T_ab assumption). Theorem 3 adds the dynamical obstruction in dimension >= 3 under the generic and half-integral null convergence conditions. Lists the escapes: IX.A drop causal compactness; IX.B weaken the curvature constraints, either by altering Einstein's equation or by large energy-condition violations; IX.C degenerate metrics; and the Euclidean path integral.

later_literature.ref: Pisana, Shoshany, Antoniou, Kauffman, Lambropoulou, arXiv:2505.02210v4 (2025, rev. 2026)
later_literature.what: Restates Geroch's theorem exactly (Thm III.2). Builds a non-singular 4-D wormhole nucleation (0-surgery plus #CP2) whose non-degenerate metric necessarily carries CTCs and 'violates all the standard energy conditions'. Geroch's conclusion is met, not evaded. The paper also shows that energy-condition violation is the price of the construction, which is the route Borde IX.B names. A discrepancy is recorded, not treated as a refutation: its ref [7] prints Geroch's year as 2004, where Borde ref 5 gives J. Math. Phys. 8, 782 (1967).
later_literature.read_status: READ (cached full text 2505.02210.txt; secs I, III.A-B and references)

later_literature.ref: Visser, arXiv:gr-qc/0204022 (2002), 'The quantum physics of chronology protection'
later_literature.what: 'theorems that localized topology change implies either causal pathology or naked singularities; either possibility is objectionable', citing Friedman 1991, Horowitz 1991 and Gibbons-Hawking 1992.

Topology change with metrics that are degenerate at isolated points, in the first-order formalism. This lies outside Geroch's non-degeneracy hypothesis, and it is the escape create.ESCAPES leaves out.

later_literature.ref: Gibbons & Hawking, Commun. Math. Phys. 148, 345 (1992), 'Selection rules for topology change'
later_literature.what: Selection rules from spin structure and kink number. According to 2505.02210 they 'do not appear to prohibit the creation of wormholes, as long as they are created in pairs'.

later_literature.ref: Dowker, Garcia, Surya, Class. Quant. Grav. 17, 697 (2000), 'Morse index and causal continuity'
later_literature.what: Topology change through Morse singularities (degenerate metrics), with a causal-continuity criterion based on Morse index. This is the degenerate-metric branch.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for THIS result. The theorem has no empirical input. Geroch (1967) and Borde (1994) used only the listed hypotheses: a non-degenerate, time-orientable Lorentz metric, spacelike boundaries, and compactness or causal compactness. No measured quantity enters, so no later datum can move the conclusion. Everything that came later is mathematical or concerns the framework, and all of it is consistent with the theorem. Borde widened the class from compact to causally compact and kept the conclusion. Gibbons and Hawking added selection rules. 2505.02210 (2025) built an explicit non-singular wormhole nucleation and found the CTC Geroch forces, exactly where the Misner connected sum puts it. Evidence AGAINST 'the authors lacked data and so were wrong' for this result: 58 years of use, two independent restatements whose content agrees, an explicit instance built in the re-derivation, and no counterexample within the hypotheses in anything read. Evidence FOR 'incomplete': the result is deliberately scoped. Its hypotheses (non-degenerate metric, time orientation, causal compactness, classical Lorentzian framework) are exactly what the later escapes relax: degenerate or Morse metrics, non-time-orientable creation from nothing, non-compact interpolation, and Euclidean or quantum approaches. Borde himself says the theorems' 'true value' is to 'pinpoint what modifications we have to make'. That incompleteness lies in the scope, not in the data. It is also where the tree's use narrows: the dropped non-degeneracy hypothesis and the overreach about exotic matter.
audits.grade_evidence: The kinematic theorem itself stands. Every quotation the tree carries is verbatim in Borde (part A). 2505.02210 Thm III.2 restates Geroch's statement consistently. Borde's own 2-D example, built with an explicit non-degenerate metric, shows the forced CTC and the proof's accumulation mechanism (part D). The finite core of the proof and the Thm1/Thm3 logic pass z3, with vacuity guards (part F). No datum enters. The tree's USE is narrower than the source in three named places, and none of them is a refutation. (1) Time-orientability is dropped (create.py:64-66, specthm.py:1146-1148 and 1843, ledger.py:626-628). This is harmless unless a boundary is empty. (2) The non-degenerate-metric hypothesis is dropped, and Borde's escape IX.C 'Degenerate metrics' is missing from create.ESCAPES (create.py:211-220). So 'none stays inside Lorentzian GR without a pathology' (ledger.py:630-631) holds only if a degenerate point counts as a pathology. The tree does not say so, and the point bears on M's singular-throat mechanism. (3) 'SO EXOTIC MATTER CANNOT HELP' and EXOTIC_MATTER_HELPS_CREATION = False (create.py:60, 186 and 340; ledger.py:628-629; specthm.py:1148-1149 and 1838-1841) are supported only in the sense 'exotic matter cannot remove the forced CTC' (z3 unsat). Borde IX.B names large energy-condition violation as the way past the dynamical obstruction to wormhole creation, and 2505.02210 realises it: non-singular, with CTCs, all energy conditions violated. In z3, created & cc & Einstein & exotic is sat with ctc True. Under M-S1A-P3, where a CTC disqualifies only at the seat, that route is exactly the one left open. This agrees with the tree's own OPEN verdict on W-create-cc.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree adds time-orientation and a Lorentz metric non-degenerate everywhere to H_cc or the GEROCH-BORDE fact; adds Borde IX.C (degenerate metrics) and the energy-condition half of IX.B to create.ESCAPES; and scopes EXOTIC_MATTER_HELPS_CREATION to 'cannot remove the forced CTC'. To WRONG: a time-oriented, causally compact interpolating spacetime with a smooth non-degenerate Lorentz metric, non-diffeomorphic spacelike boundaries and no CTC. No such spacetime appears in anything read, and Borde's and Geroch's proofs rule it out. To OPEN, on the source side: the cached Borde or 2505.02210 text turns out not to be the arXiv version. Re-read both at alphaXiv when the quota resets. Geroch 1967 itself stays NAMED-NOT-READ at source either way.

verifiers.reason:
The grade survives. The alphaXiv quota had reset, so I read both sources at source this stage instead of relying on the cache: gr-qc/9406053v1 pp. 1, 3, 5, 6, 12-14, 17, 19-22, 30 and 35-37, and 2505.02210v4 pp. 1, 2, 4-6, 14, 17 and 22. Every passage the auditor relies on is in the source and matches the cached texts.

What the source confirms:
- Thm 1 is stated for a '(time-oriented)' spacetime.
- Sec. VII and IX: a non-time-orientable metric avoids the CTC only when one boundary is empty.
- IX.B names a second route past Theorem 3's condition (ii): 'violations of the energy conditions large enough ... Some discussions of wormhole creation are ... based precisely on large violations of the energy condition'. It says this 'would not affect the presence of causality violations'.
- IX.C lists 'Degenerate metrics' among the escapes 'within the general Lorentzian framework', and also names its problems: no inverse, so no curvature at those points, and a causal structure that may be undefined.
- 2505.02210 Thm III.2 and Def. 6 ('everywhere non-degenerate time-orientable') are as quoted, and so is 'violates all the standard energy conditions'.
- 2505.02210 ref [7] prints 2004; Borde ref 5 gives J. Math. Phys. 8, 782 (1967).

The theorem itself stands. No datum enters it. The rederivation re-runs at 51/51, 0 FAIL, exit 0.

The narrowing is real and comes from the source text, not from a misreading:
- create.py:215-217 ESCAPES[1] keeps only the 'altering Einstein's equation ... fairly severe' half of IX.B and drops Borde's energy-condition half.
- ESCAPES leaves out IX.C, and its third entry is the Euclidean path integral, which Borde places outside the Lorentzian framework.
- So EXOTIC_MATTER_HELPS_CREATION = False (create.py:186; ledger.py:629; specthm.py:1842) is supported only as 'exotic matter cannot remove the forced CTC'. Borde himself says energy-condition violation may get past the dynamical obstruction (Thm 3), the very wall create.py quotes as BORDE_DYNAMICS.

audits.published_statement: Hawking-Ellis Prop. 4.5.12 as restated by 2408.00154, 2010.05086 and Galloway math/9909158: an achronal null geodesic contains no pair of conjugate points. The equivalent form in Gao-Wald gr-qc/0007021 (from Wald Sec. 9.3 and HE): suppose a null geodesic gamma from p to r contains a pair of conjugate points lying between p and r, with the first conjugate point strictly before r. Then gamma can be deformed, endpoints fixed, into a timelike curve, so r is in I+(p). A point q in J+(p) - I+(p) is reached only by a null geodesic with no conjugate points between p and q. Two points are conjugate when a nonzero Jacobi field vanishes at both, i.e. det A = 0 with A(p) = 0, A'(p) = 1.

It drops FFKP's state class (79), without which FFKP say no DSNEC in standard form can be written. It also drops the free-scalar, null-smearing, massless and factorisation hypotheses. audits.published_statement: NOT QUOTED (source unreadable here). The standard form, re-derived in the script: for L[u] = (p u')' + q u with p > 0 and q real (piecewise continuous / L^1_loc), the Lagrange identity v L[u] - u L[v] = d/dx[p (v u' - u v')] holds. So L with Dirichlet conditions u(a) = u(b) = 0 is (formally) self-adjoint, and the Wronskian p W is constant on solutions. Sturm separation (1836): the zeros of two linearly independent real solutions strictly interlace. Oscillation: the number of zeros in (a,b) of the solution with u(a) = 0 equals the number of Dirichlet eigenvalues of -L below 0, and the Dirichlet spectrum is invariant under x -> a + b - x. The in-tree 'reversal theorem' (06ee6bf:transit.py:50-54), quoted: 'Let u'' + q u = 0 with u(0) = u(L) = 0. Define the path read from the far end, q~(x) = q(L - x). Then v(x) := u(L - x) satisfies v'' + q~ v = 0 with v(0) = u(L) = 0 and v(L) = u(0) = 0. The SAME pair is conjugate. QED'.
published_hypotheses: (H1) scalar, linear, second order, in self-adjoint (Sturm-Liouville) form (p u')' + q u = 0 with p > 0 -- here p = 1, no first-derivative term
(H2) q real and piecewise continuous / L^1_loc (Sturm assumed continuity; L^1_loc via Caratheodory solutions is the later extension -- stated from the re-derivation, not read)

(H3) q a FIXED function of the affine parameter, independent of the solution's initial data (for the Jacobi equation: Ricci-only scalar focusing, or the full matrix Jacobi equation with a SYMMETRIC tidal matrix T)
(H4) self-adjointness is with respect to Dirichlet conditions at both ends of the interval; separation and oscillation need only real coefficients and a sign-definite Wronskian
(H5) 'reading from the far end' = the SAME segment with the affine parameter reversed (lambda -> L - lambda); R_ab k^a k^b is even in k, so q is reflected, not changed
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED LEMMA (proof route), seatindex.py:105-107 and :354. The fold c -> L - l - c is justified by 'transit.py's reversal theorem', but that theorem (06ee6bf:transit.py:50-54) is TWO-ENDED: it maps a conjugate pair (0, L) to itself. seats() (seatindex.py:144-156) is ONE-ENDED: u(0)=0, u'(0)=1, 'does u vanish in (0, L]?'. Reflection maps a zero of u0 at b to the pair (L-b, L), which does not start at 0, so the pair theorem alone does not give seats(q) == seats(q~). The missing step is Sturm separation: u0 has a zero in (0,L] iff the solution vanishing at L has a zero in [0,L). It is proved here by z3 [3] and confirmed exactly on 3,960 profiles [4]. The CONCLUSION is true; the cited justification is incomplete. For the same reason the canonical hypothesis 'Dirichlet conditions at both ends of [0, L]' is not the fold's hypothesis: admission has Dirichlet at 0 only.

ATTRIBUTION WEAKER THAN STATED, seatindex.py:109-110 ('the Jacobi operator is self-adjoint, so reading the path from the far end gives the same answer') and 06ee6bf:transit.py:56. The pair substitution v(x) = u(L-x) uses no self-adjointness (sympy [2]); it holds for any linear 2nd-order ODE with reflected coefficients. Sturm separation needs only a sign-definite Wronskian (W' = -r W, sympy [1]). What self-adjoint form actually buys is CLOSURE of the index family under reversal: with a drift term r u', reversal sends r -> -r(L-x) (sympy [1]). Keeping +r breaks the Boolean in 6/30 RK4 trials; flipping it restores 0/30 [7]. A discrepancy of wording, not of result.

SCOPE NOT NAMED (Boolean only), seatindex.py:105-107 ('c and L - l - c the same cell', 'SYMMETRIC ABOUT ITS MIDPOINT'). Only seat/no-seat folds. The turn position seats() returns does not: at the fixture m=6, l=0.9, L=12, c=0.5 turns at 1.4208 while c'=10.6 turns at 11.2570 [6]. The index's cells (scan(), seatindex.py:222-234) store only the Boolean, so the index's use is inside scope; reusing the fold for the turn value would not be.

HYPOTHESIS NOT NAMED (H3, fixed q / symmetric T), seatindex.py:98-112. seatindex.py never mentions shear (reversal.py:14-17 records this for the file). In a scalar reduction with shear, q_eff = (R_kk + sigma^2)/2 depends on sigma integrated from the starting end's data, so the scalar fold does not follow. For the full 2x2 Jacobi equation with SYMMETRIC T it does: existence is reversal-symmetric in 40/40 trials and first conjugate points coincide in 40/40. With an antisymmetric part added it fails (6/40 existence, 4/40 coincidence) [8]. T is symmetric for Levi-Civita curvature (pair symmetry), so the fold extends to the true Jacobi operator; only the scalar-with-shear shortcut is excluded.

HYPOTHESIS NOT NAMED (H5, same segment), seatindex.py:110-112 ('reading the path from the far end ... M's both-ends prediction'). The theorem is about the same null segment with the affine parameter reversed; the tree's own measurement did exactly this (06ee6bf:transit.py:161-166, sampler(reverse_at=L)). That difference is worked by hand, not computed on a bubble here. Within seatindex's model slabs this is interpretive only.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply here in the usual sense. The result is a finite theorem about linear second-order ODEs (Sturm and Liouville 1836-37, Jacobi 1837) that uses no data: no measured input enters it, so no later datum can move it. Evidence: the re-derivation reproduces it symbolically and exactly (0/3,960 fold mismatches, no discretisation). What the 1836 authors did lack is matrix Jacobi systems on Lorentzian null geodesics and Weyl (shear) focusing. That is exactly where the tree's use needs care, and on the true operator it goes the tree's way: with a symmetric tidal matrix the reversal symmetry survives (40/40), and it fails only for a non-symmetric T (6/40), which Levi-Civita curvature never produces. (1) The source is now READ, not NAMED-NOT-READ. alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on arXiv:math/0311049 (B. Simon, 'Sturm oscillation and comparison theorems', v1, 4 Nov 2003) returned the full text. The audit dates it 2005; the copy read is v1, 2003. Three statements in it match the audit's re-derivation:
- Section 3, Theorem 3.1 (Sturm comparison): with E2 = E1 and u2(a) != 0, a solution u2 has a zero in (a,b) whenever u1(a) = u1(b) = 0. This is exactly the Sturm separation step the one-ended fold needs (the audit's drift (a), z3 check [3]).
- The proof of Theorem 3.1 uses only W' = (E2 - E1) u1 u2, so at equal E the Wronskian is constant. This backs the audit's drift (b): the separation step needs a Wronskian of fixed sign, not self-adjointness.
- Theorem 3.3 and Theorem 3.4 (oscillation, Dirichlet u(0) = u(a) = 0 on L^2(0,a)) back check [4].
Stated hypotheses: Schrodinger form -u'' + V u, V a bounded function (Section 3). For the paper as a whole Simon says he restricts to 'bounded and continuous perturbations' for simplicity and that standard techniques extend this. The tree's slab q is bounded, piecewise constant and discontinuous. It is therefore covered by Section 3's 'V bounded' and by the proof, which needs only C^1 solutions. Continuity is a pedagogical simplification, not a hypothesis of the theorem.
- agrees_with_source moves from 'partly' to 'yes'.
- The caveat 'STANDS rests on computation, not the text' is lifted for Simon.
- Sturm 1836 (J. Math. Pures Appl. 1, 106-186, cited as Simon's ref [22]) stays NAMED-NOT-READ, restated through Simon.

(2) One of the audit's supporting claims about the TREE'S INTEGRATOR is sample-dependent. This is not about the theorem. The audit reports 0/54 fold mismatches in the tree's seats() near threshold, with the edge disagreement 'the same on both sides of the fold'. My independent threshold sweep (sl_indep.py) found 4/44 tree fold mismatches. The method: tune the exterior value by exact bisection until the first zero sits at L, then step it by ±1e-3 and ±1e-5. Example: m=6, l=0.5, c=0.3, L=12, exterior -0.4974982. The exact forward zero is at 6.149. The tree's seats(), with its default n=4000, gives 5.847 forward and None reversed. With n=40000 it gives 6.113 and 11.9997; with n=400000, 6.145 and 11.99982. So the reversed zero lies within about one step (h = 0.003) of L. The fold holds in the continuum and fails only in the discrete instrument. One-ended admission is therefore not discretely symmetric near threshold. That is the tree's integrator, not Sturm.

The theorem itself holds exactly in my independent check: mpmath exact piecewise-constant propagation, 40 digits, with q of both signs and 1 to 6 segments. Fold mismatches: 0/4000. The auditor's script re-runs to exit 0 with 'ALL CHECKS AGREE'. scan() uses a fixed grid away from threshold, where the auditor reports 0/160, so the index's actual use stays inside scope.

None of these narrows the external result as the index uses it.

audits.name: Earnshaw's theorem: no static configuration of point sources under an inverse-square potential is stably in equilibrium (harmonic potential has no strict minimum; Hessian of 1/r traceless), for any signs

That re-derivation does not depend on any reading. Two things remain unread: whether this content is correctly attributed to Earnshaw 1842, and the exact hypotheses Earnshaw himself stated. audits.published_statement: NOT QUOTED FROM SOURCE, because the source cannot be read here. The only wording available is a search-engine summary from WebSearch, which is not a reading: 'a collection of point charges cannot be maintained in a stable stationary equilibrium configuration solely by the electrostatic interaction of the charges', applying 'to classical inverse-square law forces (electric and gravitational)'. It is recorded here as the conventional modern form and flagged as unread. Nothing in the grade rests on it; the grade rests on the re-derivation.
published_hypotheses: These were NOT read at source. Each item below is a hypothesis the re-derivation shows the conclusion needs, not a quotation.

H1: the only forces come from a potential whose kernel is EXACTLY 1/r, i.e. the force is exactly inverse-square. S6a shows Lap r^-(1+d) = d(1+d) r^-(3+d), which vanishes only at d = 0. S6b shows a Yukawa kernel is not harmonic.
H2: the fields are static, the frame is inertial, and there are no velocity-dependent or time-dependent forces.

H3: the bodies are point particles, so only translational degrees of freedom count. For extended rigid bodies the translational conclusion survives by superposition; rotational equilibria are not covered.
H4: there are no induced or response sources (no polarisable or diamagnetic media). The charges or masses are fixed.
H5: the potential is evaluated away from the sources (r != 0).

H6: 'stable' means Lyapunov stable. The step from 'the potential has no minimum' to 'unstable' needs one of two things. If the Hessian is non-zero, the instability is exponential (S3, S4). If the Hessian is zero but the potential is not constant, it needs the Chetaev-Kozlov instability theorem, which is NAMED-NOT-READ; S5 gives numerical evidence.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKER ARGUMENT, CONCLUSION INTACT (stability.py:114-119; chain.py:141-150; paper/CLAIMS.md:988-991; obstruct.py:236-239). The tree argues: harmonic, therefore no strict minimum of U = m phi, therefore no stable equilibrium. It handles negative masses with 'negating m flips U = m phi, and -phi is harmonic too' (chain.py:148-149). The minimum-of-U criterion (Lagrange-Dirichlet) assumes the kinetic energy is POSITIVE-DEFINITE. The tree's own negmass.py case breaks that assumption. For a Bondi negative mass (inertial mass = passive mass < 0) the equation of motion is a = -grad phi whatever m is, so U = m phi is the wrong function and its minimum criterion runs backwards. The CONCLUSION still holds for every sign pattern. The linearisation K = M^-1 Hess U is traceless, because it is a sum of traceless diagonal blocks, but it is NOT symmetric. A traceless matrix cannot have an all-real-positive spectrum, so some mode grows exponentially unless the spectrum is {0}. S4 shows this for 7 free mixed-sign static equilibria: trace about 1e-17, all 7 K non-symmetric, growth rates 0.097 to 7.48. This is a flaw in the argument, not a refutation.

MISSING STEP (stability.py:116-117, 'a harmonic function has no strict minimum and NO static configuration is stably in equilibrium'). 'No minimum' does not by itself imply 'unstable'; the converse of Lagrange-Dirichlet is not a general theorem. For harmonic potentials the gap closes in two cases. Case 1, non-zero Hessian: a traceless symmetric matrix has a negative eigenvalue, so growth is exponential; in S3 all 93 equilibria found are saddles. Case 2, zero Hessian with a non-constant potential: the leading Taylor form is a non-zero harmonic polynomial with zero spherical mean (S2, k = 1..6), so there is no minimum, and instability then follows from the Chetaev-Kozlov theorem, which is NAMED-NOT-READ. Numerically (S5), for phi = x^3 - 3xy^2 a particle released at rest at 1e-3 leaves r < 0.5 at t = 92.1. The tree states neither step. chain.py:336 correctly names the escape as 'Hessian identically zero', meaning a constant potential, not a Hessian that is zero at one point.

UNDERSTATED, NOT OVERSTATED (stability.py:116). 'No strict minimum' is weaker than the truth. S2 shows a harmonic function has no local minimum of any kind, strict or not, unless it is locally constant. This SUPPORTS the tree's claim that 'the one escape Earnshaw permits is the DEGENERATE case, constant potential' (stability.py:118-119).

UNSTATED ASSUMPTION INSIDE THE WORD 'NEWTONIAN' (stability.py:120-123, 'the Newtonian CEILING' and 'a non-gravitational channel'). The ceiling needs a kernel that is EXACTLY 1/r (H1). Lee et al. 2020 (arXiv:2002.11761) test for an added Yukawa term, V_N[1 + alpha exp(-r/lambda)], and motivate it from GRAVITATIONAL physics (dilaton, heavy graviton, extra dimensions), not only from non-gravitational channels. Any such term makes the potential inside the shell non-constant. S6c gives phi_in = -alpha G M lambda e^{-R/lambda} sinh(r/lambda)/(R r). S6e gives the curvature at the centre as -alpha G M e^{-R/lambda}/(3 R lambda^2), which is restoring only if alpha*M_shell < 0. The tree's list of escapes names 'a non-gravitational channel' and 'GR' but not a gravitational term that departs from 1/r. Taking 'Newtonian gravity' as the stated hypothesis, the tree's statement is exact.

THE INSTRUMENT MEASURES THE PREMISE AND REPORTS THE CONSEQUENCE (chain.py:323-326, has_strict_minimum). The check returns relative_laplacian > 1e-9. It measures harmonicity at one point and reports 'no strict minimum' as what the theorem then implies. Its docstring says this openly. This is not a fault; S2-S5 supply the step from the premise to the consequence.

SCOPE (stability.py:117, 'NO static configuration ... any placement'). The theorem covers point sources and translational stability only (H3). The tree applies it to a core inside an extended shell. By superposition, the core's potential energy as a function of its displacement is still harmonic; inside a uniform 1/r shell it is constant (S6d). The application is therefore within scope.

ATTRIBUTION (stability.py:114, 'CLOSED IN NEWTONIAN GRAVITY BY chain.py'). The owner credits a peer file with the closure, and chain.py:132-162 carries the argument. paper/CLAIMS.md:1001 labels it 'PROVEN ... Earnshaw from the traceless Hessian'. The traceless Hessian proves harmonicity only. To call the instability PROVEN also needs the S2/S4 steps, plus Chetaev-Kozlov in the degenerate case.

data_at_publication.quantity: The exponent of the force law, i.e. whether it is exactly 1/r^2. This is premise H1, and the whole theorem rests on it.
data_at_publication.value_then: In 1842 the law was taken as exactly inverse-square, by assumption. The experimental bounds available to Earnshaw (Cavendish and Coulomb for electricity, planetary motion for gravity) are NAMED-NOT-READ.
data_at_publication.value_now: Lee, Adelberger, Cook, Fleischer, Heckel, arXiv:2002.11761v1 (2020). Read from the local cache src/casmag/all/2002.11761v1.txt (md5 622a98c0aca3ad072ad15ea81a23d00f), lines 20-23 and 564-565: 'Newtonian gravity gave an excellent fit to our data, limiting with 95% confidence any gravitational-strength Yukawa interactions to ranges < 38.6 um'. The Yukawa form is V(r) = V_N(r)[1 + alpha exp(-r/lambda)] (lines 51-54), and the data cover separations from 52 um to 3.0 mm. Bounds on |alpha| < 1 at longer lambda (their Fig. 5 cites previous works) are NAMED-NOT-READ.
data_at_publication.source_now: arXiv:2002.11761, read from the local cache of an earlier alphaXiv extraction; the alphaXiv quota was exceeded at this stage.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: NO, as long as the stated hypothesis 'Newtonian gravity' holds. Computed in S6: a Yukawa term breaks harmonicity, since Lap e^{-r/L}/r = e^{-r/L}/(L^2 r). It turns the neutral seat into a restoring one (alpha*M < 0) or an anti-restoring one (alpha*M > 0). The stiffness relative to the Newtonian scale GM/R^3 is |alpha|(R/lambda)^2 e^{-R/lambda}/3. At the bound read here (lambda = 38.6 um, |alpha| = 1) it is 10^-11242.8 for R = 1 m, 10^-8.9 for R = 1 mm and 10^-0.8 for R = 0.1 mm. So for any macroscopic device the deviation the data still allow at gravitational strength changes nothing. Only a sub-millimetre device, or a short-range term stronger than gravity (|alpha| > 1 at lambda < 38.6 um, not read here), could move the conclusion. Either would be outside 'Newtonian', and the tree's escape clause covers that only as 'non-gravitational'.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (exit 0) across 17 checks. S1 (sympy): tr Hess(1/r) = 0 exactly, and the Laplacian of three point sources with SYMBOLIC strengths and positions is 0, so any signs are covered. S2 (sympy): for k = 1..6, the homogeneous harmonic polynomials in R^3 form a space of dimension 2k+1, and every one has exactly zero spherical mean, so each takes negative values. Hence a non-constant harmonic function has no local minimum, strict or not. S3 (numeric): 93 equilibria of a test particle among 2-5 fixed sources with random signs were found; all 93 are saddles (eigenvalues of both signs), with max |tr H|/scale = 1.5e-15. S4 (numeric): 7 static equilibria of FREE collinear mixed-sign Bondi 3-body systems. The masses come from the null vector of the antisymmetric coupling matrix, and the residual acceleration is 0. In all 7 the linearisation is traceless (|tr| <= 2e-17) and non-symmetric, and every one has an exponentially growing mode (rates 0.097 to 7.483). So Earnshaw's conclusion holds for any signs, even where the tree's potential-minimum argument does not apply. S5 (numeric): at the degenerate critical point of phi = x^3 - 3xy^2 (zero Hessian, not constant), a particle released at rest leaves the point (t_exit = 92.1). S6 (sympy): Lap r^-(1+d) = d(1+d) r^-(3+d), and the Laplacian of a Yukawa kernel is non-zero. An exact integral gives the Yukawa potential inside a shell as phi_in = -alpha G M lambda e^{-R/lambda} sinh(r/lambda)/(R r). Its Newtonian limit is the constant -GM/R, which reproduces the tree's degenerate seat. The curvature at the centre is -alpha G M e^{-R/lambda}/(3 R lambda^2).

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. Earnshaw's theorem is a theorem, not a measurement. Given its premise, a static and exactly harmonic potential of fixed sources (i.e. exactly 1/r), the conclusion is re-derived exactly here and needs no datum. The only empirical input is the premise itself: that the force law is EXACTLY inverse-square. In 1842 that was an assumption. Two things came later. (a) Laboratory tests of gravity's 1/r^2 law; the tightest one read here, Lee et al. 2020, finds no gravitational-strength Yukawa term at lambda >= 38.6 um (95% CL). (b) General relativity, where static stability is a different question; the tree keeps the GR version NOT-RUN. Would having these data change the conclusion? Computed evidence on each side. For 'no change': the Yukawa stiffness the data still allow inside a shell, at |alpha| = 1, is 10^-11242.8 of the Newtonian scale for a 1 m shell and 10^-8.9 for a 1 mm shell (S6). The Newtonian ceiling therefore survives to any precision that matters for a macroscopic device. Against 'no change': the data leave room at lambda < 38.6 um, and for |alpha| > 1 there. In that region a shell smaller than 0.1 mm would feel a Yukawa stiffness of about 10^-0.8 of the Newtonian scale, and of EITHER sign (restoring only if alpha*M_shell < 0). The ceiling would then not be a ceiling. That region lies outside 'Newtonian gravity', the tree's stated hypothesis, so it does not falsify the tree's statement. But the tree's escape list ('GR, time dependence, or a non-gravitational channel') leaves out a gravitational term that departs from 1/r, which is how Lee et al. themselves frame the dilaton and heavy-graviton possibilities. No datum that Earnshaw lacked overturns the theorem.
audits.grade_evidence: The mathematical content the tree uses is re-derived in full here; the re-derivation passes all 17 checks. (1) The potential of point sources of any signs is harmonic (S1, exact). (2) A non-constant harmonic function has no local minimum at all (S2, exact, k = 1..6). So the only case with a minimum is the constant potential, which is exactly the tree's 'one escape ... the DEGENERATE case' (stability.py:118-119). (3) Every equilibrium among fixed sources of random signs is a saddle (S3, 93/93). (4) Free mixed-sign Bondi static equilibria are exponentially unstable (S4, 7/7). (5) A particle leaves the degenerate zero-Hessian critical point (S5). (6) The Newtonian potential inside the shell is the constant -GM/R (S6d). While the stated hypothesis 'Newtonian gravity' holds, no datum that has moved changes the conclusion (S6: 10^-11242.8 at R = 1 m). Two flaws in the tree's argument are recorded, not repaired, and neither is a refutation. First, the tree's minimum-of-U argument assumes positive inertia, which the tree's own negative-mass case violates; the traceless-K argument rescues the conclusion (S4). Second, 'no minimum, therefore unstable' is stated without the zero-Hessian step (Chetaev-Kozlov, NAMED-NOT-READ; numerical evidence in S5). CAVEAT ON THE GRADE: Earnshaw 1842 and every restatement are NAMED-NOT-READ, because the alphaXiv quota was exceeded and arXiv and Wikipedia are egress-blocked. STANDS therefore certifies the statement as the tree uses it, by re-derivation. It does not certify the attribution to Earnshaw or that the tree matches his own hypotheses.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED in either of two cases. (a) Earnshaw's paper or a reliable restatement, once read, states a hypothesis the tree drops that the re-derivation did not surface, e.g. a restriction to like-sign sources or to positive inertia that the published proof actually needs. (b) The degenerate zero-Hessian case turns out NOT to be covered by the Chetaev-Kozlov instability theorem for some harmonic potential. DATA-DEPENDENT if the device's scale were set below about 0.1 mm. There, a gravitational-strength Yukawa term at lambda < 38.6 um, which is still allowed, would give a stiffness of order the Newtonian scale and of either sign. WRONG only if a counterexample is shown. One would be a static equilibrium of a test particle in an exactly 1/r field of fixed sources (any signs) whose linearisation is stable. Another would be a free mixed-sign point configuration whose linearisation K is non-zero, has its spectrum in [0, inf), and has bounded solutions. S3 and S4 found neither, and tr K = 0 rules both out by construction. OPEN would apply only if the re-derivation were withdrawn.

On p.2 it uses the Laplacian criterion "unstable if Lap_d F <= 0", which is the same harmonic-trace route the tree uses. Earnshaw 1842 itself stays NAMED-NOT-READ. The attribution is now corroborated by a read restatement, not by a search snippet.

A DEFECT IN THE AUDIT'S EVIDENCE, NOT IN ITS GRADE. The audit's data claims overstate how small a non-Newtonian departure can be, and that error favours the tree.
1. It evaluates the Yukawa stiffness at one range only, lambda = 38.6 um. From that it reports 10^-11242.8 of GM/R^3 for R = 1 m. It concludes that the departure the data still allow "changes nothing" for any macroscopic device.
2. The stiffness ratio is |alpha|*(R/lambda)^2*e^{-R/lambda}/3. Its maximum over lambda is at lambda = R/2, where it equals 0.180*|alpha|. So the real ceiling is about 0.18*alpha_max(lambda ~ R/2), the bound at a range of about R/2. That bound is finite at every scale, and the audit leaves it NAMED-NOT-READ. It is not an exponent of -11242.8.
3. I read one bound from source. Adelberger, Heckel and Nelson, hep-ph/0307284, p.56, give the lunar-laser-ranging limit dw/w = (alpha/2)(a/lambda)^2 e^{-a/lambda} < 1.6e-11 (95% CL). That expression has the same functional form as the stiffness. For a shell of lunar-orbit radius, the allowed stiffness is therefore below 1.07e-11 of the Newtonian scale for EVERY lambda. The audit's method at that radius would give 10^-4.3e12. Script: verify/refute/earnshaw_yukawa_scan.py.
4. At R = 1 m the bound lives only in that review's Fig. 4, a plot I did not read numerically, so the actual value stays NAMED-NOT-READ. Nothing read suggests it is anywhere near super-exponentially small.
5. The audit's "DATA-DEPENDENT below ~0.1 mm" threshold is an artefact of fixing lambda. A small non-zero Yukawa stiffness of either sign is still allowed at every scale.

All of this lies outside the stated "Newtonian" hypothesis, so it does not touch the grade. The audit's lacked_data, moves_conclusion and what_would_change_the_grade should be restated: the departures still allowed are bounded by alpha_max(lambda ~ R/2), not by the 38.6 um point, and the 10^-11242.8 figure should not be quoted as the margin.

The audit's hypothesis-drift note stands and is now sharper. The tree's escape list ("GR, time dependence, or a non-gravitational channel") omits a gravitational term that departs from 1/r. That term is how hep-ph/0307284 eq. 2 and Lee et al. frame it. The tree's statement stays exact only because the word "Newtonian" carries it.

Every figure in the audit matches: 93 of 93 equilibria are saddles; the 7 S4 rates run from 0.097 to 7.483; t_exit is 92.1; the stiffness ratios are 10^-11242.8, 10^-8.9 and 10^-0.8. - S1 is the exact premise (harmonicity with symbolic signs and positions), not a toy.

VACUITY GUARD. Six checks in earnshaw-vacuity.py, of which 4 discriminate and 2 are vacuous.
- (V1) S2 even k discriminates: the non-harmonic forms r^2, r^4, x^4+y^4+z^4 and r^6 have spherical means 4pi, 4pi, 12pi/5 and 4pi.
- (V1b) VACUOUS: the odd-k rows of S2 (k = 1, 3, 5) pass for ANY polynomial by parity. They carry no information, though the conclusion for odd k is trivially true anyway.
- (V2) VACUOUS: S3's random-source search, rerun with the hypothesis negated (kernel 1/r^2 or 1/r^0.5, not harmonic), still finds only saddles: 76 of 76, 96 of 96, and 68 of 68 with all sources the same sign. So S3 would also pass with H1 false. Its 93 of 93 follows from S1 (a non-zero, symmetric, traceless matrix always has eigenvalues of both signs), not from independent evidence. Symmetric cages do discriminate (earnshaw-vacuity2.py): at the centre of a like-sign tetrahedron, octahedron or cube, the 1/r^2 kernel gives a definite Hessian (eigenvalues 0.30, 4 and 0.59, each triple) and 1/r^0.5 gives a negative-definite one, while 1/r gives EXACTLY ZERO. - (V4) S5 discriminates: x^2+y^2 and x^4+y^4 (a degenerate minimum) stay bounded, while the harmonic cubic escapes in 12 of 12 release directions.

A harmonic quartic released exactly along an invariant ray can stay bounded in exact arithmetic (11 of 12 escaped), so a single-ray release test is weak evidence.

2. S2's odd-k rows are vacuous.

Neither changes the grade. WHAT HOLDS. (1) value_now is quoted correctly. The cached 2002.11761v1.txt has md5 622a98c0aca3ad072ad15ea81a23d00f as stated. Its abstract reads 'Newtonian gravity gave an excellent fit to our data, limiting with 95% confidence any gravitational-strength Yukawa interactions to ranges < 38.6 um'. The Yukawa form V_N[1+alpha exp(-r/lambda)] and the 52 um to 3.0 mm range match. The page-5 text adds: 'any gravitational-strength Yukawa interaction must have lambda < 38.6 um', with dilaton and heavy-graviton motivation. (2) value_then is honestly marked NAMED-NOT-READ. (3) The S6 algebra is right; I re-derived it independently with sympy in verify/data/earnshaw_data_lens.py. The curvature at the centre is -alpha G M e^{-R/lambda}/(3 R lambda^2). The stiffness ratio is |alpha|(R/lambda)^2 e^{-R/lambda}/3. At |alpha| = 1 and lambda = 38.6 um it gives 10^-11242.80 for R = 1 m, 10^-8.90 for 1 mm and 10^-0.78 for 0.1 mm, matching the audit. (4) The top-line 'NO, as long as the stated hypothesis Newtonian gravity holds' follows. It is a hypothesis-conditional claim, so the grade of the theorem as the tree uses it (STANDS, by re-derivation) is unaffected.

WHAT IS REFUTED. The quantitative support for 'no change', and the scale threshold built on it, rest on the wrong slice of the data. The ratio has the form (R/lambda)^2 e^{-R/lambda}. It peaks at lambda = R/2 (sympy argmax x = 2), where the ratio is 0.180*|alpha|. The audit evaluates only |alpha| = 1, which the data allow only for lambda < 38.6 um. For R much larger than 77 um that is the far tail, e^{-25907} at R = 1 m. The audit's number is the maximum on that slice and nowhere else. The data also allow |alpha| < 1 at every longer lambda, and there the allowed stiffness for a shell of radius R is about 0.18*alpha_max(R/2), not 10^-11242.8. The audit itself marks alpha_max at longer lambda as NAMED-NOT-READ, yet lacked_data concludes 'The Newtonian ceiling therefore survives to any precision that matters for a macroscopic device'. That is presumed, not computed. It over-represents in the tree's favour, which M's rules forbid.

I READ ONE LONGER-RANGE BOUND. Adelberger, Heckel and Nelson, hep-ph/0307284, read now via alphaXiv. Page 56 gives the lunar-laser-ranging bound delta omega/omega = (alpha/2)(a/lambda)^2 e^{-a/lambda} < 1.6e-11 at 95% CL. That is the same functional form as the shell stiffness. It gives alpha_max of about 5.9e-11 at lambda = a/2, and a maximum allowed stiffness ratio of about 1.1e-11 for a shell at the lunar-orbit scale: small, but nowhere near 10^-11242. For laboratory R (1 mm to 1 m), the alpha bounds at lambda ~ R appear only in the review's Figs. 4 and 5 as plots. No number was read, so the true allowed stiffness at those scales is OPEN, not 'negligible to any precision'. The same review (p.56-57) says that in 2003 'at gravitational strength (alpha = 1) the ISL has been verified down to lambda = 200 um'. That is consistent with Lee et al.'s later 38.6 um and supports the 'data moved' framing.

CONSEQUENCES. The 'DATA-DEPENDENT if the device's scale were set below about 0.1 mm' clause in what_would_change_the_grade is an artefact of fixing |alpha| = 1. At any R, a sub-gravitational Yukawa at lambda ~ R/2 with |alpha| up to alpha_max(R/2) gives a non-zero stiffness of either sign, about 0.18*alpha_max. Whether it is negligible depends on alpha_max at that range, which was not read for laboratory scales. M's hypothesis is answered with evidence only on the |alpha| = 1 slice. The direction 'no datum Earnshaw lacked overturns the theorem' still holds: the theorem is conditional on an exact 1/r kernel, and that is untouched. But the sentence claiming the ceiling survives to any precision for macroscopic devices is unsupported, and should read 'bounded by 0.18*alpha_max(R/2); alpha_max at laboratory ranges NAMED-NOT-READ; about 1e-11 at the LLR scale (read, hep-ph/0307284 p.56)'.

GRADE. STANDS for the statement as the tree uses it, under its named hypothesis 'Newtonian gravity'. The data row's moves_conclusion and lacked_data are NARROWED as described: a discrepancy in the supporting argument, recorded, not a refutation of the theorem.

audits.published_statement:
AMM abstract (p.1): 'The criterion proposed is that solutions to the semi-classical Einstein equations should be stable to linearized perturbations, in the sense that no gauge invariant perturbation should become unbounded in time.'

AMM Sec. III (p.10): 'A necessary condition for the validity of the large N semi-classical equations of motion (2.9) is that the linear response equations (3.4) should have no solutions with finite non-singular initial data for which any linearized gauge invariant scalar quantity grows without bound.'

AMM Sec. II (p.7): 'we should regard the Planck scale as the physical UV cutoff which defines the extreme limit of possible validity of semi-classical gravity, and ... confine our attention to only those predictions of the theory which involve length scales l much greater than the Planck length.' The large-N solution is 'the exact solution of this equation without any perturbative re-expansion of G[g]'.

AMM Sec. V (p.13): the condition is 'necessary, though perhaps not a sufficient'. Flat space is stable 'provided we restrict ourselves to solutions with 4 G_N |k^2| << O(1)'.

AMM p.14: 'Further important and interesting examples to which the criterion may be applied are solutions with event horizons, such as Schwarzschild and de Sitter spacetimes ... In the Hartle-Hawking state one can construct a static solution to the semi-classical equations (2.9) that is quite close to the classical one near the horizon.'

Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 p.35: 'known violations of the AANEC involve Planck length distances, where the validity of QFT in curved spacetimes and/or semiclassical quantum gravity is doubtful ... Violations at Planck scale are allowed, because they probably lie outside the range of validity of the semiclassical Einstein equation.'

Kontou 2405.05963 p.19, on the Hochberg-Popov-Sushkov (HPS) self-consistent wormhole: 'The throat of the wormhole derived is of Planck length or up to the order 10^2 l_pl, so it is doubtful that it can be considered in the regime of the semiclassical approximation. However, it would be of interest to examine that wormhole solution using one of the QEIs for the nonminimally coupled fields ... to determine its exact validity.'

On the pages read, none of the three states a threshold on a metric-perturbation amplitude eps (or h) beyond which semiclassical gravity stops applying.
published_hypotheses: AMM H1: the background g solves the renormalised large-N semiclassical equations (2.9); the linear response (3.4) is the first variation about that solution (pp.8-9)
AMM H2: large N with N G finite, in the state |in>. A failed test means the approximation is 'not valid for that particular geometry, at least not for that particular state' (p.13)
AMM H3: validity is judged at length scales l >> l_Pl, i.e. 4 G_N |k^2| << O(1) (pp.7, 13), with the fourth-order coefficients of order 1
AMM H4: the criterion is necessary, not sufficient (p.13)
AMM H5: the allowed gauge transformations are those of (3.11); a growing one is excluded if the action (2.7) is not invariant under it (p.10)
Kontou-Sanders: the Planck-scale exclusion is hedged as 'probably', 'doubtful' and 'questionable'. It is a judgement, not a theorem
Kontou 2024: the stated reason for doubt is the HPS throat scale (1 to 10^2 l_P), and the exact validity is left to a future test with QEIs for non-minimally coupled (NMC) fields
hypothesis_drift: ATTRIBUTION DRIFT, AMM (substantive). throatmass.py:68-72, carried into ledger.py:1684-1685 and LEDGER.md:204 ('the corridor is EXPELLED rather than refuted'), credits AMM with the claim that 'eps ~ 1 lies outside semiclassical gravity's domain'. On the pages read, AMM draw the domain's edge in two places: length scales approaching l_Pl (p.7, and p.13's 4 G_N|k^2| << O(1)), and a growing gauge-invariant linear-response mode about a self-consistent solution (p.10). AMM call their large-N solution non-perturbative (p.7). On p.14 they name Schwarzschild horizons and the Hartle-Hawking static solution as places to apply the criterion, and h = 2M/r = 1 exactly at a horizon (rederive C3). So AMM treat an h = 1 geometry as inside their framework, not outside it.

ATTRIBUTION DRIFT, Kontou (substantive). The same site credits 'Kontou' with the eps ~ 1 claim. Kontou-Sanders pp.2 and 35 put the doubtful region at Planck-length distances. Kontou 2024 p.19 doubts HPS because its throat is 1 to 10^2 l_P, and p.25 calls a Planck-size throat the 'quantum gravity regime'. Both criteria are length scales, not metric amplitudes. The corridor has h = 1/2 at a free scale b; at a = 1 m it is 6.19e34 l_P.

DROPPED: AMM's criterion is a test that can pass or fail, and a failure names something: a growing gauge-invariant mode, which means 'the quantum fluctuations of the geometry should be included' (p.13). throatmass.py:71-72 ('an expulsion names nothing') and EXPULSION_WORSE_THAN_NO_GO (throatmass.py:163) leave this out. In addition, linstab.py records that AMM's criterion cannot yet be evaluated on the corridor, because no self-consistent solution is in hand (AMM_NEEDS_A_SOLUTION).

DROPPED: AMM's large-N setting (H2), 'for that particular state' (p.13), and 'necessary, not sufficient' (H4). This site applies nothing else of AMM, so these drops cause no over-claim beyond the attribution.

WEAKENED (hedge dropped): Kontou-Sanders say 'probably' and 'doubtful'; Kontou 2024 says 'doubtful' and asks for a test 'to determine its exact validity'. The tree's wording 'are right that ... lies outside' reads as a firm boundary; the conditional 'If' keeps only part of the hedge.

ADDED: the parameter eps. It is Flanagan-Wald's family parameter, graded in its own audit. Neither AMM nor Kontou uses a parameter of that kind. Grouping all three authors under one 'eps ~ 1' criterion is the tree's own construction.

POSSIBLE SOURCE OF THE CONFLATION (a reading, not claimed as the tree's intent): AMM pp.2-3 restate Kuo-Ford's fluctuation-to-mean ratio, which is 'of order unity' in many states including the Casimir vacuum. That is a '~1' breakdown measure, but it is a ratio of stress-tensor fluctuations, not a metric amplitude, and AMM criticise it as coordinate dependent. Kuo-Ford 1993 is NAMED-NOT-READ.

audits.lacked_data:
What AMM had in 2002 was a criterion and a single evaluation (Minkowski, free scalar, vacuum). They had no evaluation on any curved self-consistent background and list Schwarzschild and de Sitter as future work (p.14).

What came later is GMMPS 2604.01047, which contests the flat-space verdict itself by tying it to renormalisation constants that AMM took to be of order 1. That moves AMM's stability result, which is now contested. It does not move the part the tree uses: AMM's domain boundary is set by length scale plus a stability test, and no later datum turns it into an eps threshold.

Kontou's data (the 1997 HPS throat scale and l_P) have not moved. No measured datum enters any of the three conclusions.

The data that are still missing, curved-background linear response and the renormalisation constants, would be needed to decide whether the corridor passes AMM's test. They would not supply the tree's antecedent. On this result, M's hypothesis finds no data gap that changes the conclusion.
audits.grade_evidence:
The statements were read at source in the banked arXiv text layers. The tree's sentence at throatmass.py:68-72 credits AMM and Kontou with 'eps ~ 1 lies outside semiclassical gravity's domain'. Shi, arXiv:2107.04206v1, abstract and p.15 (the static configuration is not unique; 1010/1210 phase boundary at M ~ 2.7e14 a_m^2 kg); (4) Cline, Kainulainen, Scott, Weniger, arXiv:1306.4710v5 sec.5.1 eqs.(10)-(13), p.8 (Higgs-nucleon coupling f_N m_N/v, SVZ heavy-quark sum, f_N = 0.30 +- 0.01). audits.published_statement: Brax-Burrage 2101.10693 eq.(4) is a simplified SM with a real Higgs h and one Dirac fermion. The fermion term is -lambda_psi h psibar psi. The paper states: 'we replace psibar psi -> <psibar psi> = n_psi where n_psi is the number density of the medium. After identifying the mass of the fermions as m_psi = lambda_psi v, the equations of motion ... become ... box h + mu^2(phi) h - lambda h^3 - rho/v = 0 (10)', with mu^2 = lambda v^2 (eq.7). In the linear static case (eqs.(56),(58)), the perturbations outside a constant-density sphere are 'decreasing exponential functions' B e^{-sqrt(y)(r-R_0)}/(sqrt(y) r). Footnote 2 says: 'the Higgs field should couple to alpha rho in (10). We ignore this alpha coefficient.' Shi 1908.02159 p.1 gives '<phi> ~ +-v - f<psibar psi>/u^2' in the perturbative regime, significant only at rho ~ v^2 u^2 ~ 1e29 kg/m^3. Cline 1306.4710 eq.(11) gives 'sum_{c,b,t} f_q = (2/9)(1 - sum_{u,d,s} f_q)' (SVZ) and a Higgs-nucleon coupling f_N m_N/v with f_N = 0.30 +- 0.01.
published_hypotheses: Tree-level classical field equation of a real scalar with quartic (Mexican-hat) self-coupling. One Dirac fermion stands in for the SM (Brax-Burrage p.5).
psibar psi is replaced by its medium expectation value and identified with the number density n, i.e. nonrelativistic matter (Brax-Burrage p.5).
Linear perturbation theory about the vacuum, requiring a source density that is not too high (Brax-Burrage p.14; Shi 1908.02159: the shift matters only at rho ~ v^2 u^2).
Static configuration, constant-density source, decay at infinity, continuity at the surface (Brax-Burrage eqs.(54)-(58)).
Perturbative branch: Shi 2107.04206 shows the static solution is not unique beyond a size-dependent critical source (the 1210 phase).
For nucleons the coupling is alpha*rho = f_N m_N/v, with f_N from the SVZ heavy-quark relation at leading order in alpha_s plus the u, d AND s sigma terms (Cline eq.(11)).
hypothesis_drift: No drift on the field equation. address.py:138 '(nabla^2 - m_h^2) dphi = (m_psi/v) n' is exactly Brax-Burrage eq.(10) linearised (sympy residual 0) and matches Shi's shift. The uniform solution at address.py:140 re-derives. Only m_h^2 enters, so the unmeasured trilinear does not.

Weakened qualifier 'EXACT' (address.py:140, :145; source_to_field_ratio docstring at address.py:674-678). The law is exact only as the linear, tree-level, uniform statement. The exact uniform solution for the SM shape is rho = 8|V_min| eps(1+eps)(1+eps/2), so the exact source/field ratio is 4(1+eps)/(eps(2+eps)), not 8/(eps(2+eps)^2). The two differ by 1.3e-15 at eps_det and by a factor of 3 at the eps_0 = 1 of address.py:166. This is a discrepancy, not a refutation.

Dropped at the formula: psibar psi -> n, the nonrelativistic identification (address.py:137-142 uses the mass density rho). The tree knows the relativistic form, the (mc^2/E)^2 lemma at address.py:244-250. For a free Fermi gas at n0, rho_s/rho_B = 0.9774 (-2.3%).

Coupling hypothesis (address.py:104, :143). For a Higgs field displacement, the READ literature supports H1 = SVZ (Cline eqs.(11)-(13), f_N = 0.30). H2 (f = S) has no READ support as a Higgs-nucleon coupling. The one exception is Brax-Burrage footnote 2, which says the gluon part is uncoupled, contrary to SVZ; that is recorded as a discrepancy in the reading source. The tree refuses to choose (address.py:460).
Dropped (sibling sigma-term-scan): EPS_NUCLEAR (address.py:943) uses S = 0.06, which counts u and d only. SVZ sums over u, d and s. At S = 0.09, eps = -3.55e-13, 433x eps_det(H1).
Weakened (siblings dlnlambdaqcd-dlnv-2-9, svz-1978): the 2/9 is leading order in alpha_s and in the heavy-quark limit. Beyond LO, f = 0.2818 at S = 0.06 (+4.8%).

Unnamed hypothesis: that the perturbative branch is the unique static solution. The tree's criterion is eps << 1 (address.py:166, 297-303). Shi 2107.04206 p.15 puts the nonperturbative boundary at rho_c ~ 8.8e11 kg/m^3 for a 1 m sphere with the tree's H1 f, where eps ~ 1e-18. The boundary is far away for EPS_NUCLEAR (margin 4.7e8) and for the atom-scale courier (margin 4.5e9). It is relevant to the 1 m sources of address.py sections 6 and 9. It is contested for the SM, because Shi's model is a toy.

Weakened (sibling yukawa-green-function, re-shown in R7): the multiplicative form '[1 + O((lambda_h/L)^2)]' at address.py:181 fails where J = 0 but dphi != 0. The absolute form |dphi + J/m^2| <= |J''|/m^4 holds.

Discrepancy (sibling address-domination-theorem, re-shown in R3): address.py:164 and :697-722 start the exterior tail at eps_0. For a uniform sphere with R >> lambda_h, the surface value is half the interior value, so the standoff is overstated by lambda_h ln 2 = 1.09e-18 m. This is conservative.

audits.name: Raychaudhuri equation with shear: sigma^2 >= 0 only ever helps focusing

source.located: A. K. Raychaudhuri, Phys. Rev. 98, 1123 (1955), for timelike congruences, and R. K. Sachs, Proc. Roy. Soc. A 264, 309 (1961), for the null version. Neither classic has an arXiv copy. Both are restated exactly in E. Witten, arXiv:1901.03928v6 (eqs. 5.11-5.12, 8.46-8.53, sec. 8.6), and in S. Kar & S. SenGupta, arXiv:gr-qc/0611123 (eqs. 12, 15-17, 44, plus the Sturm-comparison remark after eq. 16).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1901.03928 (pp. 34-35, 43, 49-53, 75-88) and on gr-qc/0611123 (pp. 3-4, 10-14, 22). Fewster & Galloway arXiv:1012.6038 eq. (5.5) was read as a third restatement. Raychaudhuri 1955 and Sachs 1961 themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ. The history (Raychaudhuri 1955 timelike, with shear and rotation; Sachs 1961 the first null version) comes from Kar-SenGupta pp. 3-4 and 13, and Witten p. 49.

audits.published_statement: Witten 1901.03928 eq. (5.12), equivalently (8.52) with Einstein's equation, for an affinely parametrised, twist-free null congruence in D dimensions: 'dtheta/du + theta^2/(D-2) = -Tr sigma^2 - 8 pi G T_uu'. Here sigma is the traceless part of the transverse matrix E'E^-1 (eq. 8.51), and the equation is valid 'for any twist-free solution, that is, any solution whose Wronskian vanishes' (p. 87). Kar-SenGupta eq. (17) in D=4 reads 'dTheta/dlambda + Theta^2/2 + sigma^2 - omega^2 = -R_ab k^a k^b'. They rewrite the equation in second-order form and apply Sturm comparison: 'convergence occurs if R_ab v^a v^b + sigma^2 - omega^2 >= 0 ... Thus, rotation defies convergence, while shear assists it' (p. 12). Their null lensing form, eq. (44), is d_A''/d_A = -(1/2)R_00 - (1/2)sigma^2. Witten sec. 8.6: Weyl curvature sources shear (eq. 8.53), and shear forces theta to minus infinity, giving 'a Jacobi field with two zeroes, showing that l is not achronal' (p. 88).
published_hypotheses: H1: the congruence is geodesic and affinely parametrised. A non-affine parametrisation adds a -kappa*Theta term but leaves the focusing conclusions unchanged (Kar-SenGupta sec. II.E).

H2: the congruence is twist-free (hypersurface-orthogonal, vanishing Wronskian). A congruence from a point, or orthogonal to a codimension-2 surface, is twist-free (Witten pp. 84, 87). With twist, the +omega^2 term opposes focusing (Kar-SenGupta eq. 16).
H3: the transverse (screen) space is spacelike, so sigma_ab sigma^ab = Tr sigma^2 >= 0 as a sum of squares. This is an algebraic fact, not an energy condition.
H4: spacetime dimension D enters as theta^2/(D-2); D=4 gives theta^2/2.

H5: the equation itself is a geometric identity. Setting R_kk = 8 pi G T_kk needs Einstein's equation, in Einstein frame (Kar-SenGupta p. 11; Witten fn. 26). A cosmological constant drops out because k is null.
H6: for a smooth M, a focal or conjugate point occurs exactly where theta goes to minus infinity, which is exactly where det A = 0 (Witten fn. 24, p. 88).
H7: the sign of the shear term needs no energy condition. The NEC is needed only for the Ricci-focusing theorem (Witten eqs. 5.13-5.15).
hypothesis_drift: NONE on the shear-sign claim itself. anecscope.py:52-57 ('sigma^2 does only ever help focusing. More focusing means a conjugate point SOONER, or where there was none') matches Kar-SenGupta p. 12 ('shear assists it') and Witten eq. (5.12). It holds with R_kk of either sign (H7), which is the case the tree needs for ANEC-violating rays.

WEAKENED WORDING, a discrepancy and not an error: anecscope.py:53 and achronal.py:61 say 'SOONER'. Sturm comparison gives 'no later': the two coincide when Tr sigma^2 vanishes identically on the interval. In 300 random trials (C3), no conjugate point came later.
ADDED but harmless: the canonical entry lists 'shear term enters with sign that focuses (sigma^2 >= 0)' as a hypothesis. At source it is a theorem (H3), and C2 proves it symbolically.

CONSISTENT: the canonical hypothesis 'null geodesic congruence, twist-free' is H2. The tree's Jacobi field with u(start)=0, u'(start)=1 (achronal.py:225-236) is the congruence from a point, which is twist-free (Witten pp. 84, 87).

CONSISTENT: 'scalar reduction u'' = -4 pi T_kk u valid only shear-free' (achronal.py:48-50, anecscope.py:64-66). With theta = 2u'/u and u = sqrt(det A), the full equation is u'' = -(R_kk + Tr sigma^2)/2 u (Kar-SenGupta eq. 44). The reduction drops exactly the Tr sigma^2 term (C1).
IMPLICIT and unstated at achronal.py:52: R_kk = 8 pi T_kk assumes the Einstein equation in Einstein frame (H5). This does not affect the shear-sign claim, which is geometric.

ADJACENT DRIFT, recorded here but not graded (it belongs to key conjugate-point-not-achronal): achronal.py:41 says 'A null geodesic is achronal EXACTLY up to its first CONJUGATE POINT'. Witten p. 43 says the absence of a focal point is 'necessary but not sufficient' for promptness, and prompt is equivalent to achronal. C5 gives a counterexample: flat R x S^1 has no conjugate point, yet the ray is not achronal. anecscope's conclusion uses only the sound direction (conjugate point implies non-achronal). Its counterexample() at anecscope.py:242-244 does treat 'no conjugate point' as 'achronal', but that can only add false candidates, never hide real ones, so its empty result stands.

ADJACENT, not a drift in this key: anecscope.py:66-68 says Weyl 'focuses one eigendirection whatever the sign of the source, and det A = 0 happens with R_kk identically zero'. The focusing tendency is algebraic (C4 sign-flip check). An actual conjugate point, though, needs enough integrated Weyl strength. Witten sec. 8.6's generic-condition guarantee assumes NEC and completeness, which the corridor lacks. The tree measures the conjugate point numerically rather than invoking that theorem (see keys sachs-weyl-shear-focusing and vacuum-ricci-flat-traceless-tidal).
